title: 红十字会借足球号召更多人捐血
description: 红十字会借足球号召更多人捐血 图片由新加坡红十字会提供 为鼓励更多年轻人前来捐血，新加坡红十字会日前展开“BE THE 1”捐血活动，而这项全球推广活动，找来了定期捐血的世界杯足球赛葡萄牙国家足球队队长克·罗纳尔多（Cristiano Ronaldo）作为推广大使，希望通过足球号召更多人为捐血献一分力。 在本地，去年共有7万3107人捐血，但当中只有26%是年龄介于16至25岁的年轻人。受访的新加坡红十字会捐血者招募计划指导总监张维龙告诉联合早报：“本地人对于捐血与输血的概念有初步认识，但对于捐血过程、捐血者的符合条件以及本地血液库存量的需求未必有足够的了解。” 呼吁公众发表捐血宣言 通过与新加坡体育理事会（SportSG）合作，新加坡红十字会将从即日起至7月31日，在新加坡足球节（Singapore Football Festival）活动上以路演方式推广捐血活动。在活动会场上，将有新加坡红十字会的职员与义工与公众分享捐血须知，包括通过海报、宣传册子等方式让公众了解更多有关捐血的过程、血液的使用方面，以及解开人们常有的捐血误解与疑问。人们也能在现场与新加坡红十字会的捐血吉祥物合照，以及现场发表捐血宣言。 新加坡红十字会也鼓励人们在这段期间将个人自拍照或是与设在本地四个血库的克·罗纳尔多人形看板合照，并将照片、一小段的捐血宣言同时附加标签（hashtag活#BeThe1DonorSG，一起上传到个人社交网页上，帮忙推广捐血运动，且呼吁朋友与追随者（followers）响应号召。 借足球活动宣导捐血意识 与此同时，本月21日早上在加冷草场，将举行”Be The 1 Football Clinic”足球训练班，让新加坡红十字会血液流动组织者网络下的指定中学和初院学生有机会报名参加。名额限制为30至40人，并能与ActiveSG足球学院的教练以及其他热爱足球的同学一起踢足球，学习宝贵的技能。 ActiveSG足球学院主任林东海说：“足球是一项能让新加坡人团结起来表现对彼此的关爱的有力工具。我们希望在这足球节期间，借此机会宣导与提高参加者与家人及朋友的捐血意识。” 欲知更多有关新加坡足球节所举办的竞赛以及全家人可参与的活动，可浏览网站footballfest.sg。 足球训练班 7月21日（星期六） 早上9时至11时 加冷草场 购买此文章

This global promotion campaign has hired Cristiano Ronaldo, captain of the Portuguese national football team in the World Cup who regularly donates blood, as a promotion ambassador, hoping to call on more people to donate blood through football. Zhang Weilong, Director of Blood Donor Recruitment Program of the Singapore Red Cross who was interviewed, told Lianhe Zaobao: "Local people have a preliminary understanding of the concepts of blood donation and blood transfusion, but they may not have enough understanding of the blood donation process, the qualifications of blood donors, and the demand for local blood stocks." Festival) to promote blood donation activities in the form of road shows. People can also take photos with the Singapore Red Cross blood donation mascot and make a blood donation declaration on the spot. The Singapore Red Cross also encourages people to take selfies or photos with the Ronaldo-shaped billboards at four local blood banks during this period, and upload the photos and a short blood donation declaration with the hashtag (hashtag #BeThe1DonorSG) to their personal social networking pages to help promote the blood donation campaign and call on friends and followers to respond to the call. title: 福建会馆与红十字会成功募集15单位血液
description: 福建会馆与红十字会成功募集15单位血液 新加坡福建会馆与新加坡红十字会昨天联手举办捐血活动，成功收集到15个单位血液。 捐血活动从昨天上午10时至下午4时在信立路5号的福建会馆文化学院举行。在阻断措施期间，捐血属于必要项目，主办单位获卫生部和卫生科学局批准进行。全天共有18人前去捐血，但有三人不符合资格。 15名合格捐血者包括福建会馆会员和公众，以及看了本报的活动预告新闻前往的忠实读者。大多数捐血者都已预先报名，因此等候时间缩短，整个过程井然有序。 这是福建会馆第一次在信立路会所举办捐血活动，会长陈精毅说：“能够在这个非常时期尽一分绵力回馈社会，意义重大。接下来若有需要，我们会在能力所及范围全力配合。感谢所有前来捐血的会员和公众，也希望大家务必保持健康，积极防疫。” 新加坡红十字会捐血者招募计划总监张维龙表示，红十字会每天须收集约400个单位血液，才能维持新加坡六天的紧急医疗需求。血液保存期很短：红血球六周，血小板五天，所以须经常收集捐血。过去数周血库库存偏低，尤其是Rh血型（O-和A-）。阻断措施启动的第一周，每天所收集到的血液已少于平日的四分之一。 张维龙呼吁：“捐血属于必要项目，每天都有病人需要血液，希望健康人士能继续捐血。我们已做足防护措施，床位隔一米距离，活动现场有清楚的指示牌，确保捐血者在等候区和休息区保持安全距离。” 除了捐血活动，福建会馆也推出一组向前线医护人员致敬的发糕仔WhatsApp贴图，包括“有你真好”“幸苦了”和“好好休息”等贴心造型。“用肥皂洗手”“多喝水”“加油加油”等则吁请大家齐心协力对抗疫情。 这是配合福建会馆今年180周年庆推出的其中一组WhatsApp贴图。另一组贴图则富本地福建特色，有本地人熟悉的“发啊”“保庇保庇”和“好势（Ho Say）”等。两组贴图欢迎公众免费下载，详情可上网 www.shhk.com.sg/zh/huat-kueh-boy-whatsapp-stickers/ 查询。 购买此文章
description_translated: The Hokkien Huay Kuan and the Singapore Red Cross successfully collected 15 units of blood. The Singapore Hokkien Huay Kuan and the Singapore Red Cross jointly held a blood donation event yesterday and successfully collected 15 units of blood. The blood donation event was held from 10 am to 4 pm yesterday at the Fujian Huay Kuan Cultural College, 5 Shun Lai Road. During the circuit breaker period, blood donation is an essential item and the organizer is approved by the Ministry of Health and the Health Sciences Authority. A total of 18 people came to donate blood throughout the day, but three were not eligible. The 15 qualified blood donors include Fujian Association members and the public, as well as loyal readers who went after reading the event preview news of this newspaper. Most blood donors have pre-registered, so wait times are short and the process is orderly. This is the first time that the Fujian Association holds a blood donation event at the Xin Lai Road Club. President Chen Jingyi said: "It is of great significance to be able to contribute to the society during this extraordinary period. If necessary, we will fully cooperate within our capabilities. We would like to thank all members and the public who came to donate blood. We also hope that everyone will stay healthy and actively prevent the epidemic." Singapore Red Cross Blood Donor Recruitment Program Director Zhang Weilong said that the Red Cross must collect about 400 units of blood every day to meet Singapore's emergency medical needs for six days. Blood has a short shelf life: six weeks for red blood cells and five days for platelets, so donated blood must be collected frequently. Blood bank stocks have been low over the past few weeks, especially for Rh blood groups (O- and A-). In the first week of the circuit breaker measures, the amount of blood collected each day was less than a quarter of normal levels. Zhang Weilong appealed: "Blood donation is a necessary item. title: 孙燕姿老公加入武装部队志愿军团
description: 孙燕姿老公加入武装部队志愿军团 （本地讯）本地天后孙燕姿老公纳迪姆当兵去？ 最新一期的国防部月刊《国锋报》（Pioneer）中，刊载了一名新加坡武装部队志愿军团军人纳迪姆（Nadim Van Der Ros）的文章，文章述说了他为何加入新加坡武装部队志愿军团，而该名志愿军团军人纳迪姆，正是本地天后孙燕姿的丈夫。 纳迪姆是荷兰籍印尼裔，2011年和孙燕姿结婚后，两人育有一对儿女，虽然身为天后的丈夫，但目前已经是新加坡永久居民的纳迪姆，向来十分低调，除了在社交媒体晒照分享生活日常之外，极少在媒体前曝光。纳迪姆对于孙燕姿的歌唱事业却十分支持，像疫情期间，孙燕姿曾办线上演唱会，他可是忠实观众，也给妻子留言点赞。 蓄着一脸落腮胡，被媒体昵称为“胡须男”的纳迪姆，创办了一家咨询公司，协助社会组织制定品牌策略，但为何会加入武装部队志愿军团？ 根据他在文章叙述，他是因2016年有恐怖组织策划从印尼峇淡岛发射火箭炮攻击本地的滨海湾金沙事件，带给他很深的启发，于是在2021年报名加入新加坡武装部队志愿军团（SAF Volunteer Corps），目前担任保安辅助队员（Auxiliary Security Trooper），职责包括在樟宜机场等重要设施执行保安巡逻。 他写道：“我想通过服务他人，表达我对社区的感激，回馈我这些年来获得的恩惠。” 纳迪姆（右一）与新加坡红十字会的义工，为斯里兰卡的学生分发食物。（取自纳迪姆IG） 常参与人道救援工作 纳迪姆经常参与人道救援工作，出国为贫困家庭盖房子。 在雅加达出生，后来被一对荷兰籍夫妻领养的纳迪姆，加入志愿军团前也经常参与人道救援工作，曾经在今年8月跟随新加坡红十字会的义工团队走访斯里兰卡的学校，派发食物给学生、安装滤水器，教导学生们良好的口腔卫生和正确的洗手步骤。 他曾带领志愿组织“仁人家园”到峇淡岛，为当地的低收入家庭盖房子。 针对纳迪姆加入志愿军团，《新明日报》尝试联络孙燕姿，但经纪人表示不愿发表意见。 明星 孙燕姿 义工 上一篇 抱病来新与粉丝比哭戏 李俊昊竟然输了 下一篇 《深网》穿校服当学霸 容启航首挑战演反派 购买此文章
description_translated: Stefanie Sun’s husband joins the Armed Forces Volunteer Corps (Local News) Local diva Stefanie Sun’s husband Nadeem will join the army? The latest issue of Pioneer, the monthly magazine of the Ministry of National Defense, published an article by Nadim Van Der Ros, a volunteer soldier of the Singapore Armed Forces. The article described why he joined the Volunteer Corps of the Singapore Armed Forces. Nadim Van Der Ros, a volunteer soldier of the Singapore Armed Forces, is the husband of local queen Stefanie Sun. Nadeem is a Dutch-Indonesian. After marrying Stefanie Sun in 2011, the two have a son and a daughter. Although he is the husband of a diva, Nadeem, who is now a permanent resident of Singapore, has always been very low-key. Apart from posting photos and sharing daily life on social media, he is rarely exposed in front of the media. Nadim is very supportive of Stefanie Sun's singing career. For example, during the epidemic, Stefanie Sun held an online concert. He was a loyal audience and also left messages and likes for his wife. Nadim, who has a beard and is nicknamed "The Bearded Man" by the media, founded a consulting company to assist social organizations in formulating brand strategies, but why did he join the Armed Forces Volunteer Corps? According to his narration in the article, he was deeply inspired by the 2016 incident in which a terrorist organization planned to launch rocket launchers from Batam Island in Indonesia to attack the local Marina Bay Sands, so he signed up to join the Singapore Armed Forces Volunteer Corps (SAF Volunteer Corps) in 2021. He is currently serving as an Auxiliary Security Trooper, and his responsibilities include performing security patrols at important facilities such as Changi Airport. He wrote: "I want to express my gratitude to the community by serving others and repay the favor I have received over the years." Nadeem (first from right) and a Singapore Red Cross volunteer distribute food to students in Sri Lanka. (Taken from Nadim’s IG) Often participates in humanitarian relief work Nadim often participates in humanitarian relief work and goes abroad to build houses for poor families. Nadeem, who was born in Jakarta and later adopted by a Dutch couple, often participated in humanitarian relief work before joining the volunteer corps. In August this year, he followed a volunteer team from the Singapore Red Cross Society to visit schools in Sri Lanka, distributing food to students, installing water filters, and teaching students good oral hygiene and correct handwashing procedures. He once led the voluntary organization Habitat for Humanity to Batam to build houses for local low-income families. In response to Nadeem joining the volunteer corps, Shin Min Daily News tried to contact Stefanie Sun, but her agent expressed unwillingness to comment. title: 我国拨款100万元 作为加沙人道援助筹款启动资金
description: 我国拨款100万元 作为加沙人道援助筹款启动资金 我国将为加沙提供100万元人道援助筹款的启动资金，支援加沙人道救援工作。这将是自2023年10月以哈冲突爆发以来，新加坡向加沙受影响平民提供的第11批人道援助。 外交部星期六（12月20日）发文告说，这笔款项将平均分配给新加坡红十字会、全福基金会（Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation）、仁心组织，以及本地人道救援组织慈援（Mercy Relief），用于支援加沙的饮水、环境卫生、个人清洁、粮食及其他紧急人道救援工作。 连同此次拨款，新加坡政府与社会各界提供的人道援助总额已超过2500万元。文告说，新加坡将继续与区域伙伴以及本地非政府组织密切合作，协助应对加沙当前迫切的人道需求。 本地义工到街头为加沙平民筹款 配合联合国国际人类团结日，约200名来自不同族群、年龄层与职业背景的义工星期六走上街头，为加沙平民筹募人道援助款项。 这项名为“加沙街头筹款行动”（Street Collection for Gaza Relief）的活动，由新加坡仁心组织（Humanity Matters）主办。 延伸阅读 我国将加大对加沙人道援助 与巴勒斯坦深化合作助实现建国目标 新加坡向约旦捐赠义肢 助加沙巴勒斯坦截肢者 任代总理的副总理兼贸工部长 颜金勇 星期六在仁心组织为加沙筹款活动主持开幕时说，这项行动充分体现了“新加坡精神”如何化为实际行动。 “我们今天也看到在新加坡工作的外籍人士与客工参与筹款，共同为这一值得投入的努力尽一分力，这与政府的人道援助做法形成互补。” 颜金勇说，希望这些努力能在一定程度上缓解加沙受影响平民的苦难。“这是非常重要的一项工作，我们将继续动员全社会的力量，尽我们所能提供援助。” 他也重申，新加坡呼吁各方促成人道援助迅速且不受阻碍地送入加沙。他强调，维持和平与停火至关重要，并须继续推动进入下一阶段，为加沙的重建创造条件。 加沙 以哈冲突 援助 上一篇 监狱署车辆与两辆私家车涉追尾车祸 一囚犯受轻伤 下一篇 涉淡滨尼咖啡店持刀伤人 53岁男子被捕后面控 购买此文章
description_translated: my country will allocate 1 million yuan as a start-up fund for humanitarian aid in Gaza. my country will provide Gaza with 1 million yuan as a start-up fund for humanitarian aid to support humanitarian relief work in Gaza. This will be the 11th batch of humanitarian assistance provided by Singapore to affected civilians in Gaza since the outbreak of the Israel-Kazakhstan conflict in October 2023. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement on Saturday (December 20) saying that the funds will be distributed equally among the Singapore Red Cross, Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation, Charity Organization, and local humanitarian relief organization Mercy Relief to support drinking water, sanitation, personal hygiene, food and other emergency humanitarian relief work in Gaza. Together with this allocation, the total amount of humanitarian assistance provided by the Singapore government and all sectors of society has exceeded 25 million yuan. The statement said that Singapore will continue to work closely with regional partners and local non-governmental organizations to help respond to the current urgent humanitarian needs in Gaza. Local volunteers took to the streets to raise funds for civilians in Gaza. In conjunction with the United Nations International Day of Human Solidarity, about 200 volunteers from different ethnic groups, ages and professional backgrounds took to the streets on Saturday to raise funds for humanitarian aid for civilians in Gaza. The event, called "Street Collection for Gaza Relief", was organized by Humanity Matters in Singapore. Singapore donates prosthetic limbs to Jordan to help Palestinian amputees in Gaza. Gan Kim Yong, deputy prime minister and minister of trade and industry, who serves as acting prime minister, said at the opening of a fund-raising event for Gaza organized by Humane Heart on Saturday that this action fully reflects how the "Singapore spirit" can be transformed into practical actions. "We also see today that foreigners and guest workers working in Singapore are participating in fundraising and jointly contributing to this worthy effort, which complements the government's humanitarian aid approach." Gan Jinyong said, hoping that these efforts can alleviate the suffering of the affected civilians in Gaza to a certain extent. "This is a very important task, and we will continue to mobilize the whole of society to do our best to provide assistance." He also reiterated Singapore's call on all parties to facilitate the rapid and unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid to Gaza. He stressed that maintaining peace and ceasefire is crucial, and that we must continue to promote the next phase and create conditions for the reconstruction of Gaza. title: 我国红十字会与慈援筹款助雅加达洪灾灾民
description: 我国红十字会与慈援筹款助雅加达洪灾灾民 我国红十字会和人道救援组织慈援已分别展开筹款活动，为印度尼西亚首都雅加达的洪灾灾民筹集善款。于此同时，红十字会将先捐出5万元赈灾，慈援也于昨天派遣灾难应对小组，到灾区协助。 印度尼西亚首都雅加达跨年夜豪雨引发洪灾和山体滑坡。慈援（Mercy Relief）昨天在文告中指出，洪水导致断电与路段关闭，也引发山体滑坡，目前已夺走66条人命，估计有1800万人受灾，急需干净的食水、粮食、医护照料和住宿。 慈援将向公众筹募赈灾款项，募款活动下个月6日截止。有意捐款者可上慈援网站 https://www.mercyrelief.org/join/donate/ 查询更多详情。 新加坡红十字会则于星期一宣布，该会募款的同时会先捐5万元，资助印尼红十字会添置卫生用品、睡袋以及食用水等物资。 红十字会也为澳洲林火募款 此外，新加坡红十字会也将为澳大利亚林火募款，并同时承诺捐出5万新元帮助澳洲红十字会进行人道救援。 有意通过新加坡红十字会捐款的公众，可以把现金送到红十字会办事处，或把支票邮寄到Red Cross House，15 Penang Lane，S238486。支票收款人须注明Singapore Red Cross Society。捐款人也须在支票背面注明Australian Bushfire Emergency或Jakarta Floods Response，并附上自己的姓名和地址。 在澳洲有广泛业务的本地德士公司康福德高则宣布设立新的基金（CDC We Care Fund），帮助解决澳洲灾民的住房需求等。康福德高已初步注入50万澳元（46万4000新元左右），帮助受灾情影响的员工及社区成员。 购买此文章

At the same time, the Red Cross will first donate 50,000 yuan for disaster relief, and Tzu Chi Aid also dispatched a disaster response team to assist in the disaster area yesterday. Heavy rains on New Year's Eve caused flooding and landslides in Jakarta, the Indonesian capital. Mercy Relief pointed out in a statement yesterday that floods caused power outages and road closures, and also triggered landslides, which have claimed 66 lives so far. An estimated 18 million people have been affected and are in urgent need of clean water, food, medical materials and accommodation. Charity Aid will raise funds for disaster relief from the public, and the fundraising will end on the 6th of next month. Those who are interested in donating can go to the Mercy Relief website https://www.mercyrelief.org/join/donate/ for more details. The Singapore Red Cross announced on Monday that while raising funds, it would first donate S$50,000 to help the Indonesian Red Cross purchase hygiene products, sleeping bags, drinking water and other supplies. The Red Cross will also raise funds for the Australian bushfires. In addition, the Singapore Red Cross will also raise funds for the Australian bushfires and has also pledged to donate S$50,000 to help the Australian Red Cross conduct humanitarian relief. Members of the public who wish to donate through the Singapore Red Cross can send cash to the Red Cross office or mail a check to Red Cross House, 15 Penang Lane, S238486. Checks must be made payable to Singapore Red Cross Society. Donors must also write Australian Bushfire Emergency or Jakarta Floods Response on the back of their check and include their name and address. title: 新加坡红十字会筹款 助黎巴嫩和加沙人民
description: 新加坡红十字会筹款 助黎巴嫩和加沙人民 新加坡红十字会展开筹款活动，协助受到中东战火波及的黎巴嫩和加沙人民。此外，它也将捐出5万美元（约6万5400新元）给黎巴嫩红十字会，支持重要的救援行动。 新加坡红十字会星期四（10月10日）的文告指出，黎巴嫩首都贝鲁特自9月27日以来遭受一系列轰炸，已有超过2000人丧命及超过1万人受伤。数万个家庭流离失所，导致约10万人涌到邻近的叙利亚寻求庇护。该区域的人道主义援助需求不断扩大，难以负荷。 黎巴嫩红十字会已经动员数百名志愿者及救护车，协助展开救援与疏散行动。此外，它也呼吁全国人民捐血给伤者，并出动流动诊所为那些因战火流离失所的平民，提供重要的医疗保健服务。 红十字会也向受影响家庭分派被单、食物和个人卫生用品，并提供食水、卫生设施和临时庇护所。 以色列的战斗机于9月27日夜间至28日凌晨，猛烈轰炸贝鲁特南部及其郊区，是自2006年黎巴嫩真主党与以色列上次交战以来，以军对这一真主党据点最猛烈的袭击。 延伸阅读 新加坡捐10万美元 助尼泊尔洪灾灾民 红十字会捐赠5万元援助缅甸应对洪灾 新加坡红十字会 黎巴嫩 以色列 上一篇 新加坡捐10万美元 助尼泊尔洪灾灾民 下一篇 李资政到李玮玲医生灵堂表达哀思 购买此文章
description_translated: The Singapore Red Cross raises funds to help the people of Lebanon and Gaza. The Singapore Red Cross launches fundraising activities to assist the people of Lebanon and Gaza who have been affected by the war in the Middle East. In addition, it will also donate US$50,000 (approximately S$65,400) to the Lebanese Red Cross to support important relief operations. The Singapore Red Cross issued a statement on Thursday (October 10) stating that Beirut, the capital of Lebanon, has suffered a series of bombings since September 27, with more than 2,000 people killed and more than 10,000 injured. Tens of thousands of families have been displaced, causing an estimated 100,000 people to seek asylum in neighboring Syria. The region's humanitarian assistance needs are growing and overwhelming. The Lebanese Red Cross has mobilized hundreds of volunteers and ambulances to assist in rescue and evacuation operations. In addition, it also called on people across the country to donate blood to the wounded and mobilize mobile clinics to provide vital medical care to civilians displaced by the fighting. The Red Cross is also distributing linens, food and personal hygiene items to affected families, as well as providing water, sanitation and temporary shelter. Israeli fighter jets violently bombed southern Beirut and its suburbs from the night of September 27 to the early morning of September 28. It was the most violent attack by the Israeli army on this Hezbollah stronghold since the last war between Hezbollah and Israel in Lebanon in 2006. title: 车商赞助红十字会 添置具伸缩式轮椅斜道护送车
description: 车商赞助红十字会 添置具伸缩式轮椅斜道护送车 冠病疫情期间，必要的长期医疗复诊和治疗仍得进行，汽车销售公司赞助新加坡红十字会15万元，购买并将一辆车改装成具有伸缩式轮椅斜道的护送车，接送低收入或独居老人与残障人士往返医疗机构和日间活动中心。 护送车的交接仪式昨天在位于槟榔巷的新加坡红十字会办事处举行，销售豪华汽车的Eurokars集团赞助的护送车主要用于红十字会的护送服务（TransportAid）。 红十字会秘书长兼首席执行官班杰明·威廉（Benjamin William）受访时指出，在病毒阻断措施期间，组织发现载送是一项需要持续的必要服务。 “护送服务的受益者大多是独居、低收入且长期需要复诊的有需者，在普通情况下他们已很难负担市面上一般费用较贵的护送服务。面对疫情肆虐，我国经济受创，一些援助服务减少，不只弱势群体的生活素质恶化，更多家庭也陷入困境，需要帮助的人更多。” 红十字会一个月可完成约1000趟次的护送服务，每年则超过1万1000多趟次。包括Eurokars集团赞助的护送车，该组织目前有八辆护送车和三辆救护车。 Eurokars集团往年也曾赞助各种救援车给例如陈笃生医院、国家传染病中心和SPD（前称新加坡体障人士协会），并根据各组织的需求将车子改良成内设医疗援助设备。 该集团执行董事王丽玲指出，集团业务的可持续发展和成功与所在社会的福祉紧紧相连。“作为我国最大的豪华和高档汽车品牌供应商，集团希望在具有最大影响力的方面提供帮助。” 威廉也鼓励有能力的国人继续捐赠，他说：“去年因更多善心人士和企业挺身而出，通过金钱和物资给予帮助，我们才能渡过疫情高峰期。” 购买此文章
description_translated: Car dealer sponsors Red Cross to purchase retractable wheelchair ramp escort vehicle During the COVID-19 epidemic, necessary long-term medical follow-up and treatment must still be carried out. The car sales company sponsored the Singapore Red Cross S$150,000 to purchase and convert a vehicle into an escort vehicle with a retractable wheelchair ramp to transport low-income elderly or disabled people living alone to and from medical institutions and day activity centres. The handover ceremony of the escort vehicle was held at the Singapore Red Cross office in Pinang Lane yesterday. The escort vehicle sponsored by Eurokars Group, which sells luxury cars, is mainly used for the Red Cross's escort service (TransportAid). Benjamin William, Secretary-General and CEO of the Red Cross, pointed out in an interview that during the circuit breaker period, the organization found that transportation was an essential service that needed to continue. "Most of the beneficiaries of escort services are those in need who live alone, have low incomes, and require long-term follow-up visits. Under normal circumstances, it is difficult for them to afford the more expensive escort services on the market. In the face of the raging epidemic, our country's economy has been hit, and some assistance services have been reduced. Not only has the quality of life of vulnerable groups deteriorated, more families have also fallen into trouble, and more people need help." The Red Cross can complete about 1,000 escort services a month, and more than 11,000 trips a year. Including escort vehicles sponsored by the Eurokars Group, the organization currently has eight escort vehicles and three ambulances. Eurokars Group has also sponsored various rescue vehicles in the past years to such institutions as Tan Tock Seng Hospital, National Center for Infectious Diseases and SPD (formerly known as the Singapore Society for People with Disabilities), and has modified the vehicles to have built-in medical assistance equipment according to the needs of each organization. Wang Liling, executive director of the group, pointed out that the sustainable development and success of the group's business are closely linked to the well-being of the society in which it operates. "As the largest supplier of luxury and high-end automobile brands in our country, the group hopes to provide help in areas with the greatest impact." William also encouraged Chinese people who are able to continue donating. He said: "Last year, because more kind-hearted people and companies came forward to help through money and materials, we were able to tide over the peak period of the epidemic." Buy this article

title: 奔走两场卫塞节活动 义工急救员守护民众安全
description: 奔走两场卫塞节活动 义工急救员守护民众安全 5月12日卫塞节当天，当许多人沉浸在庆祝活动中，50岁的面包厂物流经理叶林雄，却奔波于慈济白沙静思堂和光明山普觉禅寺，维护现场民众的安全。尽管值勤时间超过10小时，他却不觉得辛苦。 卫塞节是佛教徒纪念佛陀诞生、成道和涅槃的重要日子，又称“佛陀日”。当天，浴佛、祈福、表演等庆祝活动吸引大批民众参与，急救人员也在现场待命，随时应对突发状况。 这名原籍马来西亚的义工，在慈济活动现场接受《联合早报》采访时说，他中学时期就加入红十字会，1994年来新加坡后继续参与志愿服务，至今已近30年。 “大型活动一般都会配备急救人员。我们主要是在紧急情况提供帮助，例如有人突然感到不适，我们会先观察情况，照顾他、询问他的症状，安抚对方。如有需要，我们会建议他去医院；如果情况紧急，例如心脏病发作，我们就会立即进行急救，争取关键的‘黄金10分钟’，并等待救护车到场。” 叶林雄也是新加坡民防部队myResponder应用的社区先遣急救员，去年处理了27个急救个案。他还身兼友诺士的紧急应策与参与委员会（C2E）、社区紧急应变小组（CERT），以及市民巡逻小组（COP）成员。 延伸阅读 自闭少年爱华文 开拓华文学习路 她与人力部同龄 70岁首席统计执行员服务半世纪见证变迁 叶林雄忆述，他最难忘的一次急救经历，是处理社区突发心脏病事件时，安抚一名情绪激动的学生，陪伴对方直到家属抵达。 他说：“当时他情绪非常激动，我就在旁边陪着他。虽然只是短短20多分钟的等待，但对当时的他来说，有人陪伴是很重要的。这也是我参与急救工作学到的，急救不仅仅是救治，也包括给予心灵上的支持，而不是救完就走。” 街访街坊 义工 救援 卫塞节 上一篇 两青少年私召车内吸电子烟变“迷糊” 司机半路向交警求助 下一篇 发布冒犯回教徒脸书贴文 85岁医生被判罚款1万元 购买此文章
description_translated: Volunteer first responders attended two Vesak Day events to protect the safety of the public. On May 12, the day of Vesak Day, while many people were immersed in the celebrations, 50-year-old bread factory logistics manager Ye Linxiong rushed to Tzu Chi Baisha Jing Si Hall and Guangming Shan Phor Jie Zen Temple to maintain the safety of the people on site. Although he was on duty for more than 10 hours, he didn't feel tired. Vesak Day is an important day for Buddhists to commemorate the birth, enlightenment and nirvana of Buddha, also known as "Buddha Day". On that day, celebration activities such as Buddha bathing, blessings, and performances attracted a large number of people to participate. Emergency personnel were also on standby to respond to emergencies at any time. In an interview with Lianhe Zaobao at the Tzu Chi event, this volunteer who was originally from Malaysia said that he joined the Red Cross when he was in middle school and continued to participate in volunteer services after coming to Singapore in 1994. It has been nearly 30 years. "Large events usually have first aid personnel. We mainly provide help in emergencies. For example, if someone suddenly feels unwell, we will first observe the situation, take care of him, ask about his symptoms, and comfort him. If necessary, we will advise him to go to the hospital; if the situation is urgent, such as a heart attack, we will immediately provide first aid to gain the crucial 'golden 10 minutes' and wait for the ambulance to arrive." Ye Linxiong is also a community first responder on the myResponder app of the Singapore Civil Defense Force. He handled 27 emergency cases last year. He also serves as a member of Eunos’ Committee for Emergency Response and Engagement (C2E), Community Emergency Response Team (CERT), and Citizens’ Patrol Team (COP). Further reading: An autistic teenager loves Chinese and opens up a path for learning Chinese. She is the same age as the Ministry of Manpower. The 70-year-old chief statistician has served for half a century and witnessed changes. Ye Linxiong recalled that his most unforgettable first aid experience was when dealing with a heart attack in the community. He comforted an agitated student and stayed with him until his family members arrived. He said: "He was very emotional at the time, and I stayed with him. Although it was only a short wait of more than 20 minutes, it was very important for him to have someone with him at that time. This is what I learned from participating in first aid work. First aid is not only treatment, but also includes providing spiritual support, rather than just leaving after rescuing." title: 首次与漫画人物办“捐血希望”活动 红十字会呼吁公众踊跃捐血
description: 首次与漫画人物办“捐血希望”活动 红十字会呼吁公众踊跃捐血 本地血液库存每逢年底佳节一般会减少约两成。 新加坡红十字 会配合75周年庆，与同样庆祝75周年的花生漫画及卫生科学局联手，启动为期一个月的“捐血希望”活动，呼吁公众积极捐血救人。 “捐血希望”（Ho-Ho-Hope of Blood）活动启动仪式，星期六（11月30日）早上在卫生科学局血库（Bloodbank@HSA）举行。参与者参加了声音浴冥想、现场肖像漫画、果胶临时纹身、DIY手链制作、塔罗牌占卜等活动。已成功捐血的公众，则获得花生漫画（Peanuts）的海滩毛巾，还可参加圣诞花环工作坊。首75名注册的捐血者，还获得了花生漫画袜子。 家喻户晓的花生漫画卡通人物史努比（Snoopy）、露西（Lucy）和查理·布朗（Charlie Brown），也与捐血吉祥物Blood Buddy一起亮相，为捐血者和访客带来欢乐。这些卡通形象还将出现在各个血库，让公众拍照打卡。 所有捐血者均可获赠便签纸和渔夫帽等独家花生漫画周边礼品，传递节日的温暖与感谢。（白艳琳摄） 活动期间，各个血库将装点上花生漫画主题节日装饰，所有捐血者均可获赠便签纸和渔夫帽等独家花生漫画周边礼品，传递节日的温暖与感谢。这些礼品将在12月期间于各血库分发，送完即止。 新加坡红十字会网站的最新数据显示，截至星期六上午，仅AB+血型处于低库存状态，O+、O-、AB-以及B-血型处于适中库存状态，其余血型处于健康库存状态。 延伸阅读 六旬叔捐血42年累计348次 排前三名 青年捐血者比率十年减半 红十字会新计划鼓励青年定期捐血 首75名注册成新加坡红十字的捐血者，还获得了花生漫画袜子。（白艳琳摄） 新加坡红十字会献血者计划主任陈佩珊接受《联合早报》采访时指出，尽管今年底血库的存量情况比往年稍好一些，但库存仍在下降。 她说，日本红十字会与卡通形象合作，成功触及更多年轻人捐血，新加坡红十字会从中得到启发，于是今年也首次在本地展开这类试点，希望吸引更多青年捐血者。 新加坡红十字会 捐血 卫生科学局 上一篇 卫生部明年1月 全国推行HIV自检试剂盒 下一篇 无业男尾随老妇 趁开锁时抢钱包 购买此文章
description_translated: For the first time, the Red Cross held a "Blood Donation Hope" event with comic characters. The Red Cross called on the public to donate blood. Local blood stocks generally decrease by about 20% during the year-end holidays. In conjunction with the 75th anniversary, the Singapore Red Cross has joined hands with the Peanuts comic strip and the Health Sciences Authority, which is also celebrating its 75th anniversary, to launch the month-long "Donate Blood for Hope" campaign, calling on the public to actively donate blood to save lives. The launch ceremony of the "Ho-Ho-Hope of Blood" event was held on the morning of Saturday (November 30) at the Bloodbank@HSA. Participants participated in activities such as sound bath meditation, live portrait caricatures, pectin temporary tattoos, DIY bracelet making, tarot card readings and more. Members of the public who have successfully donated blood will receive Peanuts beach towels and can also participate in a Christmas wreath workshop. The first 75 registered blood donors also received Peanuts socks. The well-known Peanuts cartoon characters Snoopy, Lucy and Charlie Brown also appeared together with the blood donation mascot Blood Buddy to bring joy to blood donors and visitors. These cartoon images will also appear in various blood banks for the public to take photos and check in. All blood donors will receive exclusive Peanuts peripheral gifts such as sticky notes and bucket hats to convey holiday warmth and gratitude. (Photo by Bai Yanlin) During the event, each blood bank will be decorated with Peanuts-themed holiday decorations, and all blood donors will receive exclusive Peanuts-related gifts such as sticky notes and bucket hats to convey the warmth and gratitude of the holiday. These gifts will be distributed at various blood banks during December while supplies last. The latest data from the Singapore Red Cross website shows that as of Saturday morning, only AB+ blood types are in low inventory, O+, O-, AB- and B- blood types are in moderate inventory, and the remaining blood types are in healthy inventory. Further reading: Uncle in his sixties has donated blood a total of 348 times in 42 years, ranking in the top three. The rate of young blood donors has halved in ten years. The Red Cross has a new plan to encourage young people to donate blood regularly. The first 75 blood donors to register with the Singapore Red Cross also received Peanuts socks. title: 六旬叔捐血42年累计348次 排前三名
description: 六旬叔捐血42年累计348次 排前三名 多年无偿捐血不求回报，六旬阿叔捐血42年，目前累计348次，是本地捐血次数最多的前三名。 你坚持过最久的事是什么？60岁的林矜锟除了是保险公司经纪、慈济基金会义工，也是一名定期献血者。 林矜锟从18岁开始捐血，一捐就是42年。“当时我也不知道为什么我会想捐，可能就是为了救人吧。” 他接着说：“很多时候，我们都不知道自己的血究竟是捐给谁，但在慈济当义工的时候，我听到其他义工曾说家人因别人捐的血而得以存活，这让我备受感动。” 捐血一般上是三个月一次，热心的林矜锟每三个月到血库报到，后来他觉得每三个月一次太久了，所以在工作人员的建议下，他改成捐献血小板和血浆，这一过程称之为捐成分血（Apheresis）。这使他能将捐血频率从每12周一次，缩短到每28天一次。 延伸阅读 热血瑜伽导师 热心捐血200次 青年捐血者比率十年减半 红十字会新计划鼓励青年定期捐血 谈到是什么原因让他愿意持续42年不间断捐血，林矜锟坦言，最初是为了新加坡红十字会的荣誉奖，但多年前早已达200次，获得终身奖（Medal for Life）。“其实很早以前，捐血就变成了习惯。” 目前他已捐血348次，仅差四袋血就超过目前的第一名，预计明年2月能达成。 另外，他也鼓励女儿和姐姐一起捐血。女儿因为经常血红蛋白水平（即铁）不达标，所以捐血次数不多。他的二姐则是几年前开始捐血，至今累计50多次。 对林矜锟来说，捐血已成为他的个人使命。他认为，在拥有一副健康身躯的同时，回馈社会是一种荣幸。他也呼吁更年轻、更健康的捐血者站出来，帮助红十字会填补血库。 完整报道，请翻阅2024年10月29日的《新明日报》。 捐血 红十字会 上一篇 文庆组屋走廊挂“断肢” 万圣节装饰惹议 下一篇 妇女获颁庭令 禁止楼下邻居家中吸烟 购买此文章
description_translated: My 60-year-old uncle has donated blood for 42 years and has donated blood 348 times in total, ranking in the top three. He has donated blood for many years without asking for anything in return. My uncle in his 60s has donated blood for 42 years and has donated blood 348 times so far. He is among the top three locals with the most blood donations. What's the longest thing you've done? In addition to being an insurance agent and Tzu Chi Foundation volunteer, 60-year-old Lin Jinkun is also a regular blood donor. Lin Jinkun started donating blood at the age of 18 and has been donating for 42 years. "I didn't know why I wanted to donate at the time. Maybe it was just to save people." He continued: "Many times, we don't know who our blood is donated to, but when I was a volunteer at Tzu Chi, I heard other volunteers say that their family members survived because of blood donated by others, which moved me deeply." Blood donation is generally done once every three months. The enthusiastic Lin Jinkun reported to the blood bank every three months. Later, he felt that once every three months was too long, so at the suggestion of the staff, he changed to donating platelets and plasma. This process is called blood component donation (Apheresis). This allowed him to reduce the frequency of donating blood from once every 12 weeks to once every 28 days. Extended reading: Hot Blood Yoga Instructor enthusiastically donated blood 200 times. The rate of young blood donors has halved in ten years. The Red Cross Society’s new plan encourages young people to donate blood regularly. Talking about the reasons why he is willing to donate blood non-stop for 42 years, Lin Jinkun said frankly that it was initially for the Honorary Award of the Singapore Red Cross Society, but many years ago, he had already donated blood 200 times and won the Medal for Life. "Actually, donating blood has become a habit a long time ago." He has donated blood 348 times so far. He is only four bags of blood away from surpassing the current first place. He is expected to achieve it in February next year. In addition, he also encouraged his daughter and sister to donate blood together. My daughter doesn’t donate blood often because her hemoglobin level (i.e. iron) often falls short of the standard. His second sister started donating blood a few years ago and has donated blood more than 50 times so far. For Lin Jinkun, donating blood has become his personal mission. He believes that it is a privilege to give back to society while maintaining a healthy body. He also called on younger, healthier blood donors to come forward and help the Red Cross fill its blood banks. For the complete report, please read the Shin Min Daily News on October 29, 2024. title: Bekalan darah jenis AB-, AB+ dan A+ di paras kritikal
description: BEKALAN darah nasional telah menurun sebanyak satu pertiga semasa wabak Covid-19 di Singapura, walaupun bank darah telah pulih setelah menghadapi kekurangan bekalan darah secara tiba-tiba pada minggu tempoh pemutus rantaian jangkitan dilaksanakan. Pada masa itu, hanya seperempat daripada pengumpulan darah yang biasa dibuat dapat dilaksanakan, jumlah yang jauh di bawah keperluan harian negara. Sumbangan kembali meningkat setelah rayuan dibuat di media sosial dan tradisional. Sehingga Jumaat lalu, bekalan darah untuk jenis AB-, AB+ dan A+ berada di tahap kritikal dan A-dan O- pula berada pada tahap rendah. Pertubuhan Palang Merah Singapura menyatakan penurunan penderma darah dalam tempoh pemutus litar lebih besar daripada yang biasanya terjadi pada musim perayaan, hujung minggu yang panjang dan cuti sekolah, apabila sumbangan merosot 20 peratus. "Kami menyedari ramai penderma elak keluar rumah tanpa perlu. Sebilangan penderma mungkin tidak menyedari bahawa pendermaan darah tetap menjadi perkhidmatan penting dan bank darah kami masih terbuka," kata seorang jurucakap Palang Merah Singapura (SRC). "Kami juga tidak dapat melakukan usaha mengumpul darah di lapangan dengan kerap seperti sebelumnya," tambah jurucakap itu. Pada masa ini, hanya empat sesi di lapangan diadakan setiap minggu berbanding dengan sekurang-kurangnya 10 acara sedemikian setiap minggu pada masa lalu. Setiap tahun, hampir 30,000 pesakit di Singapura memerlukan bekalan darah yang berterusan untuk terus hidup. Negara ini memerlukan sekitar 400 beg darah setiap hari untuk memenuhi keperluan darah pesakit. Sejauh ini, SRC menyatakan ia belum pernah menafikan keperluan pesakit yang memerlukan transfusi darah. - The Straits Times Anda ada maklumat mengenai sesuatu berita menarik?E-mel: bhnews@sph.com.sg
description_translated: The national blood SUPPLY has dropped by a third during the Covid-19 outbreak in Singapore, although the blood bank has recovered after facing a sudden shortage of blood during the week the chain-breaking period was implemented. At that time, only a quarter of the usual blood collection was made possible, an amount far below the country's daily needs. Donations increased again after appeals were made on social and traditional media. Until last Friday, the blood supply for types AB-, AB+ and A+ was at a critical level and A- and O- were at a low level. The Singapore Red Cross said the drop in blood donations during the circuit breaker period was greater than usual during festive seasons, long weekends and school holidays, when donations dropped by 20 percent. "We are aware that many donors avoid leaving home unnecessarily. Some donors may not realize that blood donation remains an important service and that our blood bank is still open," said a Singapore Red Cross (SRC) spokesperson. "We are also unable to conduct blood collection efforts in the field as often as before," added the spokesperson. Currently, only four field sessions are held each week compared to at least 10 such events per week in the past. Every year, nearly 30,000 patients in Singapore need a continuous supply of blood to survive. The country needs around 400 bags of blood every day to meet the blood needs of patients. So far, the SRC stated that it has never denied the needs of patients who need blood transfusions. - The Straits Times Do you have information about any interesting news? Email: bhnews@sph.com.sg

title: Palang Merah S’pura kumpul hampir $1.5j bantu mangsa gempa di Myanmar, Thailand
description: Hampir $1.5 juta telah dikumpulkan untuk menyokong operasi bantuan dan pemulihan di Myanmar dan Thailand, selepas satu gempa bumi bermagnitud 7.7  menggegarkan kedua-dua negara itu pada 28 Mac. Pertubuhan Palang Merah Singapura (SRC), yang melancarkan rayuan mengumpul dana itu pada 30 Mac, turut menghantar 90 penapis air mudah alih ke bandar Mandalay dan Sagaing di Myanmar pada 2 April. Pusat gempa itu adalah di Sagaing, iaitu kira-kira 240km ke utara ibu negara Naypyidaw. Gempa bumi itu telah meranapkan banyak bangunan di seluruh Myanmar, mengorbankan lebih 2,700 orang dan menyebabkan beribu-ribu lagi kehilangan tempat tinggal. Angka kematian dijangka meningkat. Di Bangkok, runtuhan sebuah bangunan pencakar langit 30 tingkat yang dalam pembinaan telah mengorbankan sekurang-kurangnya 15 orang, dengan 72 yang lain dipercayai masih terperangkap di bawah runtuhan. Di seluruh Thailand, jumlah kematian telah mencecah sekurang-kurangnya 22 orang. Encik Benjamin William, setiausaha agung dan ketua eksekutif SRC, mengucapkan terima kasih kepada rakyat Singapura kerana telah bermurah hati menyahut rayuan mengumpul dana itu, lapor The Straits Times. “Gempa bumi itu menambah krisis kemanusiaan yang sudah teruk disebabkan oleh konflik, perpindahan manusia dan bencana masa lalu,” katanya, sambil menambah bahawa langkah menyediakan saluran air bersih akan mengurangkan risiko penyakit bawaan air. SRC juga akan terus mendekati masyarakat migran Myanmar dan Thai di Singapura dan menawarkan sokongan psikososial kepada mereka, kata Encik William. SRC akan menganjurkan satu acara kemasyarakatan pada 6 April untuk menawarkan sokongan kesihatan mental kepada migran Myanmar dan Thai yang berpangkalan di Singapura, yang mempunyai orang tersayang yang terjejas akibat gempa itu. Acara di Red Cross House di Penang Lane itu akan menampilkan kegiatan sokongan kesihatan mental dan psikososial, serta menyediakan pertolongan cemas psikologi, makanan, minuman dan Wi-Fi untuk orang ramai menghubungi keluarga mereka di tanah air. Rayuan mengumpul dana SRC itu akan berakhir pada 31 Mei. Derma boleh dibuat melalui kad kredit, PayNow, cek atau secara langsung di Red Cross House dari 9 pagi hingga 6 petang dari Isnin hingga Jumaat. Penderma korporat dan individu boleh menuntut potongan cukai untuk derma mereka, kata SRC. Derma melalui kad kredit boleh dilakukan di laman web Giving.sg atau portal sumbangan Palang Merah. Cek mesti dibuat kepada “Singapore Red Cross Society” dan dihantar ke Red Cross House, 15 Penang Lane, Singapura 238486. Penderma hendaklah menyertakan nama dan alamat mereka, dan nyatakan “Myanmar & Thailand Earthquake” di belakang cek tersebut. description_translated: Nearly $1.5 million has been raised to support relief and recovery operations in Myanmar and Thailand, after a 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck both countries on March 28. The Singapore Red Cross Society (SRC), which launched the fundraising appeal on March 30, also sent 90 portable water filters to the Myanmar cities of Mandalay and Sagaing on April 2. The epicenter was in Sagaing, which is about 240km north of the capital Naypyidaw. The earthquake has destroyed many buildings across Myanmar, killing more than 2,700 people and leaving thousands more homeless. The death toll is expected to rise. In Bangkok, the collapse of a 30-story skyscraper under construction has killed at least 15 people, with 72 others believed to be still trapped under the rubble. Across Thailand, the death toll has reached at least 22 people. Mr Benjamin William, secretary-general and chief executive of the SRC, thanked Singaporeans for generously responding to the fundraising appeal, The Straits Times reported. "The earthquake added to the already severe humanitarian crisis caused by conflict, human displacement and past disasters," he said, adding that measures to provide clean water channels would reduce the risk of water-borne diseases. The SRC will also continue to reach out to the Myanmar and Thai migrant communities in Singapore and offer psychosocial support to them, said Mr William. The SRC will organize a community event on April 6 to offer mental health support to Myanmar and Thai migrants based in Singapore, who have loved ones affected by the earthquake. The event at the Red Cross House in Penang Lane will feature mental health and psychosocial support activities, as well as provide psychological first aid, food, drinks and Wi-Fi for people to contact their families back home. The SRC fundraising appeal will end on May 31. Donations can be made by credit card, PayNow, check or in person at the Red Cross House from 9am to 6pm Monday to Friday. Corporate and individual donors can claim tax deductions for their donations, the SRC said. Donations via credit card can be made on the Giving.sg website or the Red Cross donation portal. Checks must be made out to “Singapore Red Cross Society” and sent to Red Cross House, 15 Penang Lane, Singapore 238486. full_content_eng: Nearly $1.5 million has been raised to support relief and recovery operations in Myanmar and Thailand, after a 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck both countries on March 28. The Singapore Red Cross Society (SRC), which launched the fundraising appeal on March 30, also sent 90 portable water filters to the Myanmar cities of Mandalay and Sagaing on April 2. The epicenter was in Sagaing, which is about 240km north of the capital Naypyidaw. The earthquake has destroyed many buildings across Myanmar, killing more than 2,700 people and leaving thousands more homeless. The death toll is expected to rise. In Bangkok, the collapse of a 30-story skyscraper under construction has killed at least 15 people, with 72 others believed to be still trapped under the rubble. Across Thailand, the death toll has reached at least 22 people. Mr Benjamin William, secretary-general and chief executive of the SRC, thanked Singaporeans for generously responding to the fundraising appeal, The Straits Times reported. "The earthquake added to the already severe humanitarian crisis caused by conflict, human displacement and past disasters," he said, adding that measures to provide clean water channels would reduce the risk of water-borne diseases. The SRC will also continue to reach out to the Myanmar and Thai migrant communities in Singapore and offer psychosocial support to them, said Mr William. The SRC will organize a community event on April 6 to offer mental health support to Myanmar and Thai migrants based in Singapore, who have loved ones affected by the earthquake. The event at the Red Cross House in Penang Lane will feature mental health and psychosocial support activities, as well as provide psychological first aid, food, drinks and Wi-Fi for people to contact their families back home. The SRC fundraising appeal will end on May 31. Donations can be made by credit card, PayNow, check or in person at the Red Cross House from 9am to 6pm Monday to Friday. Corporate and individual donors can claim tax deductions for their donations, the SRC said. Donations via credit card can be made on the Giving.sg website or the Red Cross donation portal. Checks must be made out to “Singapore Red Cross Society” and sent to Red Cross House, 15 Penang Lane, Singapore 238486. title: Palang Merah S’pura ikrar $50,000 bantu mangsa banjir kilat Afghanistan
description: Pertubuhan Palang Merah Singapura (SRC) telah mengikrarkan sebanyak $50,000 bagi membantu mangsa banjir kilat di Afghanistan, selain melancarkan rayuan mengumpul dana untuk menyokong operasi bantuan dan pemulihan. Dalam satu kenyataan media pada 20 Mei, SRC berkata dana tersebut akan digunakan untuk memenuhi keperluan segera mangsa yang terjejas, termasuk menyediakan makanan, tempat perlindungan kecemasan, penjagaan trauma kecemasan, barangan bukan makanan, serta air, sanitasi dan keperluan kebersihan. Bantuan itu juga secara tidak langsung akan meningkatkan usaha bantuan yang dikendalikan Masyarakat Sabit Merah Afghan (ARCS) dan Persekutuan Antarabangsa Palang Merah dan Masyarakat Sabit Merah (IFRC), tambahnya. “Kami sedih dengan kehilangan nyawa, kecederaan, dan kesan ke atas rumah dan mata pencarian akibat banjir kilat,” kata Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif SRC, Encik Benjamin William. “Kami sedang bekerja rapat dengan rakan kongsi kami dari Pergerakan Bulan Sabit Merah untuk terus mendapatkan perkembangan terkini terhadap situasi di situ. “Sedang kami memulakan usaha mengumpul dana kami, kami juga berharap rakyat Singapura akan bersama kami dalam menyokong masyarakat yang memerlukan.” Dalam kenyataannya lagi, SRC berkata bahawa ARCS, dengan kerjasama rakan kongsinya, sedang menyediakan bantuan segera kepada mereka yang dipindahkan dengan memudahkan pergerakan mereka, menyediakan tempat perlindungan sementara, dan menawarkan perkhidmatan kesihatan kecemasan mudah alih, yang dilengkapi keperluan pertolongan cemas penting. IFRC juga mengerahkan pasukan tindak balas kecemasan untuk menyokong operasi bantuan dan secara berterusan menilai keperluan yang mendesak di kawasan terjejas. Usaha mengumpul dana itu akan berlangsung dari 20 Mei hingga 31 Ogos. Banjir kilat akibat hujan lebat sejak 10 Mei telah memusnahkan kawasan perkampungan di utara Afghanistan. Ia mengakibatkan lebih 300 orang terkorban sementara lebih 1,600 lagi cedera, kata pihak berkuasa pada 19 Mei. Bencana alam itu juga mengakibatkan lebih 3,000 rumah musnah, merosakkan jalan raya dan jambatan, serta menyaksikan kerugian besar terhadap bidang ternakan dan pertanian. Keadaan muka bumi yang mencabar dan infrastruktur yang rosak telah menyukarkan lagi operasi bantuan untuk sampai ke kawasan yang memerlukan bantuan. Jabatan meteorologi Afghanistan telah memberi amaran tentang cuaca hujan yang berterusan dan kemungkinan banjir kilat yang merentasi semua wilayah negara itu. Menurut Program Makanan Sedunia Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu (PBB), bantuan masih belum lagi dapat dihantar ke Baghlan, wilayah yang teruk terjejas akibat banjir kilat itu. Afghanistan terdedah kepada bencana alam, dan PBB menganggapnya sebagai salah satu negara yang paling terdedah kepada perubahan iklim. Pakar iklim berkata Afghanistan - yang sedang dilanda perang dan terasing daripada dunia sejak Taliban mengambil alih kuasa pada 2021 - adalah salah satu negara yang paling kurang bersedia menangani kesan perubahan iklim. Setakat ini, 25 daripada 34 wilayah di Afghanistan terjejas akibat banjir, tambah SRC, manakala hujan masih diramalkan di kawasan terjejas dalam beberapa hari akan datang. Mereka yang ingin menderma kepada usaha mengumpul dana ini boleh berbuat demikian menerusi laman SRC. Anda ada maklumat mengenai sesuatu berita menarik?E-mel: bhnews@sph.com.sg
description_translated: The Singapore Red Cross Society (SRC) has pledged $50,000 to help victims of flash floods in Afghanistan, in addition to launching a fundraising appeal to support relief and recovery operations. In a media statement on May 20, the SRC said the funds will be used to meet the immediate needs of affected victims, including providing food, emergency shelter, emergency trauma care, non-food items, as well as water, sanitation and hygiene needs. The aid will also indirectly boost the relief efforts run by the Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS) and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), he added. "We are saddened by the loss of life, injuries, and the impact on homes and livelihoods due to flash floods," said SRC Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Benjamin William. "We are working closely with our partners from the Red Crescent Movement to continue to get updates on the situation there. "As we begin our fundraising efforts, we also hope that Singaporeans will join us in supporting communities in need." In its further statement, the SRC said that ARCS, in collaboration with its partners, is providing immediate assistance to those displaced by facilitating their movement, providing temporary shelters, and offering mobile emergency health services, equipped with essential first aid needs. The IFRC also deployed emergency response teams to support relief operations and continuously assess urgent needs in affected areas. The fundraising effort will take place from May 20 to August 31. Flash floods caused by heavy rains since May 10 have destroyed rural areas in northern Afghanistan. It left more than 300 people dead while more than 1,600 others were injured, authorities said on May 19. The natural disaster also resulted in the destruction of more than 3,000 houses, damaged roads and bridges, and witnessed huge losses to livestock and agriculture. Challenging terrain and damaged infrastructure have made it even more difficult for relief operations to reach areas in need. Afghanistan's meteorological department has warned of continued rainy weather and possible flash floods across all regions of the country. According to the World Food Program of the United Nations (UN), aid has yet to be sent to Baghlan, a region badly affected by the flash floods. Afghanistan is vulnerable to natural disasters, and the UN considers it one of the countries most vulnerable to climate change. Climate experts say Afghanistan - which has been ravaged by war and cut off from the world since the Taliban took power in 2021 - is one of the countries least prepared to deal with the effects of climate change. So far, 25 of Afghanistan's 34 provinces have been affected by floods, the SRC added, while rain is still forecast in the affected areas in the coming days. title: Bantuan kemanusiaan dari S’pura bagi penduduk Gaza selamat disampaikan
description: Yayasan Rahmatan Lil Alamin (RLAF) telah menyerahkan cek berjumlah $2 juta berkat sumbangan warga Singapura kepada  Agensi Bantuan dan Kerja Menyelamat Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu (UNRWA) bagi Pelarian Palestin (UNRWA) di Kahirah, Mesir pada Jumaat bagi menyokong usaha kemanusiaan yang sedang berlangsung di Gaza. Di ibu pejabat Persatuan Bulan Sabit Merah Mesir (ERC) di Kahirah pada Sabtu pula, Palang Merah Singapura (SRC) turut mengumumkan akan menyerahkan bantuan tambahan AS$100,000 ($136,090) kepada ERC bagi membantu pembelian barangan kemanusiaan yang amat diperlukan di Gaza. Sebelum ini, SRC telah menghantar bekalan bantuan kemanusiaan bernilai AS$200,000 kepada ERC bagi membantu mangsa konflik di Gaza. Penyerahan bantuan oleh RLAF dan SRC kepada UNRWA dan ERC di Kahirah itu turut disaksikan Menteri di Pejabat Perdana Menteri, Dr Mohamad Maliki Osman, yang dalam lawatan kerjanya di Mesir. “Saya berbesar hati dapat menyaksikan penyerahan bantuan kemanusiaan daripada RLAF dan SRC kepada UNRWA dan ERC. “Krisis kemanusiaan yang semakin meruncing di Gaza adalah satu tragedi, dan terdapat keperluan mendesak untuk bantuan kemanusiaan dihulurkan kepada orang awam di Gaza. “Saya bangga rakyat Singapura telah tampil dengan murah hati untuk menyokong keperluan ini,” kata Dr Maliki, yang juga Menteri Kedua (Pendidikan merangkap Ehwal Luar). Dr Maliki turut menerima taklimat berasingan oleh ERC di ibu pejabatnya dan UNRWA di Hotel Four Seasons mengenai situasi terkini di sempadan Rafah dan situasi kemanusiaan di Gaza. Dr Maliki juga berkesempatan ke gedung ERC dan bertemu dengan relawan dan kakitangan ERC yang sedang menyediakan bekalan bantuan kemanusiaan yang akan dibawa pula ke gedung ERC berdekatan dengan sempadan Rafah. Beliau turut menyingsing lengan untuk membantu mereka mengisikan kotak-kotak dengan barang makanan dan ubat-ubatan yang akan dibawa masuk ke Gaza. Dalam pertemuannya dengan pemimpin Mesir dari 9 hingga 11 November, Dr Maliki mengesahkan sokongan Singapura terhadap usaha bantuan kemanusiaan oleh pemerintah Mesir, PBB dan rakan kongsi lain untuk memberi kelegaan bagi menangani situasi kemanusiaan yang teruk di Gaza. Semasa majlis penyerahan cek oleh RLAF kepada UNRWA pada Jumaat, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif (CEO) RLAF, Encik Faizal Othman berkata beliau terharu melihat sokongan padu semua lapisan masyarakat di Singapura yang menyokong kempen itu. Beliau turut mengumumkan setakat ini, RLAF telah berjaya mengumpul lebih $5.7 juta daripada warga Singapura, dan akan berusaha menyerahkan dana itu secara bertahap kepada UNRWA. Jumlah itu merupakan rekod tertinggi dalam sejarah RLAF. “Hari ini, kami menyerahkan sebahagian daripada kutipan RLAF sebanyak $2 juta kepada UNRWA, supaya mereka boleh mempercepatkan kerja-kerja bantuan yang diperlukan di Gaza. “Kami memanjatkan doa dan harapan kami kepada mangsa yang tidak bersalah dalam konflik ini, dan saya berharap sumbangan kami akan memperbaiki keadaan mangsa yang terselamat. Kami mengucapkan terima kasih kepada semua yang telah menderma dengan ikhlas hati,” kata Encik Faizal. Penyelaras Kanan Prinsip Kemanusiaan UNRWA, Encik Andrew Hyslop menyambut baik sokongan pemerintah dan rakyat Singapura untuk membantu menyegerakan bantuan kemanusiaan bagi penduduk Palestin. “Bagi pihak UNRWA dan pelarian Palestin yang kami bantu, saya mengucapkan terima kasih atas sokongan para penderma yang murah hati. “Kami berbesar hati dan kami berterima kasih atas kerjasama pemerintah Singapura dan rakyat Singapura, khususnya RLAF, dalam menyokong usaha kita untuk menyediakan bekalan kemanusiaan yang genting untuk penduduk di Gaza,” kata Encik Hyslop. description_translated: The Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation (RLAF) has handed over a $2 million check thanks to the contribution of Singaporeans to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) in Cairo, Egypt on Friday to support the ongoing humanitarian efforts in Gaza. At the headquarters of the Egyptian Red Crescent Society (ERC) in Cairo on Saturday, the Singapore Red Cross (SRC) also announced that it will hand over US$100,000 ($136,090) in additional aid to the ERC to help purchase much-needed humanitarian goods in Gaza. Previously, SRC had sent humanitarian aid supplies worth US$200,000 to ERC to help victims of the conflict in Gaza. The handover of aid by RLAF and SRC to UNRWA and ERC in Cairo was also witnessed by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Dr Mohamad Maliki Osman, who was on a working visit to Egypt. "I was honored to witness the handover of humanitarian aid from RLAF and SRC to UNRWA and ERC. "The worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza is a tragedy, and there is an urgent need for humanitarian aid to be extended to the civilians in Gaza. "I am proud that Singaporeans have generously come forward to support this need," said Dr Maliki, who is also the Second Minister (Education and Foreign Affairs). Dr Maliki also received separate briefings by ERC at its headquarters and UNRWA at the Four Seasons Hotel on the latest situation at the Rafah border and the humanitarian situation in Gaza. Dr Maliki also had the opportunity to go to the ERC building and meet with ERC volunteers and staff who are preparing humanitarian aid supplies that will be brought to the ERC building near the Rafah border. He also extended his arm to help them fill boxes with food and medicine to be brought into Gaza. In his meeting with Egyptian leaders from 9 to 11 November, Dr Maliki confirmed Singapore's support for humanitarian aid efforts by the Egyptian government, the UN and other partners to provide relief to deal with the dire humanitarian situation in Gaza. During the check handover ceremony by RLAF to UNRWA on Friday, RLAF Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Mr. Faizal Othman said he was moved to see the strong support from all walks of life in Singapore who supported the campaign. He also announced that so far, RLAF has managed to collect more than $5.7 million from Singaporeans, and will try to gradually hand over the funds to UNRWA. That number is the highest record in the history of the RLAF. "Today, we hand over part of the RLAF collection of $2 million to UNRWA, so that they can speed up the relief work needed in Gaza. "We extend our prayers and hopes to the innocent victims of this conflict, and I hope that our contribution will improve the situation of the survivors. We thank all those who have donated sincerely," said Mr. Faizal. UNRWA's Senior Coordinator of Humanitarian Principles, Mr. Andrew Hyslop welcomed the support of the government and the people of Singapore to help speed up humanitarian aid for the Palestinian people. "On behalf of UNRWA and the Palestinian refugees we help, I thank the donors for their generous support. "We are honored and we are grateful for the cooperation of the Singapore government and Singaporeans, particularly the RLAF, in supporting our efforts to provide critical humanitarian supplies to the people of Gaza," said Mr Hyslop. title: Masjid anjur kempen derma darah
description: Dengan misi mahu mendekati masyarakat dan membantu ummah, Masjid Alkaff Kampung Melayu telah mengadakan kempen derma darah pada 24 Februari lalu. Bagi menjayakannya, masjid ini telah bekerjasama dengan Palang Merah Singapura (SRC) serta sukarelawan Kecemasan dan Pendekatan Masyarakat (C2E) di kawasan Eunos. Bertempat di pekarangan masjid di Bedok Reservoir Road itu, sekitar 60 orang awam menghadirkan diri untuk acara tersebut. Malah, penderma bukan Islam juga turut menyokong kempen derma darah tersebut. Menurut Pengurus Masjid Alkaff Kampung Melayu, Ustaz Mohd Taufiq Mohd Ismail, sebelum ini, Masjid Alkaff Kampung Melayu telah mengadakan beberapa acara derma darah. Namun, ia terpaksa dihentikan kerana Covid-19. Sambutan yang diterima daripada orang ramai juga, cukup memberangsangkan. Beliau berkata banyak kelebihan apabila seseorang menderma darah. Selain dapat membantu orang lain, menderma darah juga digalakkan dalam Islam. “Amalan menderma darah adalah satu usaha yang mulia, serta mampu menyelamatkan nyawa seseorang yang memerlukannya. “Apabila kita lihat dalam Al-Quran sendiri, terdapat banyak ayat yang menitikberatkan pemeliharaan jiwa seperti yang terakam dalam Surah Al-Maidah, ayat 32 yang bermaksud: ‘Dan barang siapa yang memelihara kehidupan seorang manusia, maka seolah-olah dia telah memelihara kehidupan seluruh manusia.’ “Oleh itu, kami bertekad mahu menghidupkan semula kempen derma darah ini di Masjid Alkaff Kampung Melayu. Kali terakhir kami anjurkan kempen ini adalah pada 2019 sebelum Covid-19 melanda,” jelas Ustaz Mohd Taufiq. Ustaz Mohd Taufiq memberitahu Berita Harian (BH), sebelum menderma, penderma perlu menjalani beberapa saringan ujian kesihatan, yang dilakukan pada hari tersebut. Setelah disahkan dan diperiksa oleh doktor yang bertugas, hanya mereka yang layak sahaja boleh meneruskan pendermaan darah mereka. “Pengurusan doktor dan petugas kesihatan serta sukarelawan C2E dari Eunos juga membantu menguar-uarkan kempen ini kepada penduduk di kejiranan di Bedok Reservoir agar tampil menderma darah. “Kami amat terharu apabila melihat sebilangan penderma yang bukan berbangsa Melayu atau beragama Islam yang turut hadir di masjid pada hari tersebut untuk menderma (darah). Ini menunjukkan semangat menghulurkan bantuan menjangkaui batasan bangsa ataupun agama di negara ini, dan mereka yang tampil juga merangkumi pelbagai latar belakang ” ujar Ustaz Mohd Taufiq. Menurut Ustaz Mohd Taufiq, sekitar 60 orang tampil menderma darah pada hari tersebut namun atas sebab-sebab tertentu, hanya 36 daripada mereka layak dan berjaya mendermakan darah mereka. Jumlah ini tidak menghambat hati penganjur yang telah pun merancang mahu menganjurkan lagi kempen derma darah ini pada pertengahan kedua tahun 2024. “Kami amat berharap lebih ramai yang akan hadir untuk menyokong kempen derma darah ini. Kami berharap dapat mengadakan lagi pada masa akan datang, mungkin pada Ogos nanti. Namun, semuanya masih dalam perbincangan. “Selain itu, masjid ini mengharapkan sokongan semua bagi ‘Projek Peningkatan Masjid Alkaff Kampung Melayu’ yang akan berlangsung tidak lama lagi,” tambahnya. description_translated: With a mission to reach out to the community and help the community, Masjid Alkaff Kampung Melayu held a blood donation campaign on February 24. To make it a success, the mosque has collaborated with the Singapore Red Cross (SRC) and Community Emergency and Outreach (C2E) volunteers in the Eunos area. Located in the grounds of the mosque in Bedok Reservoir Road, around 60 members of the public attended the event. In fact, non-Muslim donors also support the blood donation campaign. According to the Manager of Alkaff Kampung Melayu Mosque, Ustaz Mohd Taufiq Mohd Ismail, previously, Alkaff Kampung Melayu Mosque has held several blood donation events. However, it had to be stopped due to Covid-19. The response received from the public was also quite encouraging. He said there are many advantages when someone donates blood. Gempa bumi kuat berukuran 7.7 pada skala Richter melanda bahagian tengah Myanmar dan Thailand pada tengah hari Jumaat (28 Mac). Menurut kenyataan medianya pada Sabtu, sumbangan tersebut adalah bagi menghulurkan bekalan bantuan, termasuk makanan, air, selimut, kain tarpaulin dan kit kebersihan yang disediakan oleh Persatuan Palang Merah Myanmar (MRCS) dan Persatuan Palang Merah Thailand (TRCS). Selain itu, Palang Merah Singapura akan melancarkan kempen pengumpulan dana tidak lama lagi, dengan butirannya dijangka didedahkan di laman Palang Merah Singapura nanti. Hasil daripada kutipan dana tersebut akan disalurkan secara langsung bagi menyokong operasi bantuan dan pemulihan bagi penduduk yang terjejas. Setiausaha Agung/ Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif (CEO) SRC, Encik Benjamin William menyuarakan rasa keprihatinan yang mendalam terhadap mereka yang terjejas. "Ramai orang cedera, kehilangan tempat tinggal dan memerlukan bantuan mendesak. Kemusnahan meluas ke atas prasarana menghambat operasi menyelamat dan bantuan segera di lapangan. "Skala kemusnahan memerlukan tindak balas kemanusiaan yang pantas dan diselaraskan," jelasnya. Beliau menambah: "Kami bekerjasama rapat dengan rakan kongsi Palang Merah kami untuk memastikan bantuan sampai kepada mereka yang paling memerlukannya. Saya merayu kepada orang ramai untuk sama-sama menyokong usaha ini." Dalam pada itu, SRC menekankan kesiapsiagannya untuk menghulurkan bantuan lanjut, seperti mengerahkan responden kemanusiaan dalam menyokong bantuan terhadap mereka yang terjejas. SRC turut melancarkan khidmat "Restoring Family Links" (RFL) bagi membantu para penduduk Singapura yang mengalami kesukaran untuk menghubungi anggota keluarga yang mungkin terjejas oleh bencana tersebut. Mereka yang ingin meminta bantuan boleh mengirimkan emel kepada rfl [at] redcross.sg . A strong earthquake measuring 7.7 on the Richter scale hit central Myanmar and Thailand on Friday afternoon (March 28). According to its media statement on Saturday, the donation was to provide relief supplies, including food, water, blankets, tarpaulin and hygiene kits provided by the Myanmar Red Cross Society (MRCS) and the Thai Red Cross Society (TRCS). In addition, the Singapore Red Cross will soon launch a fundraising campaign, with details expected to be revealed on the Singapore Red Cross website later. The widespread destruction of infrastructure is hampering rescue operations and immediate assistance on the ground. "The scale of the devastation requires a rapid and coordinated humanitarian response," he explained. He added: "We are working closely with our Red Cross partners to ensure that aid reaches those who need it most. I appeal to the public to support this effort." In the meantime, the SRC emphasized its readiness to extend further assistance, such as deploying humanitarian responders to support aid to those affected. The SRC also launched the "Restoring Family Links" (RFL) service to help Singaporeans who are experiencing difficulties in contacting family members who may be affected by the disaster. Those who wish to request assistance can send an email to rfl [at] redcross.sg . title: Had umur penderma darah kali pertama dinaikkan kepada 65 tahun mulai 1 Jan
description: Batas umur untuk penderma darah kali pertama di Singapura akan dinaikkan daripada 60 kepada 65 tahun mulai 1 Januari 2026, sesuai dengan peningkatan jangka hayat dan orang ramai didapati lebih kuat pada usia senja mereka. Bertujuan menambah kumpulan penderma darah, langkah itu dibuat di tengah-tengah data tempatan yang menunjukkan reaksi kurang baik penderma, seperti pengsan dan pening,  berkurangan dalam kalangan penderma kali pertama apabila mereka semakin tua, kata Menteri Kesihatan, Encik Ong Ye Kung, pada 28 Jun. Menurut The Straits Times, perubahan batas umur itu juga sejajar dengan amalan seperti di Hong Kong, Taiwan, Ireland, Belanda, Korea Selatan dan Britain yang membenarkan penderma kali pertama berumur 65 hingga 69 tahun. Had umur penderma kali pertama semasa ialah 60 tahun. Sebelum ini, penderma boleh terus menderma darah sehingga sebelum hari lahirnya yang ke-66. Encik Ong mengumumkan langkah menaikkan had umur itu sempena acara Hari Penderma Darah Sedunia anjuran Palang Merah Singapura (SRC) dan Penguasa Sains Kesihatan (HSA). “Setiap derma darah menyelamatkan sehingga tiga nyawa seperti kanak-kanak yang menghidap barah,  ibu yang bersalin atau  warga emas yang menjalani pembedahan,” katanya pada majlis di Pusat Konvensyen dan Ekspo Sands di Marina Bay Sands. Pada 2023, lebih 35,000 pesakit di Singapura menerima pemindahan darah yang menyelamatkan nyawa. Encik Ong mengimbas bagaimana ibunya memerlukan pemindahan darah yang agak banyak pada masa lalu kerana sakit, tetapi Encik Ong selalu ditolak di bank darah apabila cuba menderma kerana tinggal di Britain pada 1980-an. Singapura pernah menyekat pendermaan darah daripada mereka yang pernah tinggal di Britain kerana kebimbangan terhadap penyakit Varian Creutzfeldt-Jakob (vCJD) yang dikaitkan dengan pemakanan daging lembu yang tercemar. Kebimbangan itu wajar, kata Encik Ong, tetapi beliau bersyukur kerana kini beliau boleh menderma darah selepas HSA melonggarkan sekatan untuk pendermaan darah melalui ‘aphresis’ atau prosedur melibatkan darah diproses bagi mengumpul komponen darah tertentu seperti plasma atau platelet pada 2023. Lebih 2,000 penderma darah dan 37 organisasi telah menerima pujian di majlis itu. SRC dan HSA berkata dalam satu kenyataan bersama bahawa sumbangan ini adalah penting memandangkan cabaran semasa yang dihadapi oleh bekalan darah Singapura. “Memandangkan Singapura menghampiri status ramai warga emas pada 2026, memastikan bekalan darah yang mampan menjadi lebih mendesak,” kata mereka. Penduduk Singapura yang semakin tua memberikan cabaran apabila pesakit berumur 60 tahun ke atas kini menyumbang 60 peratus daripada jumlah penggunaan sel darah merah, namun kumpulan penderma yang layak semakin mengecil, tambah mereka. Bilangan penderma darah baru telah merosot lebih 11 peratus sejak 2013. Singapura mempunyai kira-kira 18,000 penderma baru pada 2024, turun daripada lebih 20,000 pada 2013. SRC dan HSA berkata hanya empat daripada 10 penderma yang menderma lebih daripada sekali setahun. “Kadar derma ulangan yang rendah ini menggariskan keperluan mendesak untuk memupuk lebih ramai penderma komited menjadikan derma darah sebagai sebahagian daripada gaya hidup mereka,” tambah kenyataan itu lagi. description_translated: The age limit for first-time blood donors in Singapore will be raised from 60 to 65 years from 1 January 2026, in line with increasing life expectancy and people getting stronger in their twilight years. Aimed at increasing the pool of blood donors, the move comes amid local data showing adverse donor reactions, such as fainting and dizziness, decrease among first-time donors as they get older, Health Minister Mr Ong Ye Kung said on June 28. According to The Straits Times, the age limit change is also in line with practices in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Ireland, the Netherlands, South Korea and Britain which allow first-time donors to be 65 to 69 years old. The current first-time donor age limit is 60 years. Previously, donors could continue donating blood until before their 66th birthday. Mr Ong announced the move to raise the age limit in conjunction with the World Blood Donor Day event organized by the Singapore Red Cross (SRC) and the Health Sciences Authority (HSA). "Each blood donation saves up to three lives such as a child suffering from cancer, a mother giving birth or an elderly person undergoing surgery," he said at a ceremony at the Sands Convention and Expo Center at Marina Bay Sands. In 2023, more than 35,000 patients in Singapore will receive life-saving blood transfusions. Mr Ong recalled how his mother had needed quite a lot of blood transfusions in the past due to illness, but Mr Ong was always rejected at the blood bank when trying to donate because he lived in Britain in the 1980s. Singapore previously restricted blood donations from those who had lived in Britain due to concerns about Varian Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (vCJD) linked to eating contaminated beef. The concern is justified, said Mr Ong, but he is grateful that he can now donate blood after the HSA eased restrictions on donating blood through 'aphresis' or a procedure involving blood being processed to collect certain blood components such as plasma or platelets in 2023. More than 2,000 blood donors and 37 organizations have received praise at the ceremony. The SRC and HSA said in a joint statement that this donation is important given the current challenges facing Singapore's blood supply. "As Singapore approaches the status of many elderly people in 2026, ensuring a sustainable blood supply becomes even more urgent," they said. Singapore's aging population presents a challenge as patients aged 60 and over now account for 60 percent of total red blood cell consumption, but the pool of eligible donors is shrinking, they added. The number of new blood donors has declined by more than 11 percent since 2013. Singapore has about 18,000 new donors in 2024, down from more than 20,000 in 2013. The SRC and HSA say only four in 10 donors donate more than once a year. "This low repeat donation rate underscores the urgent need to cultivate more committed donors to make blood donation a part of their lifestyle," the statement added. title: Palang Merah S’pura mahu penderma darah lebih muda
description: Inisiatif baru yang dilancarkan Palang Merah Singapura (SRC) kini menyasarkan untuk melibatkan 500 belia berumur 16 hingga 25 tahun dalam tempoh lima tahun akan datang. Menjelang 2030, organisasi itu juga berharap dapat meningkatkan kumpulan penderma belia kepada 25 peratus daripada 15 peratus sekarang. Sepanjang dekad yang lalu, peratusan penderma belia telah merosot sebanyak separuh, daripada 31 peratus pada 2013. “Trend ini menggariskan keperluan mendesak untuk melibatkan diri secara aktif dan melibatkan belia kita dalam menderma darah,” kata Menteri Negara Kesihatan, Cik Rahayu Mahzam, ketika melancarkan inisiatif tersebut sempena Hari Penderma Darah Sedunia di Ekspo dan Pusat Konvensyen Marina Bay Sands pada 29 Jun. Cik Rahayu, yang juga seorang penderma darah, berkata penglibatan aktif belia hari ini adalah penting dalam memastikan kelestarian bekalan darah masa depan Singapura. Inisiatif yang dipanggil YouthInspired, akan menyaksikan SRC cuba membina hubungan dengan golongan muda melalui acara dan kempen, lapor The Straits Times. Salah satu kempen utama YouthInspired pada 2024 ialah Marathon Derma Darah Belia Asia Pasifik. Apabila ia kali terakhir diadakan pada 2022, pelajar dari 14 universiti di Singapura, Hongkong dan Korea mengambil bahagian dalam inisiatif itu. Dalam acara yang akan datang, lebih banyak negara dan institut pengajian tinggi akan mengambil bahagian, kata Cik Rahayu, yang juga Menteri Negara bagi Perhubungan dan Penerangan. Pengerusi SRC, Encik Tan Kai Hoe, berkata bahawa setiap tahun, penderma darah membentuk kira-kira 1.8 peratus daripada penduduk yang bermastautin di Singapura - yang bermakna sekitar 77,000 penderma menyumbang bagi keperluan pemindahan darah di sini. SRC akan terus melibatkan pelajar sekolah - termasuk mereka yang berumur 15 tahun ke bawah yang belum cukup umur untuk menderma - melalui perjalanan pembelajaran ke bank darah dan aktiviti pendidikan dan kegiatan lain di sekolah dan institut pengajian tinggi, ujarnya. Kumpulan beruniform Belia Palang Merah, melalui Program Penderma Darah Belia, memupuk penyokong derma darah di sekolah rendah dan menengah. SRC juga bekerjasama rapat dengan institusi pengajian tinggi untuk menganjurkan aktiviti jangkauan dan kempen derma darah di kampus. Permintaan darah akan meningkat dengan penduduk Singapura semakin tua, kata Cik Rahayu sambil menyatakan bahawa penduduk berumur 65 tahun ke atas kini merupakan hampir satu perlima daripada penduduk Singapura, berbanding 11.7 peratus daripada sedekad lalu. Kajian Penguasa Sains Kesihatan (HSA) mendedahkan bahawa pesakit berumur 60 tahun ke atas menyumbang 60 peratus daripada penggunaan darah. Apabila seseorang meningkat usia, kemungkinan mereka memerlukan pemindahan darah meningkat disebabkan oleh kerentanan yang lebih tinggi kepada anemia dan menghidap dua atau lebih penyakit. description_translated: A new initiative launched by the Singapore Red Cross (SRC) now aims to involve 500 youth aged 16 to 25 years in the next five years. By 2030, the organization also hopes to increase the pool of youth donors to 25 percent from the current 15 percent. Over the past decade, the percentage of youth donors has declined by half, from 31 percent in 2013. "This trend underlines the urgent need to actively engage and involve our youth in donating blood," said the Minister of State for Health, Ms. Rahayu Mahzam, when launching the initiative in conjunction with World Blood Donor Day at the Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Center on June 29. Ms Rahayu, who is also a blood donor, said the active involvement of today's youth is important in ensuring the sustainability of Singapore's future blood supply. The initiative, called YouthInspired, will see the SRC try to build relationships with young people through events and campaigns, The Straits Times reported. One of YouthInspired's main campaigns in 2024 is the Asia Pacific Youth Blood Donation Marathon. When it was last held in 2022, students from 14 universities in Singapore, Hongkong and Korea participated in the initiative. In future events, more countries and institutes of higher learning will participate, said Ms. Rahayu, who is also the Minister of State for Communications and Information. SRC Chairman, Mr Tan Kai Hoe, said that every year, blood donors make up about 1.8 per cent of Singapore's resident population - which means around 77,000 donors contribute to blood transfusion needs here. SRC will continue to involve school students - including those aged 15 and under who are not old enough to donate - through learning trips to the blood bank and educational activities and other activities at schools and institutes of higher learning, he said. The Red Cross Youth uniformed group, through the Youth Blood Donor Program, fosters blood donation supporters in primary and secondary schools. SRC also works closely with higher education institutions to organize outreach activities and blood donation campaigns on campus. The demand for blood will increase as Singapore's population ages, Ms Rahayu said, noting that people aged 65 and over now make up almost a fifth of Singapore's population, compared to 11.7 per cent a decade ago. A study by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) revealed that patients aged 60 and over account for 60 percent of blood consumption. As a person ages, the likelihood of them needing a blood transfusion increases due to a higher susceptibility to anemia and having two or more diseases. title: Bekalan darah kumpulan O pada ‘tahap kritikal’, penderma diperlu segera
description: Penderma mempunyai darah jenis O+ atau O- yang layak digesa menderma darah sebelum koleksi yang dijangka berkurangan semasa cuti Tahun Baru Cina, dengan bekalan semasa berada pada tahap kritikal. Pada 25 Januari, stok darah jenis O+ dan O- masing-masing disenaraikan sebagai kritikal dan rendah di laman web Palang Merah Singapura (SRC). Bekalan rendah itu disebabkan penggunaan tinggi kedua-dua jenis darah dan derma lebih rendah daripada biasa pada 2024 setakat ini, kata SRC dan Penguasa Sains Kesihatan (HSA) dalam satu kenyataan bersama pada 25 Januari. “Jika stok darah kumpulan O terus berkurangan, pembedahan elektif perlu ditangguhkan dan pemindahan yang menyelamatkan nyawa juga boleh terjejas,” kata kenyataan itu, sambil menambah bahawa stok darah kumpulan O kini boleh bertahan kurang dari enam hari dan bukannya sekurang-kurangnya sembilan hari. Sebagai kumpulan darah universal, darah kumpulan O diperlukan semasa kecemasan apabila kumpulan darah pesakit tidak diketahui. Tambahan pula, hampir separuh daripada semua pesakit di Singapura mempunyai darah kumpulan O dan hanya boleh menerima jenis darah ini. Pengumpulan darah boleh merosot hingga 20 peratus semasa musim perayaan, seperti Tahun Baru Cina yang akan datang, menjadikannya penting untuk bekalan darah kumpulan O dipulihkan ke tahap sihat secepat mungkin, kata kedua-dua pertubuhan itu. SRC dan HSA menggesa mereka yang mempunyai kumpulan darah O+ dan O-, yang mempunyai berat sekurang-kurangnya 45 kg dan berumur antara 16 dan 60 tahun, supaya menderma darah. Kedua-dua pertubuhan menggalak orang ramai menderma sebelum pergi ke negara atau wilayah yang mempunyai risiko jangkitan bawaan serangga, yang mungkin menyebabkan mereka tidak layak menderma darah untuk satu tempoh masa. Penderma baru atau mereka yang telah mengembara dalam tempoh empat bulan lalu boleh menyemak kelayakan mereka di www.hsa.gov.sg/donor_criteria, dan penderma berumur 16 atau 17 tahun mesti mempunyai borang kebenaran ibu bapa yang ditandatangani yang diperoleh daripada laman web HSA. Derma boleh dibuat di bank darah di Outram, Dhoby Ghaut, Woodlands, Westgate Tower dan One Punggol, atau di kutipan darah komuniti SRC. Semua tabung darah akan ditutup pada dua hari pertama Tahun Baru Cina (10 dan 11 Februari). Kumpulan masyarakat dan korporat juga boleh menghubungi SRC di 6220-0183 atau e-mel donate.blood@redcross.sg untuk menganjurkan derma kumpulan. SRC dan HSA menasihatkan penderma supaya berehat secukupnya pada malam sebelum menderma, dan makan ringan bersama banyak cecair pada hari pendermaan. “Setiap derma adalah penting untuk memastikan kami dapat... respons terhadap sebarang kecemasan sivil atau perubatan di Singapura,” kata kenyataan itu.​ Anda ada maklumat mengenai sesuatu berita menarik?E-mel: bhnews@sph.com.sg
description_translated: Donors with blood type O+ or O- are eligible to be urged to donate blood before collections are expected to decrease during the Chinese New Year holidays, with current supplies at critical levels. On 25 January, blood stocks of type O+ and O- were listed as critical and low respectively on the Singapore Red Cross (SRC) website. The low supply is due to high consumption of both blood types and lower-than-normal donations in 2024 so far, the SRC and the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) said in a joint statement on 25 January. "If group O blood stocks continue to decrease, elective surgeries will have to be postponed and life-saving transfusions may also be affected," the statement said, adding that group O blood stocks can now last less than six days instead of at least nine days. As a universal blood group, group O blood is needed in emergencies when the patient's blood group is unknown. Furthermore, almost half of all patients in Singapore have type O blood and can only receive this type of blood. Blood collections can drop by as much as 20 percent during festive seasons, such as the upcoming Chinese New Year, making it important for the group O blood supply to be restored to healthy levels as soon as possible, the two organizations said. The SRC and HSA are urging those with O+ and O- blood groups, who weigh at least 45 kg and are between 16 and 60 years old, to donate blood. Both organizations encourage people to donate before traveling to countries or regions with a risk of insect-borne infections, which may make them ineligible to donate blood for a period of time. New donors or those who have traveled in the past four months can check their eligibility at www.hsa.gov.sg/donor_criteria, and donors aged 16 or 17 must have a signed parental consent form obtained from the HSA website. Donations can be made at blood banks in Outram, Dhoby Ghaut, Woodlands, Westgate Tower and One Punggol, or at the SRC community blood drive. All blood drives will be closed on the first two days of Chinese New Year (February 10 and 11). Community and corporate groups can also contact the SRC at 6220-0183 or email donate.blood@redcross.sg to organize a group donation. The SRC and HSA advise donors to get adequate rest the night before donation, and eat light meals with plenty of fluids on the day of donation. "Every donation is important to ensure that we can... respond to any civil or medical emergency in Singapore," the statement said. Do you have information about an interesting news story? title: Palang Merah Singapura ikrar bekalan bantuan bernilai S$300,000 untuk Gaza
