title: 4,297 Singapore Red Cross potential donor details hacked probably due to weak password
description:
The information of 4,297 potential donors were compromised on May 8 when the Singapore Red Cross's (SRC) website experienced unauthorised access.

Personal details leaked
A statement by the SRC on May 16 reported that the affected part of the website was a section dedicated to recruiting potential blood donors.

Information that was compromised included:


Name

Contact number

Email

Declared blood type

Preferred appointment date and time

Preferred location of donation
The SRC normally uses this information to set up appointments for potential donors at various blood banks and blood mobiles.

The SRC is currently contacting affected individuals.

"Weak administrator password" could be the cause
According to the statement, no other information was affected and the SRC's other databases have not been compromised.

The Health Sciences Authority's (HSA) systems were similarly unaffected by the breach.

The SRC said that they made a police report on the same day after being alerted by their web developer.

Investigations are on-going.

The incident was also reported to the Personal Data Protection Commission and HSA.

The SRC has also engaged external consultants to conduct forensic investigations to determine the factors that allowed the unauthorised access to happen.

Preliminary findings indicate a "weak administrator password" could have led to the unauthorised access.

In the meantime, the SRC website has been disconnected from the internet and replaced with a temporary webpage with links to relevant websites.

Here's the full statement by the Singapore Red Cross:

1. The Singapore Red Cross (SRC) was alerted by our web developer on 8 May that there was an unauthorised access to part of our website (www.redcross.sg) that supports SRCs work in recruiting people interested in donating blood.

2. Through the website, members of the public can indicate their interest to make a blood donation. SRC then manually makes the appointments on their behalf with the various blood banks and blood mobiles based on their preferred dates and times.

3. The following information of 4,297 individuals who had registered their interest on the website was compromised - name, contact number, email, declared blood type, preferred appointment date/ time and preferred location for blood donations. No other information was affected. SRCs other databases have not been compromised. The Health Sciences Authoritys (HSA) systems are similarly unaffected by this incident.

4. Upon being alerted, SRC made a Police report on the same day (8 May). Police investigations are ongoing. We have also reported the incident to the Personal Data Protection Commission and HSA.

5. There were measures in place to guard against unauthorised access of the website. While our investigations to determine the nature of the unauthorised access are ongoing, our preliminary findings show that a weak administrator password could have left the website vulnerable to the unauthorised access. As a precaution, we have disconnected the website from internet access, and replaced it with a temporary webpage with links to relevant websites. The website will only be reinstated when all security checks have been completed.

6. SRC takes this incident seriously. External consultants have been engaged to conduct forensic investigations to determine the exact factors that allowed the unauthorised access to the website. The findings and measures to be taken will be reported to the SRC Council (Board) and together with the advice of our IT advisory panel and consultants, we will take necessary action to strengthen our IT security measures.

7. SRCs Secretary General/CEO Mr Benjamin William said, Our immediate priority is to ensure affected individuals and partners are notified, while working with the relevant parties to restore and strengthen our IT systems, safeguard our data, and mitigate any future risks. SRC has started to contact affected individuals. We apologise to the users of our website whose information may have been affected by this incident.

1. The Singapore Red Cross (SRC) was alerted by our web developer on 8 May that there was an unauthorised access to part of our website (www.redcross.sg) that supports SRCs work in recruiting people interested in donating blood.

3. The following information of 4,297 individuals who had registered their interest on the website was compromised - name, contact number, email, declared blood type, preferred appointment date/ time and preferred location for blood donations. 4. Upon being alerted, SRC made a Police report on the same day (8 May). Police investigations are ongoing. We have also reported the incident to the Personal Data Protection Commission and HSA.

As a precaution, we have disconnected the website from internet access, and replaced it with a temporary webpage with links to relevant websites. The website will only be reinstated when all security checks have been completed.

6. SRC takes this incident seriously. External consultants have been engaged to conduct forensic investigations to determine the exact factors that allowed the unauthorised access to the website. The findings and measures to be taken will be reported to the SRC Council (Board) and together with the advice of our IT advisory panel and consultants, we will take necessary action to strengthen our IT security measures.

7. SRCs Secretary General/CEO Mr Benjamin William said, Our immediate priority is to ensure affected individuals and partners are notified, while working with the relevant parties to restore and strengthen our IT systems, safeguard our data, and mitigate any future risks. SRC has started to contact affected individuals. We apologise to the users of our website whose information may have been affected by this incident.

title: S'pore Red Cross raises about S$2 million in 1 week, first tranche of aid arrives in Ukraine
description:
Monetary donations are encouraged as it provides more flexibility for Red Cross to respond on the ground.

Zhangxin Zheng | March 04, 2022, 12:19 PM

07 Jan 26, 10:00AM - 11 Jan 26, 10:00PM

Kallang Four Star Building

Singapore Red Cross announced on Mar. 4 that the first tranche of aid from their earlier US$100,000 commitment has arrived in Ukraine and is being distributed by the Ukrainian Red Cross Society and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).

Thus far, more than 30,000 people have received humanitarian aid from the Red Cross emergency stockpile: including hygiene and food kits, warming clothing and medicine.

Ukraine Red Cross Rapid Response Units also provide support to fire brigades and State Emergency Services in repairing damage to civilian buildings and infrastructure.

More than 50 lives have been saved during this time, Singapore Red Cross updated.

Ukraine Red Cross has also helped care for people at the border crossing points, evacuate civilians from places where shelling takes place, and distribute essentials to those who need them.

Emergency Response Teams of @RedCrossUkraine
supporting people crossing the border with Slovakia
??providing people with water & food & hygiene stuff;
??setting up a place for mother & child.

Due to the current conflict in #Ukraine, millions of people have left their homes. pic.twitter.com/DMxDKlxBbo

The #UkrainianRedCross has provided about 8,000 people, who shelter in the subway stations during the shelling  with food & basic necessities.
?? Many people have to stay in the subway for the whole night, they need food & water. #Ukraine #SupportUKraine pic.twitter.com/X2H6sXIXPb

A lot of work has been done during this week. Together with our partners, URCS intend to continue in the same spirit and do more to help those who need our help the most. https://t.co/7OhYgzc3O7

The Secretary-General and CEO of the Singapore Red Cross said that the team is working closely with their counterparts to help address the most pressing needs. He added:

"The combination of an active and bloody conflict, extreme cold weather and Covid-19 means that for the people in the conflict regions and those who have been displaced from their homes (already exceeding 1 million), the days ahead will be a struggle for survival. The essential needs continue to increase day by day."

Singapore Red Cross said their fundraising appeal had reached about S$2 million. This includes the Singapore government's contribution of  US$100,000.

It also highlighted that unsolicited in-kind donations for Ukraine remain a challenge for the Red Cross Societies to handle on the ground as there are difficulties in storage, transport and distribution.

Monetary donations are encouraged as cash can be used to purchase items quickly at the nearby unaffected regions, providing flexibility in the Red Cross' response.

title: Ong Ye Kung appeals for O blood donors, especially before travelling for June holidays
description:
Ong said that more donations of O blood were needed.

Tan Min-Wei | June 17, 2023, 04:18 PM

07 Jan 26, 10:00AM - 11 Jan 26, 10:00PM

Kallang Four Star Building

Minister of Health Ong Ye Kung spoke at an event marking World Blood Donor Day on Jun. 17 and appealed for blood donors to come forward, particularly those with O blood, as its stock has been depleting fast due to high demand.

Ong began by thanking those who had donated blood, saying:

"Most blood donors have donated unconditionally, knowing that they are saving lives, but not knowing the names and faces of people they have helped."

He said that in July 2022, during the Covid-19 pandemic, A+ and O+ blood stocks had come close to falling below critical levels, and the Health Sciences Authority and the Red Cross had attempted to get more donors to come forward.

Ong had posted an appeal for donors on social media. 1,700 blood donors came forward within four days of the appeal.

More than 34,000 patients benefited from Singapore's blood donations last year.

Since the transition to DORSCON Green, blood usage is increasing as hospitals caught up on elective surgeries and treatments that had been postponed due to the pandemic. Thus, blood stocks have remained at low to moderate levels since January 2023.

Ong appealed for donors from the O Blood group, as it has been experiencing high demand, and stock has been depleting quickly.

He said that Singapore was in the middle of the travelling season, which often means a disruption in blood donation.

"Once we have been to certain countries, we cannot donate blood for a number of weeks," Ong explained.

Therefore, he appealed to donors and potential donors to "make it a habit to donate blood before you travel", particularly now, or just before the Aug. 9 National Day holidays.

Ong also spoke about the easing of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (vCJD) restrictions for blood donors.

Ong said vCJD, which is a rare and serious degenerative neurological disorder, is sometimes referred to as "mad cow disease" due its link to the consumption of contaminated beef products, although it can also occur spontaneously due to genetic mutations.

Concern around the disease, which can incubate in an infected person for decades, and the inability to reliably detect it, meant that several countries including Singapore had disallowed blood donations from people who had lived in countries such as the United Kingdom, Ireland, and France, during particular periods of time, such as during the late 1980's.

Ong himself was affected by this, as he had lived in the UK during the late 1980s while he was studying as an undergraduate.

But a process called "leucodepletion" allows for the removal of white blood cells, that can potentially transmit the disease, from donated blood; thus far there have been no recorded transmissions of vCJD from blood processed this way.

This allowed countries such as the United States and Australia to ease restrictions, and Singapore will follow suit later in 2023.

This, Ong said, will contribute to a more stable blood supply in Singapore.

If you're considering donating blood, you can take a one-minute eligibility quiz on the Singapore Red Cross website.

You can also find a location to donate blood at this link.

Ong appealed for donors from the O Blood group, as it has been experiencing high demand, and stock has been depleting quickly.

He said that Singapore was in the middle of the travelling season, which often means a disruption in blood donation.

"Once we have been to certain countries, we cannot donate blood for a number of weeks," Ong explained.

Therefore, he appealed to donors and potential donors to "make it a habit to donate blood before you travel", particularly now, or just before the Aug. 9 National Day holidays.

Ong also spoke about the easing of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (vCJD) restrictions for blood donors.

Ong said vCJD, which is a rare and serious degenerative neurological disorder, is sometimes referred to as "mad cow disease" due its link to the consumption of contaminated beef products, although it can also occur spontaneously due to genetic mutations.

Concern around the disease, which can incubate in an infected person for decades, and the inability to reliably detect it, meant that several countries including Singapore had disallowed blood donations from people who had lived in countries such as the United Kingdom, Ireland, and France, during particular periods of time, such as during the late 1980's.

Ong himself was affected by this, as he had lived in the UK during the late 1980s while he was studying as an undergraduate.

But a process called "leucodepletion" allows for the removal of white blood cells, that can potentially transmit the disease, from donated blood; thus far there have been no recorded transmissions of vCJD from blood processed this way.

This allowed countries such as the United States and Australia to ease restrictions, and Singapore will follow suit later in 2023.

This, Ong said, will contribute to a more stable blood supply in Singapore.

If you're considering donating blood, you can take a one-minute eligibility quiz on the Singapore Red Cross website.

title: S'pore govt to contribute S$129,200 to Sri Lanka cyclone fundraising efforts by S'pore Red Cross
description:
The Singapore government has pledged US$100,000 (S$129,200) as "seed money" to help the Singapore Red Cross's (SRC) fundraising efforts for Sri Lankan communities affected by Cyclone Ditwah.

In a press release from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Dec. 12, it said that the contribution by the Singapore government will supplement the SRCs pledge of S$50,000 to support the immediate needs of affected communities in Sri Lanka.

President Tharman Shanmugaratnam and Foreign Affairs Minister Vivian Balakrishnan have written to Sri Lanka's President Anura Kumara Dissanayake and Minister of Foreign Affairs Vijitha Herath to convey their condolences over the destruction caused by the cyclone and the tragic loss of life.

According to the World Health Organization, Ditwah has displaced over 233,000 people, with 410 confirmed deaths and 336 missing.

"Access to clean water remains a critical concern. Food insecurity is rising as farmland and supply chains face severe disruption.

The health system is under mounting pressure, with increased risks of water-related illnesses and reduced access to essential services."

The Singapore Red Cross (SRC) has launched a public fundraising appeal in response to the humanitarian crisis in Ukraine.

The public fundraiser is in addition to the US$100,000 (S$135,345) that the humanitarian organisation has pledged to support the ongoing humanitarian operations mounted by the Ukrainian Red Cross Society and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

Funds raised will go towards providing relief supplies, including hygiene kits, family kits, and household kits for those displaced by the conflict.

The public fundraiser will run from now till May 31.

title: S'pore blood bank low again this Covid-19 season, blood donors needed
description:
Please donate if you can.

Syahindah Ishak | June 01, 2020, 01:25 PM

07 Jan 26, 10:00AM - 11 Jan 26, 10:00PM

Kallang Four Star Building

Stocks for a number of blood types in Singapore are running low as of May 29, according to Singapore Red Cross (SRC)'s website.

Blood types A+, AB+ and AB- are currently at 'critical' levels, which means that donors are urged to donate within the same day as you read the notice.

Meanwhile, blood types B+ and O+ are at 'low' levels.

Donors are urged to donate these blood types within the week.

According to The Straits Times, Singapore's blood stocks have dropped by a third during the Covid-19 pandemic.

The decline in the number of blood donations was particularly sharp during the first week of circuit breaker.

A spokesman for SRC told ST:

"We recognise that many donors will avoid going out unnecessarily. Some donors may not be aware that blood donation remains an essential service and that our blood banks are still open."

SRC also said that it has been unable to hold mobile drives as often as before.

Previously, the organisation used to conduct at least 10 mobile blood drives weekly.

But now, only four drives are held every week.

Although SRC has not had to turn away a patient in need of blood transfusion, it said that more needs to be done in Singapore to ensure a sufficient and sustainable supply of safe blood.

The Health Sciences Authority (HSA), which manages Singapore's blood banks, has previously stated that the risk of contracting Covid-19 while donating blood is assessed to be low.

SRC also wrote on its website that precautions are put in place to ensure safe distancing during the blood drives.

title: Soiled underwear and nuggets crawling with maggots: Trashy donations hamper charities' work
description: By Yuen Sin The Straits Times Jan 22, 2017 Mouldy cakes, soiled underwear and nuggets crawling with maggots - these are not items in trash bins, but in-kind donations to thrift shops or charities. They might be extreme cases, but charities interviewed by The Sunday Times said that up to 40 per cent of the items donated by the public end up being discarded regularly because they turn out to be unsuitable for the charities' use. Time and effort is needed to collect and sift through them. At The Food Bank Singapore (FBSG) - which collects donations of non-perishable food items like canned food and rice and distributes them to social service organisations - volunteers and staff spend about 1,700 man-hours sorting through an average of 240 tonnes of food donated by the public every year. About 10 to 20 per cent of the items are discarded because they do not fit the charity's requirements, said Ms Margarita Seah, an FBSG management associate. Bizarre examples of donations collected last year include syrup that expired in 1998. The charity also often finds used coffee cups and half-eaten food in donation boxes at some collection points - which may contaminate other donations. "It's quite shocking to see that people are leaving such items behind, as our signs clearly state that we collect only non-perishable items," said Ms Seah. The signs at collection points list examples of acceptable items, such as unopened snacks or canned food with at least four weeks of shelf life, as well as items not accepted, such as unlabelled food products. Ms Seah said that FBSG is looking at redesigning the signs with graphics to make the guidelines more obvious. It now conducts talks in schools and offices to spread awareness before it holds food drives, during which donated items are collected from the public. The Singapore Red Cross also has had its share of oddities among the unsuitable items that have been given to it. Mr Dennis Yeo, its head of fund-raising, said that last year alone, the charity received items like a beer keg, five samurai swords and even a knuckleduster. comment_text: More than 3,000 people turn up to give blood after Red Cross appeal for A+, O+ donors  SINGAPORE - An appeal to donate blood as supplies run low has drawn an overwhelming response, with more than 3,300 people coming forward over the past week.  This represents a 43 per cent increase from a typical week's collection, said the Singapore Red Cross (SRC), which is the Republic's national blood donor recruiter.  "We hope that this momentum will continue next week to bring our blood stocks up to healthy levels," said the humanitarian organisation.  Located at the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) building in Outram Road, the Bloodbank@HSA - one of four blood banks across the island - was packed when The Straits Times visited on Friday (July 15).  Among the donors there was Mr Goh Chee Wee, who said it was his first time donating since 1996.  Work and other commitments, which often require him to travel, left little time for him to donate blood in the years since then, said the 43-year-old army regular.  He was there with about 40 others from his unit, which had made an informal request for servicemen to volunteer to donate blood that day.  Mr Goh, whose blood type is A+, said he was inspired by recent social media posts put out by Health Minister Ong Ye Kung, who shared SRC's call for blood donors to come forward.  He added that as a sergeant major, he felt it was important to lead by example.  Full-time national serviceman Eldridge Surianto was a first-time blood donor.  The 19-year-old, who has O+ blood, said his decision to donate blood was a personal one - he has relatives who required blood transfusions because of cancer treatments.  "I was quite nervous at first," he said, noting that he had heard that giving blood could cause dizziness.  "But after this experience, I don't think it's that scary," said Mr Surianto, adding that he would consider doing it again in future.  On July 8, SRC had called for more blood donors, said a spokesman, as there was less than nine days' worth of A+ and O+ blood then.  1.0.2 | Source code | Contribute || I never been to any blood donation, isit painful? :O

title: Donated Blood Today Hi,  [Gallery of Pics] (http://imgur.com/a/bXU2M)  Donated Blood today, wanted to share how it went.  I donated at  Bloodbank @ Health Sciences Authority (HSA)  Its close to Outram Park MRT Station, walking distance.  List of places to donate  You can choose to donate  whole blood (regular donation) OR  platelets and plasma (apheresis)  Apheresis is recommended for non-first timers in my opinion.  Apheresis requires large veins that will not collapse for the hour long procedure.  I tried once but it collapsed halfway. They told me to try again in 2 years.  Highly recommended to make an appointment before going down  -Its pretty fast, can just make a phone call or use your SingPass  -You get placed in a priority line, which speed things up a bit depending on the crowd that day.  Once inside, this is the rough flow of things.  Fill up Questionnaire, hand it in.  Wait to be called for the doctor to take your blood pressure, temperature etc.  Next station, they prick a finger to test your haemoglobin levels to see whether you meet the minimum.  Enter the area with the chairs, and the staff will get you prepared for the procedure, pretty friendly, though it seems that they use similar lines to make donors feel at ease, better than nothing though.  Vein check, inject anaesthesia, etc, the actual process itself.  Wait for blood to be drawn out, 450 mls. My bag took 3:30 for it to be filled.  The actual process itself is very much shorter than the form-filling and waiting. Pretty fast, total time is close to half hour.  During the process itself the staff will hand you a food voucher, and some iron tablets to replenish your iron supply.  If you visit in between 11.30 and 1.30pm  It is considered lunchtime and a full meal will be redeemed using the voucher. Menu for that day  Other times would just be a snack.  I also received a pretty thick notebook. Hardcover and bound pretty nicely. Came in a plastic cover shaped like a blood bag and a sticker/decal that mimicked a blood bag label.  On top of that there was also an extra gift because of donating during my birthday month. It was an handheld electric fan with a pretty cute and cool function, where it flashed "Happy Birthday". Good for a chuckle.  More information / Everything else you need to know can be found here:  HSA Site  [Gallery of Pics] (http://imgur.com/a/bXU2M)

comment_text: I highly encourage Singaporeans to donate blood if you can, because the donor rate in Singapore is actually pretty low. Consider it helping others -- like a one-off volunteering -- and it's one of the most effortless things to do: you just lie there in an air-conditioned room, and you get free food! And you make the world a better place.  But that being said, the HSA has rather ridiculously stringent rules for donors. For example, people with multiple sex partners cannot donate for the remainder of their lives. And there is a lifetime ban for anyone who had gay sex. This is much stricter than other countries like the UK or Australia. Be aware of these rules before turning up at a donation centre. || One of my friend volunteered the blood drive and all those things. title: Blood donation had almost zero turn up from our company Recently, my company changed a policy whereby we need to apply for half day leave (from our original leave pool) if we want to donate blood. This was because the company would give an additional half day leave for each blood donation drive you went for.  This makes me think if we are really short of blood because the government keeps calling for us to donate blood, but the company removing leave for blood donation sends the opposite signal.

comment_text: The least the government should do is offer a one day MC or some form of time chit. And I’m saying this as a somewhat regular donor (~2 per year). JE/Douby open till 8pm, and can be quite crowded from 6 onwards. I have to either find time during lunch crowd or after work during weekdays.  Max you can donate blood is 4 times a year. Guess is somewhat more abusable for apheresis donation (every 4 weeks) but a time chit is the least they can do tbh. || How about some statistics on the number of blood donors from the new citizens and PRs? || Edit to add: https://giveblood.sg for more details. Group of 10 or more can charter bus. Wah swee  Donating blood takes at most 1.5 hours of your time (the longest one is plasma apheresis and they basically centrifuge your blood in cycles to separate the plasma, the more you donate the more cycles it takes).  Whole blood is in and out and you even get free snacks and milo + the knowledge that each donation saves 3 lives, and can be made into over 18 treatments for over 50 life threatening conditions.  One of the biggest blood product use cases is for cancer treatment (and of course trauma/surgery). Especially blood plasma. Immunotherapy as well for people with chronic autoimmune/immune diseases.  One day you, or someone you love could need blood products and you'd want to make sure there're enough compatible blood donations/medications made when that time comes!  Especially valuable are O negative donations as this is the universal red cell donor (O positive works for mostly everyone except pregnant women and Rhesus negative (Rh) people). O-ve is most commonly found in caucasians and indians but of course anyone can have it!  O+ follows closely behind, commonly considered the universal red cell donor as most people will receive it in an emergency transfusion if their blood type hasn't been tested yet + for the O+ people who cannot receive A, AB, B etc. Type O+ is the most common blood type, so chances are you or your family has O+ and you would like to have O+ in stock if something happens.  If you have blood type AB, you are a universal plasma donor, anyone who needs plasma can receive your donation. AB is one of the rarer types so if you have AB please consider donating plasma if you're eligible! (In Singapore, above 50kg)  Donating plasma is really simple, just chill in the chair while your blood is separated into plasma et al. They take the plasma, leaving your red cells, and then put saline back into you so your total blood volume is the same as before. It also means you have a lower risk of feeling faint!  I highly highly encourage everyone to donate when and where possible. We need everyone to roll up their sleeves and have skin in the game. Some people won't be able to donate but consider registering for the bone marrow donor registry! As a healthcare student this is something incredibly dear to my heart and it is one of the ways everyone can save lives.  On a side note, everyone should also sign up for those CC first aid/CPR AED courses/awareness days. In a joint statement on Feb 4, the Singapore Red Cross (SRC) and Health Sciences Authority (HSA) said blood stocks typically drop by 20 per cent during festive periods and long weekends.  “Therefore, there is a possibility of a decline in group O blood stock, particularly in the first two weeks following Lunar New Year, if the current momentum is not sustained,” they said.  They added that blood has a short shelf life of six weeks for red cells and only seven days for platelets.  HSA chief executive Mimi Choong May Ling called on the public to continue donating blood before and after Chinese New Year to bolster the nation’s blood reserves.  “Your regular donation is crucial to ensure that we always have at least a nine-day stockpile to respond to any civil or medical emergencies in Singapore,” she said.  In their statement, HSA and SRC thanked the 5,300 donors who responded to the Jan 25 appeal. The appeal was sparked by critically low levels of stocks for the O+ and O- blood types. The process first begins with a 4 page questionnaire which you have to fill in, asking you questions regarding your medical history, unusual sexual practices as well as travel history in the past 12 months.  Next you'll go into a doctor's room and the doctor will go through the questionnaire with you again to make sure you're not just anyhow ticking the responses. There you'll also take the blood pressure and temperature and measure your height and weight to ensure that you're suitable to donate blood.  Once you pass all these tests, you'll then go to a small station where they'll prick your finger to do a blood sugar and blood iron test. After a few minutes for the anaesthesia to set in, they will pluck this huge ass needle into your vein and the blood donation process officially begins. comment_text: sheila.mitu and 2 others Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Center sheila.mitu Edited ✨ Pop Toy Show x Red Cross Experience ✨ What an incredible weekend at @poptoyshowsg organized by @popmartsg ! We had the chance to explore four amazing booths by @sgredcross , and the experience was both meaningful and fun. At Wings of Art by @peace.of.art.sg , we created our very own Winged Barbie Doll 🎨✨ The booth was beautifully put together, and what made it extra memorable was having @jianyang1979 , the biggest Barbie collector in the world, help tie our Barbie’s hair 🎀 Proceeds from this workshop go towards the Singapore Red Cross Young Hearts Programme, supporting underprivileged children. Next, we visited the Snoopy x @sgredcrossshop Shop 🐾. We had so much fun checking out the exclusive Peanuts items and snapping pictures with Snoopy at the adorable photo spot! Then, we stopped by the SCDF x Operation Lionheart booth 🚒💪. This booth featured exclusive figurines honoring the heroes who were deployed to Türkiye during the Turkey-Syria Earthquake. We also learned about the myResponder programme and how SCDF works within our community. We also visited the YouthInspire x Blood Donor Programme 🩸 to learn how youth can contribute to keeping our nation’s blood supply strong. Plus, we checked out their cute @heybloodbuddy Blood Buddy merch! Aside from the Red Cross booths, I took some time to check out the Pop Toy Show booths, where they showcased a variety of fun, collectible toys and art.  it’s always exciting to see how these creative communities come together to celebrate pop culture and art. The day ended with the stunning Pop Mart drone show lighting up the sky 🌟 A beautiful, high-tech finale to an amazing event! I’m so grateful to @sgredcross for inviting us and for putting together such an inspiring event that brings awareness to important causes. The Secondary 2 student at @cedargirlssecondary quickly contacted her schoolmate Gracias Prasetyo and both of them rushed to the flat, where they found an elderly man unconscious on the bed. Gracias, who is in Secondary 4, applied CPR on the man while Elina ran down to find an automated external defibrillator (AED). 2 other responders also arrived at the flat to provide assistance. comment_text: sgredcross.academy Follow sgredcross.academy ⭐ At the 10th Singapore Humanitarian Conference, organised by the Singapore Red Cross under the theme “Power of You: Force for Humanity”, we explored how individuals and communities can adapt and thrive in a warming world ⭐ Our session on “Heat Resilience - Harnessing Your Power to Adapt and Thrive”, hosted by Durga Naidu, Head of Department, Centre for Psychosocial Support, Singapore Red Cross Academy (SRCA), highlighted the urgent connection between heat, health, and resilience - and the crucial role we all play in strengthening our collective response to climate challenges 💡 Key insights from our speakers: 👉 Assoc Prof Jason Lee (Director, Heat Resilience & Performance Centre), emphasised that while we can’t cool the environment overnight, we can build physiological resilience - from strategies to improve heat tolerance to innovative solutions that help our bodies cope better. 👉 Assoc Prof Lee Cheng (Clinical Director, Institute of Mental Health), reminded us that heat strain extends beyond the physical, impacting mental health as well. For those with lower heat resilience, psychological challenges can be amplified - making empathy and awareness more important than ever. This dialogue underscored the need for integrated solutions that protect both body and mind, empowering us to make better decisions during heat crises and safeguard vulnerable communities worldwide We thank Ms Durga for skillfully hosting the session, and our distinguished speakers and participants for driving meaningful conversations that will shape a more inclusive, resilient, and compassionate humanitarian future -- Want to learn more? Find out about our heat resilience courses @ https://redcross.sg/get-trained/heat-resilience-courses.html Start the conversation. 15

comment_text: bdosg Follow bdosg A Heartfelt Afternoon at the Oceanarium 🌊❤️ BDO Deals Advisory Team recently spent a joyful outing bonding with our seniors at the Singapore Oceanarium, Sentosa a day filled with laughter, meaningful conversations, and unforgettable moments. 🐠✨ Thanks to the incredible support from the Singapore Red Cross under the ElderAid Programme, the activity reminded us of the power of compassion and the importance of community. comment_text: zaobaosg Follow zaobaosg 爱女出国留学毕业后被诊断患上渐冻症，一年间全身瘫痪，父母不舍女儿在医院“躺”一辈子，把房间打造成加护病房（ICU），全天24小时贴身照顾，为女儿续写多八年的人生。 曾慧仪（32岁）自高中时期就到加拿大留学，大学毕业后又进修了一年，取得专业文凭，并留在加拿大成为了一名社工。在2014年被诊断患上肌萎缩性脊髓侧索硬化症（Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis，俗称“渐冻人”），已于3月16日过世。 2014年，当时24岁的曾慧仪感觉身体不适，随后演变成吞咽困难、声音虚弱，肌肉无力，一年内暴瘦15公斤，随后证实是渐冻症。母亲郭璐恩（62岁，家庭主妇）透露，全家人得知女儿患病后都感到十分震惊和难过，她当时特地飞去加拿大陪了女儿三个月，回新后也咨询了医生，但仍无法改变现实。“该病症是一种不治之症。不过女儿乐观要强，从没和我们抱怨过，之后积极配合治疗，我们也竭尽所能地照顾她。” 回国后，由于父母不想让女儿在医院“躺”一辈子，因此选择把她接回家，贴身照顾。“女儿起初还能独立生活，但不久后就无法自主呼吸和吃饭，也丧失了表达能力，只能靠呼吸机和插管进食，瘫痪在床。” 为了照顾好女儿，家人购买了呼吸机、氧气机、咳痰机和病床等辅助仪器，把房间打造成如同加护病房，让女儿睡在身边，24小时贴身照顾她的饮食起居。 “虽然女儿失去了活动能力，但思想智力如常，我们经常在她情况好的时候带她去看电影、用餐和散步，但出门时必须带上好几个辅助仪器，下床时也得借助升降机（hoist，图2）和三人协助才能完成。” 父母的不离不弃，让曾慧仪得到了最好的照顾，不过随着时间的推移，她的健康每况愈下，3月16日在家中去世。 郭璐恩表示，希望通过分享女儿的经历，提高渐冻症意识，也呼吁病患不要因患病而失去希望，只要通过合理的辅助，调整心态，还是可以延长病患的寿命。她也提醒，患者起初患病后会感到迷茫和担忧，他们可去运动神经元疾病协会的网站进行了解和咨询。📸：受访者提供、蔡振鸿 #zaobaosg #新加坡 #渐冻人 #肌肉萎缩 #安息 #communitystories #sgnews #singapore #amyotrophiclateralsclerosis #rip See translation koo_ksh 🙌👏 susan_6483 伟大的父母亲 See translation cailianyee ❤️ jo.ling.lee 南无阿弥陀佛🙏 See translation chowchuichoo 伟大的父母。👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏 1 like See translation ng_y_t_ angela.clk3 ❤️ vincentkstan 好动人肺腑至深，父母亲的伟大，女儿的坚强让人感到致敬。愿佛祖菩萨保佑平安健康快乐。 See translation wengkwokchee 父母亲的爱，RIP !...take care! comment_text_translated: zaobaosg Follow zaobaosg After her beloved daughter graduated from studying abroad, she was diagnosed with ALS and became paralyzed for a year. Her parents did not want their daughter to "lay" in the hospital for the rest of her life. They turned the room into an intensive care unit (ICU) and took personal care of her 24 hours a day to write another eight years of her daughter's life. Zeng Huiyi (32 years old) has been studying in Canada since high school. After graduating from university, she studied for another year, obtained a professional diploma, and stayed in Canada to become a social worker. He was diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in 2014 and passed away on March 16. In 2014, Zeng Huiyi, who was 24 years old at the time, felt unwell, which later evolved into difficulty swallowing, weak voice, and muscle weakness. She lost 15 kilograms within a year, and was later confirmed to have ALS. Mother Guo Luen (62 years old, housewife) revealed that the whole family was shocked and sad when they learned that their daughter was sick. She flew to Canada to stay with her daughter for three months. After returning to Singapore, she also consulted a doctor, but she still could not change the reality. "The disease is an incurable disease. However, my daughter is more optimistic and has never complained to us. After that, she actively cooperated with the treatment and we did our best to take care of her." After returning to China, because the parents did not want their daughter to "lay" in the hospital for a lifetime, they chose to take her home and take care of her personally. "My daughter was able to live independently at first, but soon after she lost her ability to breathe and eat on her own, and also lost her ability to express herself. She could only rely on a ventilator and intubation for feeding, and was paralyzed in bed." In order to take good care of their daughter, the family purchased auxiliary equipment such as a ventilator, oxygen machine, sputum machine, and hospital bed, and made the room like an intensive care unit, allowing her daughter to sleep next to her and take care of her daily life 24 hours a day. "Although my daughter has lost her ability to move, her thinking and intelligence are as normal. We often take her to movies, meals and walks when she is in good condition. However, she has to bring several assistive devices when she goes out. She also has to use a hoist (picture 2) and three people to assist when she gets out of bed." Her parents' perseverance allowed Zeng Huiyi to receive the best care. However, as time went by, her health deteriorated and she died at home on March 16. Guo Luen said that she hopes to raise awareness of ALS by sharing her daughter’s experience, and also calls on patients not to lose hope due to the disease. As long as they receive reasonable assistance and adjust their mentality, the life span of patients can still be extended. She also reminded that patients may feel confused and worried at first after getting sick, and they can go to the Motor Neurone Disease Association's website for information and consultation. 📸: Provided by the interviewee, Cai Zhenhong #zaobaosg # Singapore #ALS #ALS Great parents. 👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏 1 like See translation ng_y_t_ angela.clk3 ❤️ vincentkstan is so touching, the greatness of the parents and the strength of the daughter make people feel honored. After that, she actively cooperated with the treatment and we did our best to take care of her." After returning to China, because the parents did not want their daughter to "lay" in the hospital for a lifetime, they chose to take her home and take care of her personally. "My daughter was able to live independently at first, but soon after she lost her ability to breathe and eat on her own, and also lost her ability to express herself. She could only rely on a ventilator and intubation for feeding, and was paralyzed in bed." In order to take good care of their daughter, the family purchased auxiliary equipment such as a ventilator, oxygen machine, sputum machine, and hospital bed, and made the room like an intensive care unit, allowing her daughter to sleep next to her and take care of her daily life 24 hours a day. "Although my daughter has lost her ability to move, her thinking and intelligence are as normal. We often take her to movies, meals and walks when she is in good condition. However, she has to bring several assistive devices when she goes out. She also has to use a hoist (picture 2) and three people to assist when she gets out of bed." Her parents' perseverance allowed Zeng Huiyi to receive the best care. However, as time went by, her health deteriorated and she died at home on March 16. Guo Luen said that she hopes to raise awareness of ALS by sharing her daughter’s experience, and also calls on patients not to lose hope due to the disease. As long as they receive reasonable assistance and adjust their mentality, the life span of patients can still be extended. She also reminded that patients may feel confused and worried at first after getting sick, and they can go to the Motor Neurone Disease Association's website for information and consultation. 📸: Provided by the interviewee, Cai Zhenhong #zaobaosg # Singapore #ALS #ALS Great parents. 👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏👏 1 like See translation ng_y_t_ angela.clk3 ❤️ vincentkstan is so touching, the greatness of the parents and the strength of the daughter make people feel honored. comment_text: zaobaosg Follow zaobaosg 一班好友四年前筹办义走，为新加坡红十字会残疾人士之家的居民筹款。这一群善心人以“蓝星”（BlueStar）为组织命名和开展活动，犹如夜晚星星一般，闪烁光芒，关怀照耀社会上的弱势群体。 从那时候起，他们年复一年为残疾人士之家筹款。蓝星慈善义走的推手刘启兴（55岁，企业家）2018年召集一组求学时参加学生警察队认识的朋友，包括他们的一位导师，提议举办一场慈善活动。他受访时说，当时感觉到事业有成，生活已踏入舒适的阶段，应该做一些回馈社会的事。 去年由于受到冠病疫情的影响，他们首次挑战线上活动，取得不错的成绩，筹募近40万元善款。今年，他们希望筹集至少35万元。部分善款将用来成立看护者关怀与协助基金，为看护者提供一些财务资助。今年的活动除了保留虚拟形式，实体节目也会照办。实体义走在现阶段开放给50人参加，骑脚车活动则不超过80人。 2021年蓝星慈善活动详情如下： 10月30日至12月4日 ■ 参加线上义走（28公里）或骑车（128公里），按自己的时间与路线完成挑战 10月30日 ■ 五公里义走，从残疾人士之家开始 12月4日 ■ 70公里骑脚车，从胡姬乡村俱乐部开始 参加义走的捐款为28元，骑车活动为68元（包括骑车衬衫）。 欲知更多关于蓝星慈善活动与报名详情请点击 @zaobaosg 首页的Link in Bio。📸：新加坡红十字会 #zaobaosg #sgnews #bluestar #charity #蓝星 #慈善 #新加坡红十字协会 #Singapore #Redcross #爱心电灯 #筹款 See translation qiqiqiqiqixiaodi 自诩？ 128
comment_text_translated: zaobaosg Follow zaobaosg A group of friends organized a charity walk four years ago to raise funds for the residents of the Singapore Red Cross Home for the Disabled. This group of kind-hearted people named the organization and carried out activities under the name "Blue Star". They are like stars at night, shining brightly and caring for the disadvantaged groups in society. Since then they have been raising money for a home for the disabled year after year. In 2018, the promoter of the Blue Star Charity Walk, Liu Qixing (55 years old, entrepreneur), gathered a group of friends he met when he was a student in the student police force, including one of their mentors, and proposed to hold a charity event. When interviewed, he said that at that time he felt that his career was successful and his life had entered a comfortable stage, so he should do something to give back to the society. Last year, due to the impact of the COVID-19 epidemic, they challenged online activities for the first time and achieved good results, raising nearly 400,000 yuan in donations. This year, they hope to raise at least $350,000. Part of the donations will be used to establish a caregiver care and assistance fund to provide some financial assistance to caregivers. In addition to retaining the virtual format of this year’s event, physical programming will also follow suit. The physical walk is currently open to 50 people, while the cycling event is open to no more than 80 people. Details of the 2021 Blue Star Charity Event are as follows: October 30 to December 4 ■ Participate in an online charity walk (28 kilometers) or bike ride (128 kilometers) and complete the challenge in your own time and route. October 30 ■ Five-kilometer charity walk, starting from the Home for the Disabled December 4 ■ 70-kilometer bicycle ride, starting from Orchid Country Club The donation for participating in the charity walk is NT$28, and the donation for the cycling event is NT$68 (including cycling shirt). For more information about Blue Star charity activities and registration details, please click on the Link in Bio on the homepage of @zaobaosg. 📸：Singapore Red Cross #zaobaosg #sgnews #bluestar #charity #蓝星 #Charity #Singapore Red Cross Society #Singapore #Redcross #爱灯 #fundraising See translation qiqiqiqiqixiaodi boasting? 128

For collecting 541 blood bags during their #blooddonation drives on campus during the academic year 2022 and 2023, Red Cross Youth NTU Chapter has been honoured with the Blood Mobile Organisers Award (Gold) from Singapore Red Cross . comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow Presenting our Volunteer Leaders from the Blood Donor Programme — Jacques, Vidya, Neha, Vijay, Jamal, Gnanasekaran, Cherry, Suyog Jain, Marilou and Gowtham. They are among our pioneer batch of 23 volunteer leaders from various SRC services who completed our Volunteer Leadership Programme in January. SRC was appointed as Singapore's National Blood Donor Recruiter in 2001. Together with the Health Sciences Authority's (HSA) Blood Services Group, we aim to collect sufficient safe blood for the national transfusion needs. We focus on blood donor recruitment, retention and recognition, advocacy and education, and organising mobile blood drives in the community. As the first group of BDP Volunteer Leaders, they have a big part to play in ensuring that blood stocks remain at a healthy level. Through their passion, volunteering spirit, commitment and leadership, we hope to see more stepping up not only to volunteer but also to donate blood. Like the volunteer leaders, you can make a difference in our community by embarking on your volunteering journey with SRC! Find out more at volunteer.redcross.sg #PassionPeople #VolunteerwithSRC

comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow Centre of Excellence for Pandemic Preparedness | Regional Platform for Southeast Asian National Societies Palang Merah Indonesia (PMI) | Friends of CoEPP Meet Eka and Nurrista from PMI, as part of our Friends of CoEPP Campaign. Let’s hear from them as they share the work of PMI in strengthening pandemic preparedness in communities through its Community-Based Surveillance (CBS) programme and integrating it into the nationwide SatuSBM digital platform. By recognising that pandemics begin in communities and must be addressed at their root, PMI links community vigilance with national surveillance, ensuring faster detection and response. At its heart, CBS shows that strong communities, built on trust and education, are the strongest defence against pandemics. Volunteers, families, and local leaders work together to share information, change behaviours, and protect lives - proving that preparedness is not only about systems, but about people. comment_text: Toa Payoh Central Community Club Follow For over 20 years, Karunanithi s/o Letchumanan, PBM has exemplified service and dedication both locally and internationally. Starting with a group of friends, he embarked on his first mission to Indonesia during the regional haze crisis, distributing masks to vulnerable communities. This initial act of kindness marked the beginning of a lasting involvement with the Singapore Red Cross. Over the years, Karunanithi s/o Letchumanan, PBM has been on the frontlines of numerous humanitarian missions, responding to crises with compassion and resolve. Some of his notable deployments include: Barangay Dulag, Philippines – He participated in rebuilding projects, helping communities recover after natural disasters. Sri Lanka Floods – Following devastating floods, he joined assessment and relief distribution efforts, providing essentials to affected families. Palu Earthquake, Indonesia – In the aftermath of this tragic earthquake, he contributed to relief efforts, supporting survivors through difficult times. Ukraine Crisis – Most recently, he was deployed to the border regions of four countries, assisting those fleeing the conflict, ensuring they had access to essential resources and support. With a supportive employer who understands the importance of his work, Karunanithi s/o Letchumanan, PBM is often able to respond to these emergencies on short notice, exemplifying selflessness in each mission. In addition to his global work, Karunanithi s/o Letchumanan, PBM has been deeply rooted in his local community in Toa Payoh Central. His involvement with us the began in 1994 under the leadership of Mr. Dhanabalan and continued under Mr. Davinder Singh. In 2001, he established the Toa Payoh Central Indian Community (IAEC) in Toa Payoh Central, working alongside a dedicated team of volunteers. Under his leadership, the IAEC has organized a wide variety of activities that enrich the lives of residents. From karaoke, dance, and badminton sessions to unique activities like Bollyrobics, Karunanithi s/o Letchumanan, PBM has fostered a sense of community and belonging. Residents have enjoyed outings to Bird Paradise, Marina Barrage for kite flying, and Bukit Timah Hill for the Treetop Walk. Annually, he led his team in engaging our Indian residents through organizing Deepavali and Pongal yearly. "May the festival bring light, happiness, and harmony to all." As we celebrate this season, Karunanithi s/o Letchumanan, PBM extends his warmest wishes to all residents for a joyous and prosperous Deepavali. If you are passionate about giving back and would like to be part of this impactful work, the IAEC always welcomes more volunteers to join their cause. comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow This #InternationalWomensDay, we're highlighting just a few of the women whose work at the Singapore Red Cross makes an impact in unique and powerful ways. As Head of the Centre for Psychosocial Support at Singapore Red Cross Academy , Durga Naidu leads a team of practitioners, psychologists, counsellors, trainers, and healthcare professionals. Her work helps to strengthen mental health resilience in communities by empowering people with psychosocial support skills, and advocates for mental well-being to be considered a critical part of humanitarian work. She shares, "Every time I see a first responder confidently applying psychological first aid, a community leader fostering mental wellness, or a corporate team prioritising emotional resilience, I am reminded that our work is not just about knowledge, it’s about building a culture of care, empathy, and strength that lasts beyond any single crisis." #PassionPeople #sgredcross 1 comment

comment_text: 2Quilters is with Aimee Lim and Yvette Lim at HomeTeamNS Bedok Reservoir · Follow Singapore Last Monday, we were presented with the Friend of SRC Award by the Singapore Red Cross at their annual Awards Ceremony at the HomeTeamNS Bedok Reservoir Clubhouse. It was a fun afternoon for us catching up with some familiar faces and meeting the Guest of Honour and SRC Patron, President Tharman Shanmugaratnam We are very happy to support SRC and their humanitarian mission, and we thank the SRC team for their kind gesture of recognition. comment_text: SRC Toastmasters Follow SRC Toastmasters Chinese New Year “Lo Hei” Chapter Meeting – A Night of Festivity and Fellowship! Despite the rainy evening and heavy traffic, members and guests of SRC Toastmasters turned up in full festive spirit for our Chinese New Year–themed Chapter Meeting at Lounge 1883 on 25 February 2026. The weather may have been gloomy, but the atmosphere inside was warm, vibrant, and filled with laughter! We began the evening with a wonderful dinner and during the break we had an energetic “Lo Hei” session, tossing to greater heights of prosperity, success, and collective excellence for the year ahead. HUAT AH! We were honoured to have our Area M1 Director, Valerie Chow, join us. She gamely took on the role of Toastmaster of the Day, steering the meeting with poise and professionalism. The Table Topics segment, led by our creative Table Topics Master Napoleon Koh, brought plenty of spontaneous wit and laughter and heartfelt sharing from our toastmasters on topics related to the festive period! Congratulations to Anne Lee, who once again impressed everyone and clinched the Best Table Topic Speaker ribbon! Kudos for staying "true" to herself! In the prepared speech segment, Jerry Lee delivered a reflective speech, thoughtfully evaluated by our guest Toastmaster Joseph Lim, whose insightful and encouraging evaluation added great value to the learning experience. Our "Professor" Raphael Lee also gave us valuable pointers in his prepared speech on how to overcome the "Mind Blank" effect when we go on stage. Thank you to everyone who braved the rain to celebrate, connect, and grow together. Here’s to a prosperous and successful year ahead for SRC Toastmasters! #SRCToastmasters #ChineseNewYear #LoHei #SharedLearning #MutualSupport #CollectiveExcellence #ToastmastersDistrict80 Singapore Recreation Club 0:00 / 0:39 0:01 / 0:50 Write a comment…

comment_text: SRC Toastmasters Follow **SRC Toastmasters Chapter Meeting – Colours of Spring** Singapore Recreation Club What a beautifully illuminating evening we had at our recent SRC Toastmasters Chapter Meeting with esteemed guests DTM Ho Chui Lin as our Language Evaluator, Nur Farzana Rahman from Legacy Toastmasters Club and visiting toastmaster Sharlene Phua from Anchorvale Community Club Toastmasters. True to our theme, “Colours of Spring", the room blossomed into a radiant bouquet of colours. From soft pastels to bold blooms, everyone who dressed to the theme truly *illuminated* the evening with warmth, joy and the spirit of renewal. A special moment of pride for the club was witnessing our “baby” Toastmaster Helen Thng deliver her maiden speech (Icebreaker). Watching her take that brave first step reminded us all of our own beginnings, and how far we’ve come. Well done, Helen! We are so proud of you! Congratulations to our Ribbon Winners: **Best Table Topics:** Sharlene Phua **Best Evaluator:** Raphael Lee **Best Speaker:** Anne Lee Each of you truly illuminated the stage with excellence! The evening was further elevated by our engaging mini-workshop, “Boomer vs Zoomer.” It illuminated the generational code differences that often create misunderstandings, not because of attitude or entitlement, but because we sometimes speak different “languages.” For many of our Toastmasters (proudly representing the “boomers”), the session shed light on the pains, perspectives and quirks of the “zoomers,” helping us better understand, empathize and connect. It was a meaningful reminder that growth happens when we listen, learn and bridge the gap together. Spring symbolises renewal and fresh beginnings, and this meeting truly reflected that spirit. Here’s to continuing to illuminate one another’s paths through shared learning, mutual support and collective excellence. #SRCToastmasters #ColoursOfSpring #Illuminate #BoomerVsZoomer #SharedLearning #CollectiveExcellence 0:01 / 0:04 +5 1 comment

comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow This #InternationalWomensDay, we celebrate the women who have made a difference through their contributions to Singapore Red Cross' (SRC) humanitarian work. From fundraising for our local services, to championing and advocating blood donation in Singapore, women have answered the call wherever the vulnerable in our community has needed our help. Janus Ho has had several good starts in her life. Having volunteered with other organisations since 1995, Janus became a community first aider with the SRC in 2013. After attending the Overseas Disaster Deployment Training (ODDT) with SRC in 2016, Janus had been deployed on several overseas humanitarian missions in Bangladesh, Indonesia, Nepal and Vietnam. comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow We're excited to announce that the Singapore Red Cross (SRC) will be at Singapore Comic Con - SGCC from 7-8 December this year and we'd love to connect with you. Here are some key highlights you can look forward to at our booth: Discover and get inspired by SRC’s diverse humanitarian programmes and fundraising initiatives to uplift the lives of the vulnerable and enhance community resilience! We will also be showcasing The Life-Saving Figurines, also known as 'The Unbreakables', a limited edition series of 20 collector’s item figurines created in partnership with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) and Accenture, as part of SRC's “Be Our Champion for Humanity” fundraiser. In addition, get ready to snag some exclusive SRC x Peanuts™ merchandise as part of our 75th Anniversary celebrations. You can find us at Booth L1-G04c. comment_text: SRC Toastmasters is at Singapore Recreation Club · Follow Singapore Double Victory for Eugene Low! Huge congratulations to our very own Vice President Education, Eugene Low, for clinching Champion in both the Humorous Speech Contest and the Speech Evaluation Contest at the Area M1 Contests held on 20th September 2025! The contests, hosted right here at Singapore Recreation Club (SRC), saw Eugene going head-to-head with talented speakers from Mizuho, Capital Markets, and NUS Alumni Toastmasters Clubs. Eugene had the audience roaring with laughter during his hilarious speech, “Abs-solutely Hopeless”, and impressed the judges once again with an evaluation that was sharp, insightful, and delightfully humorous. comment_text: Benjamin William The road to recovery is complex and evolving, but the Singapore Red Cross remains committed to walking alongside affected communities. This next tranche of assistance reflects our focus on both immediate needs and long-term resilience, including efforts to strengthen climate resilience and public health. Our priority is to ensure that communities are equipped and supported. As we continue discussions with our partners to explore additional support for communities, we stand ready to support the provision of shelter materials for houses, and the rebuilding and recovery of community facilities, such as hospitals, clinics, and schools, addressing longer term needs. The SRC thanks the Singapore public and looks to its continued for support to the affected communities. Singapore Red Cross · Follow In response to the escalating humanitarian needs in #Myanmar, the Singapore Red Cross (SRC) is scaling up relief efforts to bring urgent aid to communities facing critical and complex challenges. Following the March 28 earthquake in Myanmar, affected communities continue to face critical needs for shelter, safe water, food, healthcare, sanitation, and livelihood restoration. Recent rainfall and thunderstorms have further deteriorated living conditions for displaced families in tents and temporary shelters. To address these growing needs, SRC will deploy an additional S$600,000 in humanitarian and resilience interventions through partners on the ground, including the Myanmar Red Cross Society International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies , and the International Committee of the Red Cross Starting May 9, a SRC volunteer will spend one month in Myanmar to coordinate current response efforts and assess future needs. comment_text: HO Ching Follow Huge thanks to the 5300 donors who stepped up since the 25 Jan 2024 appeal for O+ and O- donors when our blood bank ran critically low for O+/- stock. O blood type is super important bcos these are universal donors whose blood may be accepted by various blood type patients, esp during emergencies when their blood type is unknown and quick transfusion is needed. Do you know red blood cells have a shelf life of 6 weeks, while the platelets have a shelf life of only 7 days? This is why we need to have a regular stream of donors throughout the year. The norm is to keep a stockpile of 9 days to be able to respond to any major emergency or disaster. So the key for blood bank resilience is a steady stream of regular blood donations throughout the year. Hence, it is good for instance, if blood donation eligible folks can make a regular schedule like donating around their birthdays or some anniversary. This way, we keep a steady supply stream from those eligible to donate blood. More importantly, the blood bank typically will be 20% lower than than the norm during the festive periods. Given CNY is coming up with a long weekend, it is helpful if our eligible folks make it a point to continue to step up donations for this month of Feb, where CNY will be this weekend and the festive season covers up to 25 Feb for the 15th day of CNY. Do note that the blood banks will be closed this weekend, 10-11 Feb 2024, for the purpose of public blood donations. Eligible donors must weigh at least 45kg, between the age of 16 to 60, and must not have travelled to places with insect borne infection risks. Those who are 16-17 (below 18) should download a parental consent form from the HSA website for their parents to sign before they donate blood. Also to check travel history eligibility, go to www.hsa.gov.sg/donor_criteria. Given the travel history criteria, why not make it a point to do a good deed before your travels, to donate blood before travelling? Donations may be done at the various blood banks at Outram, Dhoby Ghaut, Woodlands, Westgate Towers, and One Punggol. Community and group donations can be organised by contacting the Singapore Red Cross or SRC at 6220-0183 or donate.blood@redcross.sg Stay safe during the upcoming festivities, esp if you are planning to travel anywhere. Take care and keep well. Ong Ye Kung · Follow My sincerest thanks to the 5,300 donors who responded to our appeal for Group O blood last week. They included the young and old, men and women, Singaporeans and non-Singaporeans, civil servants, professionals, business owners, artists and many more. It was a broad and encouraging response. As a result, there has been a 230% improvement in our O+ blood stock, or about 17 days' worth compared to below six days before Ministry of Health, Singapore 's appeal for your help. That said, we have to maintain this momentum. Blood donations typically fall by 20% during festive periods. With Chinese New Year approaching, there is a risk that our blood stock will drop again next week. Special thanks to the Health Sciences Authority and Singapore Red Cross staff for all their efforts behind the scenes. Together, we are a community of life savers.

He was once at the apex, but he has his own foolishness to thank for the downfall and imprisonment he is now going through. I was first elected to Parliament in March 2008. In June that year, deputy prime minister Najib, who was also defence minister, was waiting for his turn to speak at the Shangri-la Dialogue in Singapore. I went up to him and had my only conversation ever with him. I introduced myself as “Bukit Bendera”, the name of my then constituency. Almost instantly, he told me he appreciated that DAP leaders were less “crazy” about the Altantuya case. Then, he claimed he was a leader for a multiethnic Malaysia. It was a weird exchange. That chance meeting left me with an impression that he was a quick-witted politician and he knew that the Altantuya case was an albatross around his neck. Otherwise, why would he tell a stranger about the case in the first instance? 𝗡𝗮𝗷𝗶𝗯’𝘀 𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗶𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽 Opposition leader Anwar Ibrahim’s claim of a September 16 change of government came and went but this threat to UMNO and BN rule was slyfully used by Najib and Muhyiddin Yassin to force the hand of then prime minister Abdullah Badawi to relinquish power. On September 17, 2008, Abdullah was forced to give up the much coveted finance portfolio to Najib. Having tasted blood, Najib and Muhyiddin went to Abdullah again a week later. This time, Abdullah agreed to step down in April 2009. Abdullah permitted a very lively media scene. The unwritten rule then was that as long as the prime minister was not criticised, all other criticisms backed by facts were acceptable. But by January 2009, it was clear the short-lived media freedom would end soon. Astro decided to shut down some very popular talk shows just before Najib took over the reins. Najib was determined to instill fear and reverse the clock to the more authoritarian time of the past. Abdullah’s failure in the 2008 general election was interpreted by Najib as him not being stern enough towards the media and not able to strike fear among the noisy opposition and NGOs like Bersih. In February 2009, Najib as deputy prime minister engineered the collapse of the Pakatan Rakyat Perak state government by inducing several elected representatives to cross over in what was a precursor to the Sheraton coup. Among UMNO circles and the old establishment, many felt Abdullah could have prevented Pakatan Rakyat from taking power in Kedah, Perak, and Selangor in March 2008 by stitching together UMNO-PAS Malay unity governments. PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang had no qualms about signing up for such an arrangement, but not the upright Tok Guru Nik Abdul Aziz Nik Mat. Nik Aziz’s objection to working with UMNO at that time effectively delayed an official UMNO-PAS collaboration by a decade, until after the 2018 election. Najib showed his true colours even before he took power: he is in no way a democrat, with no respect for media freedom nor the political mandate given to opposition parties by the people in elections. And, Najib is more than ready to manipulate PAS to his advantage. If anything, becoming prime minister only fostered these reprehensible beliefs. 𝗡𝗮𝗷𝗶𝗯 𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗽𝗲𝘅 Najib the prime minister had no guiding principles, philosophy, or conviction. He was a transactional leader whose only purpose was to stay in office for as long as possible. Several characteristics stood out: 𝗙𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁, 𝗰𝗮𝘀𝗵 𝗶𝘀 𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 I think we all know this by now. Najib knew he was not loved, he was never a charismatic or visionary leader. Former prime minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad and PKR president Anwar Ibrahim were always more popular than Najib. He made up for his lack of popularity by buying support with money, inside UMNO and among the population. Najib genuinely believed money could buy him support and loyalty. He could never comprehend why people would fight for justice and dignity. 𝗦𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗱, 𝗲𝘅𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁𝘀, 𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀 Najib had been in the system long enough to know he needed to be seen doing something good for the nation although he clearly had no idea what to do and he didn’t think the civil service knew either. Hence Najib governed through consultants and made policy decisions by way of PowerPoint presentations. 1Malaysia was a slogan without much substance proposed by a PR consultant. With Pemandu, Idris Jala was the “in-house” consultant trying to make piecemeal cosmetic changes to impress voters. A Korean consultant, W Chan Kim, of Blue Ocean Strategy fame, also landed himself a consultant role with Najib. They came up with the National Blue Ocean Strategy and one of the first initiatives was putting prisoners in army camps. Military leaders were furious that prisons were set up in six army camps, which was a clear manifestation of the inability of Najib, Idris Jala, and Chan Kim, to appreciate the real purpose and functions of the armed forces, and the different roles of the prison department and the military. 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝗿𝗱, 𝗮 𝗯𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗼𝗳 𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗵𝘆 Najib is the ultimate princeling who doesn’t understand the lives of ordinary people. When he introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) as a silver bullet to cover up plundered national coffers, he failed to understand the core economic problem the country faced. Most Malaysians are not paying income tax because they are in the bottom strata and do not meet the minimum income threshold. The real challenge was to raise income, not taxes. Najib became a hated figure when GST was implemented in April 2015, which coincided with the sharp decline of global petrol prices, which prompted Najib to cut federal budget allocations massively in 2015 and 2016. And then he encouraged us to take quinoa for good health. 𝗙𝗼𝘂𝗿𝘁𝗵, 𝗶𝗺𝗮𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 Najib and his wife Rosmah Mansor governed as if they would never fall, that they would always be at the apex of power. The blatant disregard for law, rules, and norms were unbelievable. Committing crimes so brazenly is unforgivable, but what’s crazier is they never bothered to stay an arm’s length away from the incriminating evidence of their financial crimes. The SRC case which sent Najib to jail is a case in point. Because Najib felt the need to buy support from his associates, he needed cash in his bank account, to be issued with cheques signed under his own name to the UMNO and BN warlords. These left behind a money trail. Najib and Rosmah made themselves sitting ducks because they had this distorted sense of legal immunity. 𝗙𝗶𝗳𝘁𝗵, 𝗻𝗼 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁, 𝗻𝗼 𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗰𝘆 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗻𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 Najib used the state apparatus at his disposal to inflict cruelty on his opponents. The long list of people threatened with their lives or at least with lawsuits for exposing the 1MDB scandal need not be mentioned here. Muhyiddin told me he was tailed by Special Branch officers after he was sacked as deputy prime minister in July 2015. Najib also jailed his biggest political opponent at that time, Anwar. When Najib called Anwar twice by phone on election night in 2018, he must have regretted the 2015 decision to imprison Anwar as it forced the opposition to realign and eventually became a force that unseated his government. On May 9, 2018, Anwar was still held as a prisoner at a government health facility in Cheras. Najib was hoping Anwar would agree to form the government with UMNO on the assumption that Pakatan Harapan would not have enough seats. Miraculously, Harapan won 113 seats on election night, crossing the 112 line by a hair’s breadth. 𝗣𝗼𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗰𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 When Najib came into office in 2009, UMNO was no longer the hegemon it once was. In 2008, the opposition broke BN’s stranglehold on the two-thirds majority in Parliament. The opposition also captured Kedah, Penang, Perak, and Selangor, on top of Kelantan. That election, the opposition received 49% of the popular votes while BN was at 51%. It should have been a wake-up call for Najib to reform UMNO-BN. But that was not to be. He set out on a mission to crush the opposition and strengthen the one-party state. In 2013, BN won a tawdry victory under Najib’s premiership, where it received 47% of the votes and the opposition coalition Pakatan Rakyat, which consisted of DAP, PKR, and PAS at that time, received 51%. Gerrymandering allowed BN to hold on to a bigger share of seats with less vote share. He still refused to budge. In Najib’s near-decade rule, there was not a single attempt to amend the Constitution, which requires a two-thirds majority in the lower house of the Parliament, the Dewan Rakyat. The reason was simple: Najib could never bring himself to negotiate with the opposition. In comparison, constitutional amendments took place thrice after 2018, once to lower the voting age to 18 and to bring about automatic voter registration, another to reinstate Sabah and Sarawak as ‘territories’, and finally the most recent one was to pave the way for an anti-party-hopping law. There were talks between Najib’s men and Anwar’s lieutenants between the May 2013 election and National Day on Aug 31, 2013, to explore collaboration but that did not go very far. There wasn’t political will on the part of Najib to accommodate the parliamentary opposition. 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗱, 𝗡𝗮𝗷𝗶𝗯 𝗽𝘂𝗿𝘀𝘂𝗲𝗱 𝗮 𝟯-𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗱 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝘆: First, to remove Anwar from the scene hence removing the alternative prime ministerial candidate. Second, to lure PAS into UMNO’s fold via a Muslim unity platform. Third, to paint the opposition as DAP and Chinese-dominated, thus unworthy of support from the Malay electorate. Anwar was sent to prison on Feb 10, 2015, depriving the opposition of a prime ministerial candidate. Nik Aziz passed away on Feb 12, 2015 thus removing the only hurdle for PAS to align with Najib. In June 2015, PAS split right in the middle. The hardliners who very much preferred to get closer to Najib ousted the moderates at the party election, who then exited the party to form Parti Amanah Negara. I am made to understand that with increasingly damaging details about Najib’s misconduct in the 1MDB case being leaked, there were efforts in 2015 to persuade Najib to retire gracefully in exchange for protection and amnesty. If he ever thought of the slim possibility that he would one day end up in prison, a well-arranged exit could have prevented the fall of UMNO, BN, and himself. But Najib and Rosmah were never able to envisage any political order other than the one in which they were at the top and untouchable. BN won massively in the Sarawak election on May 7, 2016. UMNO also won two concurrent by-elections in Sungai Besar and Kuala Kangsar on June 18, 2016. Much as Najib was constantly under pressure by the leaks and reports about the 1MDB scandal, he was in a very comfortable position. The assumption, arising from the twin by-elections, was that UMNO and PAS could go into three-corner fights with Harapan, which was thought to be advantageous to UMNO. Malays who were unhappy with Najib and UMNO would vote for PAS. As long as their votes did not go to Harapan, UMNO would win. Najib conceived this grand strategy in March 2014 but became complacent and was caught by surprise by the game-changers introduced by his opponents. He never expected the opposition to come together, reaching an accommodation between Mahathir and Anwar on July 14, 2017; and on January 7, 2018, agreeing on Mahathir as the seventh prime minister and Anwar as the eighth, settling the leadership question in anticipation of the election. Najib recently said in hindsight that he considered dissolving Parliament in August 2017. Actually, I would argue that given the Mahathir-Anwar accommodation was newly achieved in July 2017, even an August election might not have saved Najib. Each of Najib’s gambits, such as deregistering Bersatu just before the dissolution of Parliament and setting polling day on Wednesday, a work day, caused more uproar among Malaysians towards him and his government. The grand chessboard was now in the hands of his opponent, Pakatan Harapan. During the campaign period, I was stunned watching a televised speech of Najib who claimed the huge turnouts at opposition rallies in Malacca and Putrajaya were because busloads of supporters were sent in from out of town. I knew very well that all ceramah-goers came voluntarily without any payment or transport. Najib was also highly confident of winning, claiming to “know the reality on the ground” and “have a strong base”. He and his inner circle were deluded to think BN would win with a two-thirds majority. He was completely out of touch and misguided. I commented at that time, Najib was like Hitler in his final days, hiding in a bunker, rising only sparingly and firing a few shots aimlessly. 𝗙𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘀𝘂𝗿𝘃𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝘁-𝟮𝟬𝟭𝟴 After the fall of the BN federal government in GE14, Najib should have known he would eventually end up in jail. He tried to leave the country but was stopped. On June 30, 2018, with Najib’s support, UMNO elected Ahmad Zahid Hamidi as its president. Instead of electing a new group of leaders to renew and rebuild UMNO to win power at the next general election, the party was held ransom by Najib and Zahid. They knew they had to destroy the Harapan government if they wanted to stay out of jail, or better still for them, make a strong comeback. UMNO went on a scorched earth policy to burn the house down for the Harapan government. Najib took on a new persona - “Malu Apa Bossku” - on Facebook since the Cameron Highlands by-election in January 2019. UMNO aligned with PAS from October 2018 onwards and together launched an anti-Icerd demonstration on December 8, 2018. Najib and Zahid engineered attacks after attacks on Harapan. They also played an instrumental role in the February 2020 Sheraton Move. Their aim was to free themselves from their legal cases. Subsequently, not getting what they wanted from the Muhyiddin government, they went on to bring down Muhyiddin. And, since the installation of Ismail Sabri Yaakob as prime minister in August 2021, Najib and Zahid have been pushing for snap polls and already caused state-wide elections in Malacca and Johor in November 2021 and March 2022, respectively. Now that Najib has fallen, Zahid won’t hold up for too long. Hypothetically, had Najib apologised to the nation, removed himself from politics, and begged for some form of amnesty the moment he was defeated in 2018, the outcomes would have been very different. 𝗣𝗼𝘀𝘁𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗽𝘁 In our recent battles with Najib’s Facebook admins over the question of the littoral combat ships (LCS), I realised Najib has not changed. Facts don’t matter to him. He was just putting out false narratives without even knowing if those postings would boomerang on himself later. I believe that one of the reasons why the LCS became such a massive national sensation was because Najib kept talking about it, at times with nearly 10 Facebook postings each day. Najib would listen to consultants who sound smart but hardly know anything really, such as Idris Jala or Chan Kim. You now see their new incarnations in Zaid Ibrahim and Hisyam Teh. They probably helped speed up his entry to prison. Najib has never been strategic. He committed too many follies - political or otherwise - along the way. I know there are still many who think he will come back one day. I am more than ready to write his political obituary. Liew Chin Tong

comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow The Singapore Red Cross (SRC) today deployed 90 water filters to Mandalay and Sagaing to support communities-in-need, following its needs assessment. These portable filtration systems are a vital part of SRC’s ongoing efforts in WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) and clean water access. Thanks to the support of the community, we have received close to S$1.5M in donations for the Myanmar & Thailand Earthquake fundraising appeal since its launch on 30 March 2025. comment_text: Chan Chun Sing Follow Our perception of humanitarian organisations, such as the Singapore Red Cross , often mirrors the image of a fireman: a hero who swoops in to fight fires and resolve crises. But their core mission isn’t just about saving the day. It’s also about their quiet, long-term and essential efforts to build capacity – and preventing fires from happening in the first place. At the Singapore Red Cross Humanitarian Conference today, we discussed how we can all contribute to tackling humanitarian challenges. Just as a fireman aims to prevent fires rather than extinguishing them, we must focus our efforts on empowering our communities to support and sustain themselves, and to learn how to take care of one another. When we enhance community resilience and self-sufficiency, we are building strong communities that can come together in times of need and thrive in the face of adversity. We may not be able to make the world perfect. But together, we can certainly make it a little less imperfect. +2
