comment_text: Embassy of Ukraine in Singapore Follow On 6 November 2022 a beautiful charity event to support Ukrainian children's hospital «Okhmatdyt» ( НДСЛ Охматдит ) was held in a circle of good friends of Ukraine in the Shangri-La Hotel. Guests had the opportunity to learn more about the current situation in and the «new normal» of Ukrainian doctors, who are fighting for the lives and health of patients under constant shelling of the Russian army and frequent blackouts. As mentioned by «Okhmatdyt» Executive Director Volodymyr Zhovnir in his video address to the event participants, «the funds raised this evening will allow to buy important equipment to support efforts of the medical personal in their daily struggle to save patients». The local Ukrainian community used this opportunity to introduce Ukrainian culture and music to the international attendees of the evening. Our special thanks go to Ms. Peggy Jeffs and everyone else involved for their kind initiative to organize this event and the Singapore Red Cross for yet another round of excellent cooperation in securing funds for humanitarian relief efforts in Ukraine. +4

Ms Vivian, determined by aspirations to support her family, came to Singapore in 2019, embarking on her journey as a migrant domestic worker (MDW). In mid-2023, she transferred to another employer, Mr Jon Ong. On 11 December 2023, her dreams took an unforeseen turn. Mr Ong discovered her unresponsive and promptly rushed her to Sengkang General Hospital. Medical tests revealed a ruptured aneurysm, leading to bleeding in her brain. He had treated Vivian as part of his family and his older son was very fond of her and this sudden turn of events which saw her fighting for her life saddened his family. He knew he had to assist her in any possible way and assist her to return home to her family when her health situation allowed. Vivian had undergone several surgeries and medical treatments. Mr Ong reached out to CDE and we contacted the local Philippine authorities, who worked together with the local hospital to ensure that Vivian would receive adequate care the moment she arrived in the Philippines. Our strategic partner, the Singapore Red Cross (SRC), swiftly mobilised their staff to accompany Vivian to the Philippines. SRC also worked with the Philippine Red Cross (PRC) to provide the ambulance and paramedics service over in the Philippines. We sincerely hope that Vivian can make a full recovery soon. Mr Ong has set up a crowdfunding campaign to help defray Vivian’s medical bills. The campaign can be found here: https://give.asia/campaign/help-vivian-recover / https://gogetfunding.com/helpvivianrosada/. The Domestic Employees Welfare Fund (DEWF), the charity arm of CDE, extended an ex-gratia payment to help alleviate the cost related to Vivian’s repatriation. Let’s continue to support MDWs in Singapore facing distressing situations and who may need humanitarian assistance or upskilling opportunities. Your kindness can be a beacon of hope to other MDWs who are facing similar situations. You can find more details at https://bit.ly/donatetoDEWF. comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow In celebration of its 70th anniversary, the Red Cross Youth Singapore (RCY) launched the Red Cross Junior @ Community (RCJ@Community) and unveiled RCY Youth Hub, in an outreach event graced by Guest-of-Honour, Minister for Community, Culture and Youth, and Second Minister for Law, Mr Edwin Tong In his speech, Minister Edwin Tong remarked, “Over the past seven decades, the Red Cross Youth has made significant contributions to the community. The Red Cross Youth has evolved with time, refreshing its curriculum and introducing new initiatives to stay relevant. With the launch of RCJ@Community and Youth Hub, Red Cross Youth is able to provide even more opportunities to the general public, allowing everyone to have a chance to join the Red Cross regardless of their ages, and provide a safe space for the youths’ mental health and wellbeing, and to learn more about the Red Cross’ humanitarian journey with their many initiatives to aid the vulnerable while enhancing resilience, both locally and overseas.” Mr Benjamin William , Secretary General and CEO of the Singapore Red Cross, said, “Not only has the RCY helped shape the lives of thousands of youth, it has also started many youth on their personal humanitarian journey. We thank the past and present members for their contributions, and for imparting essential skills and sound humanitarian values to our Red Cross Youth, playing an important role in their character development.” Photos by Wong Leong Jeam and Lai Wei Song, volunteers] +7

comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow Did you know? Only 1.8% of our residential population are blood donors, and only 1.5% of the donor population are Rh(D) negative: A-, B-, O- and AB-. This is why it is a challenge to maintain a sufficient supply of Rh(D) negative blood due to the limited pool of eligible donors. Singapore Red Cross' Secretary General/CEO Benjamin William explains, "There is a constant need for Rh(D) negative blood in Singapore, as Rh(D) negative patients are recommended to receive Rh(D) negative blood because Rh(D) positive blood increases their risks of developing Rh(D) antibodies. This is especially crucial to patients who require regular blood transfusion to sustain their lives.  Even if you are unsure of your blood group, we encourage you to make an appointment to donate blood in the next few weeks. Your blood donation will help to save lives regardless of your blood group." #GiveBloodSaveLivesSG #SGUnited Find out more about blood donation: https://giveblood.sg/ Source: Sunday Times © Singapore Press Holdings Limited. comment_text: Album COVID-19 (Novel Coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2) Singapore Matters added a new photo. · Follow Maybe it's because we are small. Singapore values trust. We understand that all countries are in this together. We did not interdict any supplies. 3M has a plant here,. The Singapore government put in their orders and line up, just like everybody else that 3M Singapore is supplying in Asia. At the same time, the Singapore government goes out to the world with various logistics companies to hunt for more N95 masks. Meanwhile, with our mask production relocated back to Singapore from Taiwan, Innosparks started its Air+ N95 mask production in Singapore even as we wait for other countries to lift their export bans. All countries are in this together. That is why we gave masks and test kits to China in February when the need there was great. We donated 5000 swabs to Malaysia when they asked. We also donated hazmat suits and ventilators to Batam hospitals. And Singapore Red Cross is doing their part for the international community by donating masks to 11 countries. Note: Facts regarding 3M and Innosparks are gleaned from Ms Ho Ching's facebook posts.

comment_text: High Commission of Sri Lanka in Singapore Follow Dance of Unity Charity Concert Held in Singapore in Support of Cyclone Relief for Sri Lanka A multicultural charity concert, “Dance of Unity: Rebuilding Sri Lanka,” was held on 05 March 2026 at the PGP Hall in Singapore, bringing together Singapore’s diverse arts communities to support relief and recovery efforts for communities affected by the Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka. The initiative was organised by Apsaras Dance Company, with the guidance of Ambassador K. Kesavapany, a distinguished former Singaporean diplomat, in collaboration with the Singapore Red Cross. The event was supported by the High Commission of Sri Lanka in Singapore, the Maha Karuna Buddhist Society and the Singapore Sinhala Buddhist Association, while the venue was sponsored by the Hindu Endowments Board. The concert was organised to mobilise public support for the Singapore Red Cross's humanitarian response in Sri Lanka. The event was graced by the High Commissioner of Sri Lanka, Senarath Dissanayake, Ambassador K. Kesavapany, and Mr Benjamin William, CEO of Singapore Red Cross. The religious advisor of the Mahakaruna Buddhist Society. Rev Dr. K. Gunaratana Thero sponsored refreshments for all the participants. Representatives of Singapore based Community Associations were also graced the occasion. The charity concert featured performances by several leading arts organisations in Singapore, including Apsaras Dance Company, Bhaskar’s Arts Academy, ERA Dance Theatre, Omkar Arts, Re Xin Opera Association, Singapore Indian Fine Arts Society, Svayambhu Arts, Tattva Productions, and Temple of Fine Arts. Artists representing Singapore’s Indian, Malay, Chinese and Sri Lankan communities performing together in a spirit of unity and solidarity. The event attracted over 250 attendees, including donors, business communities, representatives of religious and community organisations, and members of the Sri Lankan community in Singapore. The initiative reflected the strong bonds of friendship between Singapore and Sri Lanka and highlights the solidarity shown by Singaporean communities in support of Sri Lanka’s ongoing recovery and rebuilding efforts. Cyclone Ditwah, which struck Sri Lanka in late November and early December 2025, triggered severe flooding and landslides across many parts of the country, affecting nearly 2.35 million people from more than 668,000 families. The disaster resulted in significant loss of life and extensive damage to homes, infrastructure, agriculture, and livelihoods, with thousands of families displaced and many community institutions, including places of worship and schools, sustaining heavy damage. comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Academy Follow Day by day, we continue building capacity and strengthening communities. Over 3 enriching days, selected Singapore Red Cross staff, trainers, and volunteers came together to deepen their expertise in Psychological First Aid (PFA) for Group, a vital skillset in today’s increasingly complex world. From navigating group dynamics to responding to difficult disclosures, participants were immersed in: • Understanding psychosocial well-being in collective settings • Applying core PFA skills to group contexts • Managing emotional reactions and giving constructive feedback • Practising through role plays, demos, and real-world scenarios But capacity building doesn’t end in the classroom. What we’re doing is much more than training, we are cultivating a network of confident responders, equipped to provide emotional support, build trust, and foster psychological safety in the communities we serve. This training is part of a broader effort to: - Expand our national capacity for psychosocial support - ⁠Strengthen our pool of trainers and frontliners - ⁠Build a culture of compassion and readiness in crisis response It was an intense yet deeply meaningful journey, one that brings us closer to a shared vision: a safer, more resilient Singapore. comment_text: Aravinth அரவிந்த் Kumarasamy குமாரசாமி is with Kaisavapany Krishnasamy and 13 others · Follow There are moments when the arts remind us of their deeper purpose - not only to inspire and entertain, but to bring people together in compassion and shared humanity. It was a privilege to curate and present this special evening of performances, bringing together Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Sri Lankan Kandyan Dance and Chinese Opera on one stage. What made the evening truly meaningful was the coming together of nine remarkable dance institutions across Singapore and nearly ninety dedicated dancers, each offering their art with generosity of spirit. This collective effort supported the Singapore Red Cross fundraiser to aid the rebuilding efforts in Sri Lanka following the recent Cyclone DITWAH. In many ways, the stage became a space where art transformed into empathy, solidarity and hope. My heartfelt gratitude to the fellow artists and institutions who stepped forward to support this meaningful initiative: Bhaskar’s Arts Academy Omkar Arts – Singapore Re Xin Opera Association Singapore Indian Fine Arts Society (SIFAS) Sri Lanka Ramaya Buddhist Temple Svayambhu Fine Arts TATVA Productions Temple of Fine Arts Singapore And my wonderful dancers from Apsaras Dance Company amd Apsaras Arts Academy who continue to inspire with their dedication and passion. To see artists from different traditions stand shoulder to shoulder for a humanitarian cause was deeply moving. It reminded me once again that the arts have the power to unite hearts beyond cultures, borders and traditions. This initiative was thoughtfully mooted by our Chairman Ambassador Kaisavapany Krishnasamy with his empathy and many experiences in reaching out with a helping hand to communities at the hour of need. My sincere appreciation to all the dancers, teachers and volunteers who made this possible. Gratitude to Reverend Dr Gunaratna and the Singapore Hindu Endowments Board for their generous support. A heartfelt thank you to all donors who came forward to support the cause and to those who attended the concert and encouraged the dancers. May the spirit of “Arts Uniting Communities” continue to guide us in using the arts as a force for compassion and meaningful change. Sharing a few clicks by Lijesh Photography +6

comment_text: Tan Chin Tuan Foundation Follow We had the pleasure of another meaningful visit last week, this time to witness a collaboration in action between Singapore Red Cross and RSVP Singapore! This initiative, the Medical Chaperone and Transport Programme (MCT), was created in response to a growing need: ensuring that seniors have the support and transport they need to go for their medical appointments. Through this collaboration, Singapore Red Cross manages the MCT programme, while RSVP Singapore provides volunteer chaperones. This is a meaningful partnership that blends the strength of both organisations. During our visit, we joined the transport crew as they picked up a senior client. What stood out most was the tender attention of the RSVP Singapore volunteer: helping the client move from home to wheelchair, then into the transport vehicle with patience and dignity. At the clinic, the chaperone stayed by his side through the consultation, thoughtfully clarifying the doctor’s advice to ensure he understood every detail. This programme goes well beyond transport. It provides reassurance, companionship, and a peace of mind, making what could be a stressful journey a far more supported and dignified one. We are truly glad to be part of such collaborative work that not only uplifts seniors but also responds meaningfully to the rising needs within Singapore’s social service landscape. Write a comment…

comment_text: Migrant Connect SG added 57 photos and 23 videos from 1 January at 22:00. · Follow 1 January 𝐌𝗂𝗀𝗋α𐓣𝗍 𝐂ⱺ𐓣𐓣𝖾𝖼𝗍 𝐒𝐆 – Annual Gathering 2026 & BBQ Party 2026 সুন্দরভাবে সম্পন্ন হয়েছে। ১ জানুয়ারি ২০২৬‑এর এই আয়োজনটি ছিল প্রবাসী ভাইদের জন্য আনন্দ, বন্ধন ও ভালোবাসার একটি মিলনমেলা—যেখানে ছিল খেলাধুলা, গান‑নাচ, BBQ আর প্রাণভরা আড্ডা। এই সুন্দর আয়োজনের জন্য আন্তরিক ধন্যবাদ 𝐌𝗂𝗀𝗋α𐓣𝗍 𝐂ⱺ𐓣𐓣𝖾𝖼𝗍 𝐒𝐆 এবং বিশেষভাবে ধন্যবাদ আমাদের Founder, সাইয়েদ এশিয়া রবিন ( Sayeed Abu ) ভাইকে, যিনি পরিকল্পনা, সংগঠন ও আর্থিক সহায়তার মাধ্যমে পুরো আয়োজনটি সম্ভব করেছেন। Chief Guest SM Abdullah Al Mamun Counsellor (Labour) Bangladesh High Commission, Singapore (BDHC, SG) আমাদের অনুষ্ঠানে উপস্থিত থেকে প্রবাসী কমিউনিটিকে অনুপ্রেরণা দেওয়ার জন্য আমরা তাঁর প্রতি আন্তরিকভাবে কৃতজ্ঞ। Special Guest Mohammed Ashrafur Rahman Khan ( Robin Khan Singer: Nil Arif Dancer: Chiranjit Siddha Our Collaborators We are proud to collaborate with the following respected organisations over the past years, whose continued support and cooperation have strengthened our community initiatives. • Singapore Red Cross • Health Sciences Authority (HSA) • Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) • National Environment Agency (NEA) Sing Lit Station Their support and cooperation play an important role in strengthening our community initiatives. Special Appreciation & Credits • বিশেষ কৃতজ্ঞতা আমাদের Founder এর প্রতি—vision, planning, organising এবং financial support দিয়ে অনুষ্ঠানটি সফল করার জন্য। • ধন্যবাদ আমাদের Senior Ambassador Masud Rana Md Sabuz Ahamed , এবং তাদের টিমকে—খেলাধুলা ও activity sessions সুন্দরভাবে পরিচালনার জন্য। • আন্তরিক ধন্যবাদ আমাদের Special Guest, Mr. Mohammed Ashrafur Rahman Khan (Robin)—যিনি জরুরি কারণে উপস্থিত থাকতে না পারলেও sound system support দিয়ে নিঃশর্ত সহযোগিতা করেছেন। • ধন্যবাদ Anisuzzaman Anis ও Miah Mohammad Jany কে—transport support দেওয়ার জন্য। • ধন্যবাদ Mr. Sabbir Taibur Rahman, কে—dinner cost for BBQ preparation team & camera ও video coverage সাপোর্টের জন্য & MD Samiul Islam কে—on day BBQ তে সার্বিক সাপোর্টের জন্য। • কৃতজ্ঞতা Mr. Hossain Kamrul ও Mr. Miah Apon কে—gifts ব্যবস্থাপনায় সহযোগিতার জন্য। BBQ Preparing Team যারা রাত জেগে BBQ ম্যারিনেড করেছেন, এই ভাইদের অক্লান্ত পরিশ্রম ছাড়া BBQ সফল হতো না— • Sabbir Taibur Rahman • Farazi Mohammad Roman • Maruf Billah • Robiul Karim (MD) • Md. Golam Mohammad Bulbul আপনাদের সবাইকে আন্তরিক ধন্যবাদ Thanks to All আমাদের সকল blood doners, members, volunteers, ambassadors, well wishers ও supporters—যাঁরা সরাসরি বা পরোক্ষভাবে এই আয়োজনের সাথে যুক্ত ছিলেন—সবার প্রতি হৃদয় থেকে কৃতজ্ঞতা। এই আয়োজন আবারও প্রমাণ করেছে—Community strength comes from unity, respect, and teamwork. আগামীতেও এমন আরও সুন্দর ও অর্থবহ উদ্যোগের প্রত্যাশায়, InshaAllah. comment_text: Yap Kwong Weng Follow As we bid farewell to an extraordinary year, I am taking a moment to reflect on the year and look forward to an exceptional 2025. Under the visionary leadership of Dr. Robert Yap, we've made significant strides in expanding our SuperPort Việt Nam ™ presence, successfully relaunching with a robust strategic plan. Our commitment to sustainability has taken a leap forward, with our net-zero initiatives powered by cutting-edge technologies paving the way for a greener future in logistics. This year has been marked by forging valuable alliances that will shape our future. We've partnered with tech agencies like Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) , innovative start-ups, and national entities including VnEconomy , and VietnamPost including the University of Transport Technology. I'd also like to extend my gratitude to the Oudet Souvannavong and the ASEAN Business Advisory Council for their friendship and support – our golf session has been a delight! My journey has been enriched by meaningful involvement with organizations like the Singapore Red Cross , whose humanitarian efforts have been truly inspiring. Some months back, we witnessed the indomitable human spirit in the face of adversity, as communities affected by Typhoon Yagi demonstrated remarkable #resilience and gumption. As we stand at the cusp of a new era in global trade, where supply chains are becoming the lifeblood of ASEAN's trade flows, we are poised to make an impact. The question is always about speed, #efficiency and time. To our partners, colleagues, and supporters: thank you for being an integral part of our journey. Here's to a joyous New Year and an exceptional start to 2025! YCH Group #singapore #Vietnam #Technology #sustainability #Growth #Challenges #Logistics #Asean #Trade #NewYear2025

Recent comments questioning Singapore’s humanitarian efforts, suggesting that the Republic is “the illegal state’s pet” or that its aid is of dubious quality, reveal not insight but misunderstanding. Such accusations confuse humanitarian neutrality with political alignment, ignoring the principles that define both Singapore’s diplomacy and the Singapore Red Cross’s conduct. 1. Singapore’s Consistent Neutrality Singapore’s foreign policy has long been guided by principled neutrality, rule of law, and respect for sovereignty. It does not take sides in conflicts but consistently supports humanitarian outcomes grounded in the United Nations Charter and the Geneva Conventions. To describe Singapore as anyone’s “pet” is to disregard decades of careful, independent diplomacy, from maintaining ties with both Israel and Palestine to providing humanitarian aid through multilateral, neutral channels such as the Egyptian Red Crescent (ERC) and the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS). Singapore’s foreign aid is never an endorsement of any government or faction. It is a reaffirmation of a single principle, that human suffering must be addressed, regardless of politics. 2. The Singapore Red Cross: A Model of Transparency and Humanitarian Integrity The Singapore Red Cross (SRC), founded in 1949, operates under the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement’s Fundamental Principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, and independence. It is a registered Institution of Public Character (IPC) in Singapore, subject to oversight by the Commissioner of Charities, with all donations independently audited and published annually. In October 2025, the SRC confirmed it had delivered S$1.9 million in humanitarian aid to Gaza, including S$1.2 million in tents and essential supplies for 6,500 displaced persons, handed over symbolically to the Egyptian Red Crescent (ERC) for onward transport through the Rafah crossing (Berita Harian, 7 Oct 2025). The symbolic handover, witnessed by President Tharman Shanmugaratnam during his visit to Cairo on 21 September 2025, marked Singapore’s formal contribution to relief operations coordinated with the PRCS and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) (Channel NewsAsia, Sept 2025). Accusations that Singapore’s aid is “fishy” or of “unknown quality” ignore how humanitarian supply chains operate. The ERC and PRCS are internationally recognised for aid verification, logistics, and border compliance under international humanitarian law. The SRC’s procurement standards match global Red Cross norms, ensuring aid items meet humanitarian-grade quality. To question that process is not to question Singapore alone, it is to cast doubt on the entire Red Cross–Red Crescent Movement, an institution built on neutrality and accountability. 3. The 2025 Freedom Flotilla (Global Sumud Campaign): Symbolism and Limits In contrast, the 2025 Freedom Flotilla, part of the Global Sumud campaign led by the Freedom Flotilla Coalition, represented humanitarian idealism through defiance. Its organisers sought to challenge Israel’s naval blockade and deliver aid directly to Gaza by sea. However, under the San Remo Manual on International Law Applicable to Armed Conflicts at Sea (1994), a coastal state may enforce a blockade if it is impartial, declared publicly, and allows humanitarian exemptions through authorised routes. Israel cited these provisions when intercepting the flotilla approximately 80 km off Gaza’s coast (Reuters, 30 June 2025; Al Jazeera English, June 2025). Sixty-eight participants were detained and later released following diplomatic negotiations. As Sayigh (2024) notes, such actions often turn “conscience into confrontation,” achieving awareness but not relief. Likewise, Kosmatopoulos (2019) calls these missions “performative resistance at sea”, morally stirring but logistically futile. While the flotilla succeeded in drawing international attention to Gaza’s suffering, it failed to deliver a single package of aid. Symbolism, without lawful coordination, once again proved unsustainable. 4. The True Test of Character: Action, Not Accusation Singapore’s approach may appear understated, but that is by design. Its humanitarian operations are structured, lawful, and effective. While others seek attention, Singapore seeks outcomes. As A. Chong (2024) writes, the Republic’s diplomacy reflects “rational humanitarianism”, compassion within the constraints of law. This is not submission, it is strength. To some, silence may seem complicity, but in humanitarian work, silence often means focus, on saving lives, not winning arguments. 5. A Broader Lesson in Maturity The hallmark of a credible nation is not how loudly it condemns, but how steadily it acts. Singapore’s citizens and institutions have been shaped by values of discipline, humility, and collective dignity. Its foreign policy does not serve any external power, it serves peace and predictability. By working through recognised humanitarian channels rather than political provocations, Singapore ensures that what aid it sends, however modest, actually reaches its intended recipients. To accuse Singapore of servility is to misunderstand the quiet strength of a small state that knows the value of restraint, the cost of recklessness, and the meaning of moral consistency. Conclusion: Compassion Beyond Politics Singapore’s humanitarian diplomacy is not about sides, it is about standards. Its citizens contribute responsibly. Its government upholds integrity. Its Red Cross delivers aid through lawful, transparent, and internationally verified routes. In a world where outrage often overshadows integrity, Singapore stands apart, not as anyone’s pet, but as a principled nation guided by law and empathy. While others shout about justice, Singapore quietly delivers it, one shipment of aid, one act of humanity at a time. comment_text: SMRT Follow Riding into the HO-HO-HOlidays! #SMRT was delighted to be part of Land Transport Authority – We Keep Your World Moving 's launch event for this year's Christmas-themed trains and stations, graced by Senior Minister of State (SMS), Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment and Ministry of Transport, Dr Amy Khor as the Guest-of-Honour. Also joining in the festivities was SMRT Trains President, Mr Lam Sheau Kai, and Stellar Lifestyle President, Mr Tony Heng. The event included a stopover at Dhoby Ghaut station on the Circle Line to view the Christmas festive murals and a saxophone performance by Mr Cheong Cher Hing, a busker with disabilities, who is also part of SMRT's "Music in Community" programme. At Staytion Lifestyle Centre, a talented group of Singapore Red Cross Juniors put up a carolling performance and eight beneficiaries from ElderAid presented a hand-painted Christmas card to SMS Dr Khor. From now till 2 Jan 2025, have a holly jolly journey on Christmas-themed trains that will be running on all our lines including the North-South, East-West, Circle, and Thomson East-Coast Lines. Catch festive decor on selected bus services including 190 and 960 operated by SMRT. Don't miss the Christmas murals at selected SMRT-operated stations: Bedok (EW5), Dhoby Ghaut (CC1), Great World (TE15), Marine Parade (TE26), and Woodlands South (TE3)! #AllAboutTrains #AllAboutBuses #ESG@SMRT +2 Write a comment…

comment_text: Tringapore Again Follow It's been days and the chances of finding survivors are fading. Battling the scorching heat and the risk or diseases,  rescue team are still racing against time to find as much survivors as possible. Stay strong and stay safe to the people of Myanmarball and those countryball rescuers... Note: I wanted to draw my own version of this but Indonesiaball 3.0 beat me to it. Hence l will not publish my version, as a mark of respect to the solemn mood on the ground. Indonesiaball 3.0 · Follow ကမ္ဘာ့နိုင်ငံများမှ လူသားချင်းစာနာမှု အကူအညီများ ရောက်ရှိလာပြီး မြန်မာနိုင်ငံသည် သင့်မြတ်သော တည်ငြိမ်မှုကို ပြန်လည်ရရှိနိုင်မည်ဟု မျှော်လင့်ပါသည်။ ငါသည် Junta အာဏာရှင်မှ မိမိတို့၏ သံတမန်များကို ကူညီကယ်ဆယ်ရေးလုပ်ငန်းများတွင် ပါဝင်ခွင့်ပြုရန် မျှော်လင့်ပါသည်။ ပြည်တွင်းစစ်ကို ရပ်တန့်ပြီး ပြန်လည်ထူထောင်မှုအတွက် အာရုံစိုက်ပါ !!! ____ Humanitarian aid has arrived from various countries, and we hope that Myanmar will recover and return to peace as before. I sincerely hope that the Junta allows volunteers to assist those who are injured and still missing. Stop the civil war and focus on recovery! ____ Several countries have provided aid and rescue teams to support Myanmar in this crisis. Among them: China: Sent rescue teams, medical personnel, and aid worth 100 million yuan. India: Dispatched a field hospital and over 15 tons of relief supplies. Russia: Deployed 120 doctors and rescuers, along with an airborne hospital in Mandalay. Japan: Provided $6 million in emergency aid and sent medical teams. Malaysia: Sent 50 disaster rescue team members and donated 10 million ringgit. Philippines: Deployed a 91-member humanitarian team from various sectors. Singapore: Sent 80 members of its Civil Defence Force for rescue operations. South Korea: Pledged $2 million in humanitarian assistance. Spain: Donated €2 million through Red Cross emergency funds. Sri Lanka: Pledged $1 million in aid and prepared medical teams. Bangladesh: Sent rescue teams and emergency supplies via military transport. Cambodia: Provided an initial $100,000 in assistance. Vietnam: Sent 80 rescue personnel and donated $300,000 in aid. Israel: Sent search and rescue teams to assist in Thailand. Australia: Contributed AU$2 million and mobilized emergency response teams. United States: Promised up to $2 million and sent disaster response experts. Indonesia : Provided $1.2 million in emergency aid and sent medical teams. International assistance is crucial in supporting Myanmar’s recovery after this devastating earthquake 7.7Mw .

comment_text: Singapore Bangladesh Society Follow Dear Respected Members, we are just a week away from our Noble event “ SBS Blood Donation”. Appreciate you to register your participation via below link provided. Also, please reach out to your known and invite them to attend the event: ========= DONATE BLOOD, SAVE LIFE In celebration of Singapore National Day, SBS is going to organise Blood Donation drive on 11th August 2024( 9 AM to 5 PM). It is an incredible opportunity to  take part for the Noble cause to save life for those who are in hope. In collaboration with Singapore Red Cross using SBS Red Cross ID R0285, this time, we want to exceed the milestone of total count over 500 blood donors under SBS registry and display our care to the Society. We sincerely request you to be part to this great event, Spread the word and invite your friends, family, and colleagues to participate the program. Together, we can create a healthier community. Details: SBS Blood Donation 2024 Date: 11th August 2024 Time: 9 AM to 5 PM Venue: Bloodbank@HSA, 11 Outram Rd, Singapore 169078 Please register to donate blood, give hope to: https://docs.google.com/.../10KZR8L17jQVP9tsCXMUMs1Y.../edit The Event Powered by, Agrani Exchange House Pte Ltd Singapore Prime Exchange Co. Pte Ltd National Bank Limited PRAN Snacks Time For more inquiries please contact, Md Delwar Hossain (+65 9452 9055), Md. Rakib Hasan (8156 7217). Limited Transport will be provided to pick up Donors from remote area. Curtesy/ Abdullah Al Mamun Hilton/+65 9372 7985 Thank You for joining us on this noble Journey. Sincerely On behalf of Management Council 2024-2025 Subrata Saha General Secretary Singapore Bangladesh Society

A country of truly amazingly friendly people… always smiling and full of joy and happiness, in spite of whatever tragedy or troubles; despite whatever cruel hardships that are thrown their way. It was our first time visiting the intriguing city of Manila, home to my best friends on the race Team Eric and Rona Maggie Wilson Parul Shah , and to be completely honest at that point in time we were just happy to still be part of it all. Didn’t matter what was to come and where we would finish… simply being there was a blessing and an absolute treat; we were ready for whatever spanner that was about to be thrown into our works. We boarded a morning flight from Ho Chi Minh to Manila, and upon reaching the Ninoy Aquino International airport, we were to rush to the GRAB booth to book a Grab car that would be our transport through the city streets (our first task was to head to Quiapo Market to buy aid items for some families in need). Something hilarious actually happened at the airport that unfortunately didn’t make it to the final TV cut. Eric Eruption Tai had tried to take a shortcut by jumping over the security barrier at the drop-off area and he totally made a hash of it! Tripped over, like humpty dumpty over the wall, and all of us were semi-laughing and semi-concerned for his safety. Top drawer gold! (needless to say he'll never be pulling these kinda tricks anymore) We arrive at Quiapo before long and WOW… it was exactly as what I thought it’d be like. Thousands and thousands of people everywhere, a hundred different street stalls (and more) selling a million different items. It was like organized chaos; navigating through the streets and alleyways was a thoroughly unique experience; smells, sights, sounds that are somehow foreign and yet familiar at the very same time. Our list of items to buy were as follows… 8 Whole dried fish 4 salted eggs 12 heads of garlic 1 bottle of fish sauce 1 bottle of cooking oil 1 package of soy  sauce 1 package of vinegar 1 plastic basin 4 mugs ¼ kg of calamansi ¼ kg of salt ¼ kg of sugar 1kg of rice 4 cans of food 2 children’s toys 2 foldable umbrellas 1 first aid kit The sundries were pretty easy to find, but the first aid kit was Tough! Think we ran circles around the entire area before finally finding it! Got all our items, double checked, and then gunned it outta there! We made our way to the Red Cross Pasay chapter in 4th and… well… man it was rough seeing the families at that point. You could clearly see that they had been through a lot… recently or sometime ago, we will never know, but seeing them in the flesh you could see that tragedy, misfortune and other heart wrenching calamities had somehow made its way into their lives. You could see how they were suffering behind the joyous smiles and insane cheering they had for us. And that really cuts to the bone… despite all the odds, they’re still trying their very best to travail past their misery to CHEER for all of us teams, we don’t deserve any of that, not a single ounce at all, and yet there the families all were. Clapping, screaming, shouting at the top of their lungs to urge us on and motivate us… man it was rough watching them, being there; I just wanted to drop everything and just spend some time and see how I can give back and make their lives just that little bit better you know? It was so heart wrenchingly painful and so difficult to have to just rush out of there after saying hello and showing them what we got… being there and interacting with the families puts all our problems/tribulations into perspective really… our troubles are nothing… NOTHING… and so with a heavy heart we leave the Red Cross and made our way to the next location, Partas bus terminal. From there we were to take an overnight bus to Vigan City and once we arrived, a tricycle ride to Ilos Sur Adventure Zone would be on the agenda. At this point I’d like to give a sincere shoutout of thanks to our GrabCar driver… Cesar Campos Valdez, in his Toyota Vios! Insane skills, precision, speed, and control. He singlehandedly got us to all our destinations (from Quiapo market to the Red Cross to the bus terminal) quickly and most importantly, safely. Top drawer driver in every sense of the term! P.S. if you are reading this, which you probably aren't... do you happen to still have my green capped filtered water bottle in your car? I left it in the cup holder while rushing out of your vehicle my mum bought it for me before we went on the race! Don’t get me wrong though; our driver might have been fantastic, but the traffic conditions in Manila (as it is infamous for) weren’t exactly the most cooperative. It was literally bumper to bumper gridlock from the Red Cross to the bus terminal… at one point I thought that we would forever be stuck in this light-less tunnel, fumes of a hundred thousand vehicles swirling in our lungs, cars that stretched on forever and ever, with no end in sight. Somehow an hour or so later (take note that the distance was only what 10km?) we finally made it to the bus terminal and got the shock of our lives… it was going to be a 9-10 hour ride!!! Seriously! I mean in Singapore anything more than 45 minutes would result in unending complaints, and uncensored swearing till the cows come home. Which is why the race is not only an unrivaled adventure of epic proportions, but also a tremendous learning experience; you truly come across things that you’d never done before, do things that you’d never thought you’d ever do, accomplish tasks once thought impossible. Being on this journey and adventure makes you appreciate all the things we take for granted back home; seeing the underprivileged families and children, coming across long journeys that people embark on a daily basis... it makes all our complaints seem so trivial, and they really are. I can still recall being at that slightly grubby bus terminal; we were hungry and had leg money on us but didn’t dare to spend too much for we didn’t know what to expect in the next city. So Mike bought a cup of instant noodles while I got some potato chips at the counter (there were donuts on sale and I was THIS close to buying some when I saw a baby roach crawl across a jelly filled one; NO THANK YOU). Next thing you know though I see our buddies Eric + Rona and Maggie + Parul saunter over from somewhere… bellies full, big smiles on their faces, and pure satisfaction in their veins. “where did you guys go? Jollibee?” I asked… Turns out there was a roadside food stall just across the street from the bus terminal; apparently meals were dirt cheap like SGD$1-$1.50 for a drink and meat + rice! Wanted to try it out but unfortunately our bus had arrived and so up we went… dreading a 9 hour journey on a bus to a city far far away… the longest I’ve ever been on a bus is 1.5 hours… I remember closing my eyes, reclining my chair (it was an air conditioned deluxe bus with lazy-boy style recliners; so thank god we at least travelled in some form of comfort!), and watching a horribly shot C grade movie with surprising A grade actors (Pierce Brosnan and Owen Wilson I think?) The first scene was some important VIP being murdered… and then Pierce Brosnan at the airport or something… and then I closed my eyes… I recall opening them in a hazy and dazed state… and the next thing I heard was… “hey guys we’re here…” NO FREAKIN WAY… I actually slept for 9.5 hours straight on the freaking overnight bus! SCORE! Kind of explains our result on this leg I guess; having proper sleep for once, albeit on a bus no less. We got off the bus in Vigan and our next comedy moment arrived at the tricycles… these vehicles are basically scooters with a cart attached next to it. The proper way to ride one of these things with 2 passengers is to have one person inside the cart with the other seated behind the motorbike rider. (Like Eric and Rona did) Thing is Mike and I didn’t know about such things and weren't exactly in on the local customs and such so we BOTH tried to squeeze into the cart! I was on the floor while Mike (with the smaller butt) got the seat. It was, let's just say slightly claustrophobic and a very tight squeeze… imagine a 30 minute or so journey where you’re literally stuffed into a tin can… that’s what we endured! Ilcos Sur adventure zone… we arrive at the designated location at around 4am; pitch black, low visibility, absolute darkness… something isn’t right, are we at the right place? And then we see it; across the bridge a couple of lights… you see it was so hard to navigate in the conditions that we were in (no street lamps) so the drivers had brought all the teams to the side entrance! We race to the correct location and boom there it was… CLUE BOX! ROADBLOCK: Who’s on target? “Mike you are!” I screamed! “Hit a floating target with a flour bomb while zipping across the Abra river.” The park’s operations only started at 7am so we had 3 hours to kill. Thankfully there was a numbered system (first come first served) and we were #2. I recall bellowing at Eric to HURRY THE F UP COME HERE NOW! Because instead of joining us at the lighted area his rider had driven him all the way down the slope. So Eric managed to rush up and get his clue followed by a number! (We were both pretty close buddies by this point) So what did we all do in those 3 hours? Some teams like Treasuri and Louisa took the opportunity to nap. Yvonne and Chloe gossiped about life and all kinds of relationships with Mike. Parul tried to sleep too but was semi-successful in her endeavours. Maggie and I though… LOL we had our very own little story-telling session good times! Tom and Anita; who were on the 8pm bus (1 hour after all the other teams) soon arrived and were stuck with the #6 and last place starting position on the roadblock. A couple of hours and many stories shared later (don’t you wish you knew what stories we shared? Ask me and maybe I'll tell you) 7am was finally upon us. If you were wondering why many of us cheered Maggie on by screaming her “come on MARGE; you got this MARGARET!” well it was because we finally found out what Maggie was short formed for XD The roadblock challenge itself was HARD… in my personal opinion, really hard. All six teams had sent their ladies to do this challenge… Maggie, Rona, Anita, Chloe, Treasuri and Mike (LOL) were up on the zipline. Just imagine… 5, 6, 7 storeys or more up in the air; a flowing rushing gushing river below you, a tiny minuscule target, unpredictable winds, uncontrollable ziplining speeds… impossible task or what? So kudos to all the ladies for accomplishing this feat… Mike was top drawer but not as crazy good as Treasuri; my goodness what a beast! She flung the flour bomb like a rocket and it hit the target with a stunning explosion of white! we got our clue and for once wasn’t one of the last teams out of a task! It was Treasuri first (2-3 attempts), Maggie on her 4th, Mike on his 5th, Chloe also on her 5th, and then Rona and Anita left to fight it out. ROUTE INFO: “Make your way to Crisologo street by tricycle and search for MA Parel Souvenir shop for your next clue!” It was neck and neck at this point between us and the Malaysian beauty queens for 3rd place… we reach the shop first by the hair of a cow’s chin and chose to do the karaoke detour (I actually wanted to do the sausages one but thank god Mike was adamantly against it!) The karaoke was surprisingly doable and not as utterly challenging as the sausage one. Every team who did the sausages took considerably longer than those who sang; so in this essence we were very lucky. Which is a sweet change from the sheer bad luck we’ve endured over the last few legs; I honestly do not think that we’re bad racers… with the exception of the Bandung leg (where we broke the eggs), and the Malaysia leg (poor choreography) we had actually raced a pretty good race, doing all the things we had to do right… just very tough luck in navigation and more… And so as you’ve seen on TV we miraculously completed the karaoke song (shoutout to the ox for bringing us round the square for practice sessions!) “KWAK KWAK KWAK” in under 2 attempts and made it to the finish mat in… would you believe it… TEAM NUMBER ONE! Totally unexpected, completely and utterly shocked to the bones! YOU MEAN WE ARE NOT LAST? OR SECOND LAST? OMG FREAKIN’ SCENES! Was so ready to head home and guess what we finish this leg in FIRST PLACE. God is great! En route to the finish though you would have seen that there was a U TURN; I had desperately/frantically and totally wanted to use it on Tom & Anita. At that point we didn’t know where any of the teams were and our last knowledge of their locations was the fight to the death at the zipline between Rona and Anita. I wanted to save Eric and Rona; so so badly… but Mike was having none of it. As you can see clearly on the show not only is he a super sensitive easily offended and turned off guy but he also tries to be the heavenly angel of nice guys! So even if it meant saving one of our best friends at the expense of the season’s clear villains (come on; have you seen what Tom is like on the show?! “ANITTAAAAA” "Hope you get LOST" "ARGGHH" "Ya like dropping the target was straightforward" #StillLoveYouTom) Mike would still say NO... and so we didn’t U-turn Tom and Anita, and it was nail-biting excruciation for me to say the very least… After all the hype, excitement and joyful proclamations we reach the holding area, a beautiful but very old church next to a 16thcentury bell tower (Vigan City is stunning I tell you). I remember lighting some candles with Chloe and Yvonne, and then praying, giving thanks for letting us still be on the race and praying for the families we saw yesterday. I stood vigil by the side entrance of the church, hoping to catch a glimpse of Eric and Rona… and thank the lord they made it in 4th, shortly after our other duo of besties Maggie and Parul… phew… Mike you lucky s.o.b I would have never forgiven you if Eric + Rona went home due to something we could have prevented… At that very point of the race, many of us were relieved to see Tom and Anita go… not because we hated them or anything but because they were stiff competitors and were basically like those T-1000 terminators who never gave up and kept on coming back from the dead! However as strong as they are first places and winners on The Amazing Race aren’t due simply to brute strength or brainpower or strategy… it’s a potent combination of 25% strength, 25% brains/strategy, 25% good driver, and 25% LUCK (or fate depending on what you believe)… and I guess it’s just time that we finally had a good hand (when it comes to LUCK) for once! Besides, it’s so GREAT to be able to prove everyone wrong. Every single team who’s been eliminated had earmarked us to be the next team to go in ALL their exit interviews… EVERY TEAM has done so! Brandon and Alphaeus said we would be next… Rach and Vicky said we would be next… Muscle Bros said we would be next… Even Tom and Anita said we would be next… (this one is still up for grabs and we shall see NEXT week if we’re still in the race!!! Nervous and really want to prove them wrong!!!) Our hard luck can actually be a brilliant thing at the end of the day… I mean come on; it means everyone will underestimate us! WIN WIN! Side Notes; (i) Being 1st is great; for the first time ever, even greater! I remember the van bringing us back to our hotel had its radio on… and TAYLOR SWIFT’S SHAKE IT OFF was blasting on the speakers! It was heaven! (SHAKE IT OFF SHA SHA SHA SHAKE IT OFF!) (ii) we’ve made it more than halfway through the competition… no matter what happens from hereon we are grateful and extremely happy to have been here… forget first place, we are thrilled to have been able to survive this leg! (iii) Eric is literally the BIGGEST man in the Philippines… everywhere we went people were clamouring to take photos with the star that is ERIC THE ERUPTION! Seriously though I never knew what a celebrity he was until coming here! You should have seen it! Women, children, uncles, aunties… I remember all the staff (and I mean ALL OF THEM, THE WHOLE STORE CEASED OPERATIONS) of a particular fast food outlet (that sells sandwiches shaped like trains) running out of the store to grab a selfie with him! (iv) Vigan City… a beautiful, stunning, breath-taking, and wondrous phenomenon of a city… it might be 10 hours away by overnight bus but it’s worth every single minute I tell you. It’s like being thrown back in time… the architecture is literally like from nowhere else on earth today… classically preserved and so unbelievably marvellous… I recommend it to anyone and everyone; you MUST visit Vigan City! It’s a UNESCO world heritage site too you know (v) Chicken Inasal… my goodness how has it been hiding from me all this time? The dish I had at the Hotel we were staying at was top quality one of the best chicken dishes I have ever had in my life… and trust me, I’ve had plenty of chicken! Moist, juicy and succulent on the inside; charred, grilled and finger licking mouth-watering lip-smackingly delicious from the outside in… I would totally take the plane ride + bus ride from Singapore to Vigan JUST for that very same bite again! Believe it or not Eric actually had thrice the number of plates I had, and I'm pretty sure there were at least 3 plates of Chicken Inasal on my table at the end of the meal XD Other quality local Filipina dishes we had included Garlic fried rice, Vigan sausages (LOL! note: NOT the ones made by the other teams), corned beef, beef caldereta, and more! The local iced tea was divine! Really miss Vigan city so so much... really feel like taking the next plane out of here just to go back there! Bring my wife for a walk down the cobbled streets, past ponies and buffaloes and more... eating delicious food and meeting friendly local folk ahhh... And so there you have it… a magnificent leg in a splendid country! Home ground up next as we fly to Uniquely Singapore; thing is we can’t expect any sure things or guarantees… I mean come on… at this point of the race, NO TEAM HAS WON IN THEIR OWN COUNTRY YET! Teams from Malaysia won both Indonesia legs so far, while Team Indonesia won Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam legs… so anything can happen… we could even be GOING HOME, while AT HOME!!! Cross fingers it won’t happen; from the bottom of our hearts thank you so much for the support and please wish us the best of luck! Remember to keep your televisions locked to AXN Asia as we embark on leg 7 of The Amazing Race Asia #TARAJKMIKE #AXNTARA

A country of truly amazingly friendly people… always smiling and full of joy and happiness, in spite of whatever tragedy or troubles; despite whatever cruel hardships that are thrown their way. It was our first time visiting the intriguing city of Manila, home to my best friends on the race Team Eric and Rona Maggie Wilson Parul Shah , and to be completely honest at that point in time we were just happy to still be part of it all. Didn’t matter what was to come and where we would finish… simply being there was a blessing and an absolute treat; we were ready for whatever spanner that was about to be thrown into our works. We boarded a morning flight from Ho Chi Minh to Manila, and upon reaching the Ninoy Aquino International airport, we were to rush to the GRAB booth to book a Grab car that would be our transport through the city streets (our first task was to head to Quiapo Market to buy aid items for some families in need). Something hilarious actually happened at the airport that unfortunately didn’t make it to the final TV cut. Eric Eruption Tai had tried to take a shortcut by jumping over the security barrier at the drop-off area and he totally made a hash of it! Tripped over, like humpty dumpty over the wall, and all of us were semi-laughing and semi-concerned for his safety. Top drawer gold! (needless to say he'll never be pulling these kinda tricks anymore) We arrive at Quiapo before long and WOW… it was exactly as what I thought it’d be like. Thousands and thousands of people everywhere, a hundred different street stalls (and more) selling a million different items. It was like organized chaos; navigating through the streets and alleyways was a thoroughly unique experience; smells, sights, sounds that are somehow foreign and yet familiar at the very same time. Our list of items to buy were as follows… 8 Whole dried fish 4 salted eggs 12 heads of garlic 1 bottle of fish sauce 1 bottle of cooking oil 1 package of soy  sauce 1 package of vinegar 1 plastic basin 4 mugs ¼ kg of calamansi ¼ kg of salt ¼ kg of sugar 1kg of rice 4 cans of food 2 children’s toys 2 foldable umbrellas 1 first aid kit The sundries were pretty easy to find, but the first aid kit was Tough! Think we ran circles around the entire area before finally finding it! Got all our items, double checked, and then gunned it outta there! We made our way to the Red Cross Pasay chapter in 4th and… well… man it was rough seeing the families at that point. You could clearly see that they had been through a lot… recently or sometime ago, we will never know, but seeing them in the flesh you could see that tragedy, misfortune and other heart wrenching calamities had somehow made its way into their lives. You could see how they were suffering behind the joyous smiles and insane cheering they had for us. And that really cuts to the bone… despite all the odds, they’re still trying their very best to travail past their misery to CHEER for all of us teams, we don’t deserve any of that, not a single ounce at all, and yet there the families all were. Clapping, screaming, shouting at the top of their lungs to urge us on and motivate us… man it was rough watching them, being there; I just wanted to drop everything and just spend some time and see how I can give back and make their lives just that little bit better you know? It was so heart wrenchingly painful and so difficult to have to just rush out of there after saying hello and showing them what we got… being there and interacting with the families puts all our problems/tribulations into perspective really… our troubles are nothing… NOTHING… and so with a heavy heart we leave the Red Cross and made our way to the next location, Partas bus terminal. From there we were to take an overnight bus to Vigan City and once we arrived, a tricycle ride to Ilos Sur Adventure Zone would be on the agenda. At this point I’d like to give a sincere shoutout of thanks to our GrabCar driver… Cesar Campos Valdez, in his Toyota Vios! Insane skills, precision, speed, and control. He singlehandedly got us to all our destinations (from Quiapo market to the Red Cross to the bus terminal) quickly and most importantly, safely. Top drawer driver in every sense of the term! P.S. if you are reading this, which you probably aren't... do you happen to still have my green capped filtered water bottle in your car? I left it in the cup holder while rushing out of your vehicle my mum bought it for me before we went on the race! Don’t get me wrong though; our driver might have been fantastic, but the traffic conditions in Manila (as it is infamous for) weren’t exactly the most cooperative. It was literally bumper to bumper gridlock from the Red Cross to the bus terminal… at one point I thought that we would forever be stuck in this light-less tunnel, fumes of a hundred thousand vehicles swirling in our lungs, cars that stretched on forever and ever, with no end in sight. Somehow an hour or so later (take note that the distance was only what 10km?) we finally made it to the bus terminal and got the shock of our lives… it was going to be a 9-10 hour ride!!! Seriously! I mean in Singapore anything more than 45 minutes would result in unending complaints, and uncensored swearing till the cows come home. Which is why the race is not only an unrivaled adventure of epic proportions, but also a tremendous learning experience; you truly come across things that you’d never done before, do things that you’d never thought you’d ever do, accomplish tasks once thought impossible. Being on this journey and adventure makes you appreciate all the things we take for granted back home; seeing the underprivileged families and children, coming across long journeys that people embark on a daily basis... it makes all our complaints seem so trivial, and they really are. So Mike bought a cup of instant noodles while I got some potato chips at the counter (there were donuts on sale and I was THIS close to buying some when I saw a baby roach crawl across a jelly filled one; NO THANK YOU). I was on the floor while Mike (with the smaller butt) got the seat. Maggie and I though… LOL we had our very own little story-telling session good times! Tom and Anita; who were on the 8pm bus (1 hour after all the other teams) soon arrived and were stuck with the #6 and last place starting position on the roadblock. comment_text: Singapore Red Cross Follow This #InternationalWomensDay, we cast the spotlight on just a few of the women whose work at the Singapore Red Cross makes an impact in unique and powerful ways. Sarinah is part of a vital team that works to match volunteers with programme needs and ensure that their volunteering journey is a fulfilling one. Her prior experience in the education sector shaped her understanding of vulnerable communities among us and showed her just how much of an impact she could make by offering her time and support. What she witnessed inspired her to pursue a career in humanitarian service. People remain at the heart of what she does, as she puts it — "We work to create an environment where volunteers feel genuinely valued. Through regular recognition, training opportunities, and fostering a strong sense of community, they'd know that their contributions matter, and be encouraged to continue." #sgredcross #PassionPeople #VolunteerWithSRC

comment_text: Ong Ye Kung Follow Today is World Blood Donor Day, a time to express our gratitude to blood donors for their gift of life, mostly to strangers that they do not even know. In Singapore, over 77,000 people stepped forward to donate blood last year. 22% were first-time donors. In total, we collected almost 123,000 units of blood. However, by 2030, the projected annual demand will reach 160,000 units. Partly because of demographics, the number of youth donors has been declining over time. I know our young today are far more socially conscious than previous generations, so I hope blood donation can feature as one of their social causes. From time to time, I will learn that a colleague or a family member is donating blood. Always makes my day. I hope to see more people joining our community of lifesavers. I wish everybody a very happy World Blood Donation Day. +2

comment_text: Sim Ann 沈颖 Follow The Blood Donation Drive at Bukit Timah CC is in full swing! Please help share and tag your friends and family members. Do you know Fact 1: For many patients, blood donors are their lifeline. One unit of blood can save three lives! Every hour of the day, 15 units of blood are used in Singapore. Fact 2: Blood is needed to save lives in times of emergencies and to sustain the lives of those with medical conditions, like leukemia, thalassaemia and bleeding disorders, as well as patients who are undergoing major surgeries. Donors have been coming forward since 10am but we need more donors! Do drop by and help save a life today. The blood donation drive will be open till 4pm today. The event details are as follows: Date: 22 June 2019, Saturday. Time: 10am to 4pm. Venue: Bukit Timah Community Centre, Level 1 Multi-Purpose Hall. 20 Toh Yi Drive, S596569. Please be reminded to bring along the following items: ·       NRIC/Driver’s license/Work pass/ Donor card ·       Donors Aged 16-17, kindly bring the signed parental consent form available at hsa.gov.sg/parent_consent If you have any questions, you can call Singapore Red Cross at 6220 0183 or visit giveblood.sg Do bring your family and friends down to support this meaningful cause! For blood donor criteria, kindly visit bit.ly/donorcriteria for more details. Also, visit https://facebook.com/Bukit.Timah.CC.YEC/ or @yec_bukittimahcc on instagram for updates on the activities planned. +4

comment_text: Rotary Club of Garden City is with Matthew Yong at Wak Hassan Drive · Follow Singapore *Important Announcement* At our club’s Board of Directors meeting on August 28, 2025, we decided to confer honorary membership on Charter Member and Past President Chong Choo Chai, without a term limit. Henceforth, he shall be known as Honorary Member (HM) Chong Choo Chai. HM Chong Choo Chai is our third club president. He served as the Founding Chairman of the Foundation of Rotary Clubs (Singapore) Limited for the first nine years of its existence. He organized our club’s annual blood donation drive for around 20 years and has supported the annual Gift of Sight project in Nepal since its inception, making a yearly donation of US$1,000 for over 20 years. His contributions have exceeded the Major Donor Level 2 threshold. He has also graciously donated his club per capita dues to our club for our community service projects. Our club members and spouses have visited HM Chong Choo Chai to offer our congratulations to him on 5th October 2025. *重要公告* 本社于2025年8月28日召开董事会，决定授予创始会员兼前任社长张楚材荣誉会员资格，且无任期限制。自此，他将被称为“荣誉会员张楚材”。 荣誉会员张楚材是本社的第三任会长。他曾担任新加坡扶轮社基金会成立后九年的创始主席。他组织本社的年度献血活动近20年，并自尼泊尔“光明之礼”眼疾项目成立以来一直提供支持，这20多年来每年捐款1000美元。他的捐款已超过二级主要捐赠者的门槛。 他也慷慨地将自己缴纳的会费捐赠给我社，用于我们的社区服务项目。 我们新加坡狮城扶轮社的社友们和宝眷已于 2025 年 10 月 5 日星期天下午拜访了HM张楚材并向他和夫人表示祝贺。 Veronica Yip Michael Yee Matthew Yong HK Tung Richard Cheung Florence Chong #rotaryinternational #uniteforgood2025 +6

comment_text: Tzu-Chi Foundation SG 慈济基金会 Follow 20年前的6月14日，SARS疫情肆虐，新加坡血库存量因而锐减，慈济响应红十字会号召，于当时的牛车水会所举办首次捐血。 20年来，慈济与红十字会合作数百次捐血活动，累计超过3万2千袋血。 今年6月17日，是世界献血者日，慈济再次获颁流动捐血金奖，是该奖项的最高级别。这是慈济自2008年来，每年所获得的肯定。 在此，我们感恩志工20年来，在街头宣导、专车接送、捐血关怀和陪伴接待的无私付出，也感恩这些年来曾经响应捐血活动的您。 Over the past 20 years, Tzu Chi has collaborated with the Red Cross in hundreds of blood donation drives, accumulating over 32,000 packets of blood. In conjunction with World Blood Donor Day, which falls on 14 June each year, Tzu Chi was again awarded the Gold Award for Mobile Blood Donation, the highest level of the award, on 17 June 2023. This is a recognition that Tzu Chi has been receiving every year since 2008. We would like to thank our volunteers for their selfless and relentless efforts in advocating the blood donation drive on the street, providing shuttle bus services, and accompanying blood donors during the campaigns for the past 2 decades. Last but not least, a big thank you to those who have donated blood over the years.

comment_text: 新加坡佛教居士林 The Singapore Buddhist Lodge Follow 【居士林向新加坡红十字会捐助20万元】 本林向新加坡红十字会捐助20万元，以帮助其在加沙地区展开的人道救援工作。 2023年12月13日，本林林长陈立发居士、首席佛学导师延续法师、财政叶云涌居士前往新加坡红十字会，捐助20万元人道援助善款，救助加沙难民。 红十字会秘书长 Benjamin J. William 和国际事务主任 Rebekah Lim 接待了陈林长一行，并介绍了目前国际救援物资遇到的各种问题。秘书长 Benjamin J. William 对居士林的捐助表示真诚感谢。 本林一向秉持佛教的慈悲思想，不分种族不分宗教救护众生，以实际行动援助在战争中受苦的难民与家庭，祈愿双方早日停火，恢复和平，天下众生皆能平安，脱离苦难。 【SBL Donated SGD200K  To Singapore Red Cross Society】 SBL donated SGD 200,000  to the Singapore Red Cross to aid in its humanitarian relief efforts in the Gaza Strip. On 13 December 2023, SBL President Mr Tan Lee Huak, SBL Head of Dharma Guiding Teacher Venerable Yanxu and Honorary Treasurer Mr Yeap Yuen Yon visited the Singapore Red Cross to contribute SGD 200,000 in humanitarian aid funds to assist Gaza refugees. Secretary-General/CEO Mr Benjamin J. William and Head, Global Engagement Ms Rebekah Lim welcomed President Mr Tan Lee Huak and his delegates, providing insights into the various challenges faced by international relief efforts. Mr Benjamin expressed sincere gratitude for the donation from The Singapore Buddhist Lodge. SBL has always upheld to the compassionate principles of Buddhism, extending assistance to all beings regardless of race or religion, and taking practical actions to help refugees and families suffering from war. Sincerely hope for an early ceasefire, the restoration of peace, and for all beings to live in harmony, free from suffering.

comment_text_translated: Aceh Opinion Follow SINGAPORE - Indonesian DIASPORA who live in Singapore are complaining about the policy of sending aid to Sumatran disaster victims. One member of the diaspora named Fika said that aid sent from outside Indonesia would be taxed by the Indonesian government. He shared this via uploads on his Instagram account @ffawzia07. "If there are donations from the diaspora and the Sumatran flood disaster has not been declared a national disaster, then the aid will be subject to tax," he wrote in the upload, quoted on Thursday, December 11 2025. He explained that aid from the diaspora sent to Sumatra would also be considered imported goods. According to him, this policy makes no sense considering the impact of the Sumatran floods which caused almost a thousand people to die. Data from the National Disaster Management Agency recorded that as of Wednesday, December 10, the number of victims of the Sumatran floods reached 969 people. Fika said that the imposition of taxes on sending aid to Sumatran flood victims had limited the initiative of the diaspora. He said that currently the diaspora can only help by donating money to the Sumatran flood victims. Tempo contacted the Indonesian Embassy to Singapore. The Indonesian Ambassador to Singapore, Suryo Pratomo, requested that this information be asked of Customs and Excise. However, Suryo acknowledged receiving questions from the diaspora regarding sending aid to Sumatran flood victims. The Indonesian Embassy to Singapore, he said, could not facilitate the delivery of aid to Sumatra. According to him, the embassy does not have the authority to encourage the central government to declare national disaster status for the Sumatran floods so that aid from abroad can come in. He stated that he could only provide an alternative for the diaspora who wanted to send aid. "Send money donations, you can send them to the Indonesian Red Cross," said Suryo when contacted on Thursday, December 11 2025. Suryo also directed the diaspora who want to help Sumatran flood victims to contact agencies that are open to accepting aid. He said his agency did not know the procedures for sending aid from abroad. "Because until now there has been no assistance from outside Indonesia for the flash flood disaster," he said. Director of Communications and Service User Guidance at the Directorate General of Customs, Nirwala Dwi Heryanto, was unable to provide an explanation. He said he had to coordinate with related officials. "I confirmed this with the offices in charge," he said when confirmed regarding the imposition of tax on diaspora aid, Thursday, December 11 2025. The central government previously stated that it had not opened space for other countries to distribute aid funds for handling the Sumatran disaster. Minister of State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi claims that the government is still able to overcome all disaster problems in Aceh, North Sumatra and West Sumatra. "We feel that the government is still capable of dealing with all the problems we are facing," said Prasetyo at Halim Perdanakusuma Air Base, Jakarta, Wednesday, December 3 2025. According to Prasetyo, many countries are paying attention to this disaster. There are also other countries that want to provide assistance. However, this Gerindra politician claims that the government is still able to overcome various problems. The government has sufficient food and fuel stocks. "This includes having to use methods that may not be normal," said Prasetyo. "We are trying to carry out air dropping because it adapts to the disaster conditions faced in the field." #PrayForAceh #Disaster #Flood #National #International #Malaysia #Turkey #Russia #Australia #America #Kadana #Japan #SaudiArabia #France #Libya #GAM #Dermak #Netherlands #TotalPolitik #Prabowo #Sumatra #Aceh #Mualem #UN #Singapore

comment_text: Nik Nor Hidayah Follow Waahh.. Siti 'Aisyah Rozalli · Follow #MadrasahKanser : Macam mana nak jadi donor Stem Cell? Maha Suci Allah. Ramai yang bertanya pada saya cara jadi donor stem cell. Baiknya hati anda semua. Semoga dengan terdetik dan terlintas je niat tu, Allah terus catat sebagai pahala besar. Jom kita cerita sikit. Untuk jadi donor stem cell, ianya perlu melalui Malaysian Stem Cell Registry (MSCR). Mereka yang akan match kan penerima dan penderma. Stem cell ni akan ikut bangsa tau. Bukan sebab racist ya Tapi, sebab DNA matching tu. Maksudnya, melayu hanya boleh terima stem cell dari melayu. Cina dari cina. India dari india. Bila nak cari donor, ada 2 options. Cari dalam Malaysia dan luar negara. Melayu agak susah nak cari. Sebab registry kita tak banyak. Ada dari Malaysia, Thailand, Singapura. Tu pun registry number kecil. So, apa yang akan berlaku kalau kita nak jadi donor stem cell? Step 1: DAFTAR DI REGISTRY. Yang ni, simple je. Kena bagi sample air liur untuk mereka buat HLA (Human Leukocyte Antigen) Matching. Ni first step. HLA kena matching dulu. 50% ke atas tak silap saya. Step ni, buat dari rumah je pun boleh. - Register di link MSCR - MSCR hantar kit sample ke rumah kita - Kita bagi pos semula sample kita pada MSCR (sampul surat semua dah siap ada, fee poslaju pun MSCR dah bayarkan). Ni link daftar: https://docs.google.com/.../1FAIpQLSeggOwPdvHZ2t.../viewform Step 2: KALAU ADA YANG MATCH. Kita akan perlu ke hospital terdekat (MSCR akan bagitahu hospital mana yang terdekat dan boleh buat 2nd test ni). Diorang akan ambil darah, untuk test antibodi. Samada antibodi penerima ada tak melawan antibodi kita. Kalau OK, sesuai. Diteruskan ke step 3. Kalau tak OK, tamat di sini. Maybe tunggu kalau ada penderma lain pula yang matching. Step 3: STEM CELL HARVEST Yang ni, dah sampai step untuk penderma mula derma stem cell. 1. Penderma akan disuntik Granulocyte Colony-Stimulating Factor (G-CSF), untuk rangsang penghasilan darah putih untuk proses collection stem cell. Yang ni selama 4 hari berturut. Cucuknya sekejap je. Lepas cucuk, balik. Tapi, G-CSF ni akan buat badan rasa sengal-sengal sikit. Sebab dia rangsang sum-sum. Saya kena cucuk benda ni kerap masa tempoh rawatan hari tu. Sengal kejap je. Lepas tu, lupa dah 2. Lepas 4 hari, hari kelima aktiviti harvest stem cell akan bermula. Untuk ini, penderma akan dicucuk femoral line. Jarum kat kawasan atas paha. Proses harvest ni 4 jam. Macam dialisis. Dia ambil darah kita, masuk dalam machine, ambil stem cell, masuk balik darah baki dalam badan kita. 3. Siap harvest, rehat. Esoknya boleh balik. Dr kata, donor takde risiko apa-apa. Risiko kena cuti masa proses harvest je. Dan sakit nak kena cucuk tu Donor akan dikira sebagai pemegang certificate organ donor kebangsaan. Semua rawatan kat hospital kerajaan 100% free. Jadi, untuk yang berminat nak masuk dalam registry, dan berpotensi jadi asbab penyelamat nyawa, boleh register kat link atas tu. Oh, dan. Nanti, penerima stem cell tu, seluruh produk sum-sum tulang dia: sel darah merah, sel darah putih, platelet dan yang berkait adalah dari DNA penderma. Anda akan jadi sebahagian besar kehidupan penerima stem cell. Setiap oksigen yang dibawa oleh sel darah merah dan sampai ke segenap organ penerima… Setiap sel darah putih yang melawan segala jenis jangkitan… Setiap luka yang disembuhkan oleh platelet… Semua tu dari stem cell yang anda dermakan. Semoga segala kebaikan yang dibuat oleh penerima stem cell anda tu, ada pahala berkait juga dengan anda Aminn Write a comment…
comment_text_translated: Nik Nor Hidayah Follow Waahh.. Siti 'Aisyah Rozalli · Follow #MadrasahKanser : How to become a stem cell donor? Glory be to God. Many people ask me how to become a stem cell donor. Good luck to you all. I hope that by tickling and crossing that intention, God will continue to record it as a great reward. Let's talk a little. To become a stem cell donor, it is necessary to go through the Malaysian Stem Cell Registry (MSCR). Those who will match the recipient and the donor. This stem cell will follow the race. Not because of racism, but because of the DNA matching. Meaning, Malays can only receive stem cells from Malays. Chinese from china. Indian from India. When looking for a donor, there are 2 options. Search in Malaysia and abroad. Malay is a bit hard to find. Because our registry is not much. There are from Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore. Even the registry number is small. So, what will happen if we want to be a stem cell donor? Step 1: REGISTER AT THE REGISTRY. This one is simple. Have to give a saliva sample for them to do HLA (Human Leukocyte Antigen) Matching. This is the first step. HLA must be matched first. 50% and above, I'm not mistaken. This step, you can do it from home. - Register at the MSCR link - MSCR will send the sample kit to our house - We will repost our sample to MSCR (the envelopes are all ready, MSCR has already paid the postage fee). This is the registration link: https://docs.google.com/.../1FAIpQLSeggOwPdvHZ2t.../viewform Step 2: IF THERE IS A MATCH. We will need to go to the nearest hospital (MSCR will tell us which hospital is the closest and we can do this 2nd test). People will take blood, for an antibody test. Whether the recipient's antibodies are not against our antibodies. If OK, appropriate. Continued to step 3. If not OK, end here. Maybe wait if there are other matching donors. Step 3: STEM CELL HARVEST This is the step for donors to start donating stem cells. 1. The donor will be injected with Granulocyte Colony-Stimulating Factor (G-CSF), to stimulate the production of white blood for the stem cell collection process. This one for 4 days in a row. The poke is for a moment. Leave the poke, come back. But, this G-CSF will make the body feel a little queasy. Because he stimulates the marrow. I had to poke this thing often during the treatment period that day. Just a moment's pain. After that, I forgot 2. After 4 days, the fifth day of the stem cell harvest activity will begin. For this, the donor will be punctured in the femoral line. Needles in the thigh area. The harvest process is 4 hours. Like dialysis. He takes our blood, enters the machine, takes stem cells, returns the remaining blood in our body. 3. Complete harvest, rest. You can come back tomorrow. Dr said, the donor has no risk whatsoever. The risk of being off during the harvest process. And it hurts to be pricked. The donor will be counted as a national organ donor certificate holder. All treatment at the government hospital is 100% free. So, for those who are interested in entering the registry, and potentially becoming a life-saver, you can register at the link above. Oh, and. Later, the recipient of the stem cell, all his bone marrow products: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and related are from the donor's DNA. You will be a big part of the stem cell recipient's life. Every oxygen that is carried by red blood cells and reaches all the recipient's organs... Every white blood cell that fights all kinds of infections... Every wound that is healed by platelets... All of that is from the stem cells that you donate. May all the good deeds done by your stem cell recipient, there is a reward related to you as well Aminn Write a comment...
